name: Aba Nigeria Temple
description: The Aba Nigeria Temple is prominently located on the outskirts of Aba, north of the Ogbor River. A concrete bridge built by the Church connects the temple complex, which features a stake center and an administration office with guest accommodations. This temple was the first in Nigeria, the second in West Africa, and the third on the African continent, following the Johannesburg South Africa Temple in 1985 and the Accra Ghana Temple in 2004. President Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated the temple during a global tour that included stops in various cities, with his first sighting of the temple from a helicopter. It is the 121st temple dedicated, featuring an exterior of Namibian pearl granite and a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Abidjan Ivory Coast Temple
description: The Abidjan Ivory Coast Temple is situated in the Cocody suburb of Abidjan, directly behind the Cocody Cote d'Ivoire Stake center. The temple features a steeple topped with a palladium-leafed statue of the angel Moroni, symbolizing the restoration of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Announced by President Thomas S. Monson on April 5, 2015, it is the first temple in the Ivory Coast and the seventh in Africa. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on November 8, 2018, led by Elder Neil L. Andersen. The temple was dedicated on May 25, 2025, and is designed with mid-century modern influences, incorporating local cultural motifs and a calming color palette.

name: Abuja Nigeria Temple
description: The Abuja Nigeria Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the sixth in Nigeria, following the dedication of the Aba Nigeria Temple in 2005. Other planned temples in Nigeria include the Benin City, Calabar, Eket, and Lagos Nigeria Temples. Nigeria is home to over 230,000 Latter-day Saints across approximately 810 congregations, with Abuja serving as the capital.

name: Accra Ghana Temple
address: 57 Independence Ave North Ridge P.M.B. CT 209 Cantonments
description: The Accra Ghana Temple is the first temple established in West Africa and the second in Africa, following the Johannesburg South Africa Temple, which was completed in 1985. In 2002, the first Missionary Training Center in Africa opened in Tema, near Accra. The tradition of a youth cultural celebration prior to a temple dedication began with the Accra Ghana Temple, initiated by President Gordon B. Hinckley, and continued until the Cedar City Utah Temple dedication in 2017. President Hinckley announced the temple's construction during an outdoor gathering in Accra on February 16, 1998, after encouraging members to support new converts. Groundbreaking took place on November 16, 2001, with Elder Russell M. Nelson and the Ghanaian Vice President participating in the ceremony.

name: Adelaide Australia Temple
description: The Adelaide Australia Temple is situated a few miles northeast of Adelaide's city center in the suburb of Marden, adjacent to a college campus on Lower Portrush Road. This granite structure features a gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni and is surrounded by gardens and gathering plazas on all sides. It was the second temple established in Australia, following the Sydney Australia Temple, which was dedicated in 1984. The groundbreaking for the Adelaide Australia Temple took place on the same day as ceremonies for the Louisville Kentucky Temple and Veracruz Mexico Temple, with Elder Vaughn J. Featherstone presiding. President Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated the temple on June 15, 2000, during a trip where he dedicated four temples across Asia and the Pacific.

name: Alabang Philippines Temple
address: Filinvest Avenue and Corporate Avenue Alabang
description: The Alabang Philippines Temple will hold an open house starting with a media day on November 17, 2025, followed by tours for invited guests. The public can visit from November 21 to December 13, 2025, excluding Sundays. Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles will dedicate the temple on January 18, 2026, with the session broadcast to local congregations. This temple, located in Alabang, Muntinlupa City, will be the fourth in the Philippines and is designed as a two-story granite building with a tapering spire. It aims to serve the nearly 750,000 Latter-day Saints in the country, providing a closer option for those in southern Metro Manila.

name: Albuquerque New Mexico Temple
description: The Albuquerque New Mexico Temple is a striking presence in the arid landscape of northeastern Albuquerque, located in the North Albuquerque Acres neighborhood. Its grounds feature lush greenery and a variety of native plants, complemented by a stunning water feature at the entrance. The temple's exterior is adorned with celestial symbols, including moons, stars, and suns, arranged in their astronomical order. Dedicated on March 5, 2000, by President Gordon B. Hinckley, the temple serves as a sanctuary for peace and contemplation. It was the first temple established in New Mexico, following missionary efforts that began in the 1860s among the Zuni Indians.

name: Anchorage Alaska Temple
description: The Anchorage Alaska Temple will undergo reconstruction, as announced by the First Presidency on January 23, 2023. The existing 11,930-square-foot temple will remain operational during the construction of a new 30,000-square-foot facility, expected to begin in early 2024 and finish by summer 2026. After the new temple is completed, the old building will be decommissioned, and a new meetinghouse will be constructed. This temple, the first built in Alaska, features a stunning chandelier and unique granite etchings of the North Star and Big Dipper. The Anchorage Alaska Temple has previously undergone expansion and renovations, enhancing its facilities significantly since its dedication.

name: Antananarivo Madagascar Temple
address: Lot 208 A Fokontany Andranoro Commune Ambohibao Antehiroka
description: The Antananarivo Madagascar Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony on March 15, 2025, presided over by Elder Denelson Silva, First Counselor in the Africa South Area Presidency. It will be constructed on a 9.8-acre site on Lalana Général Andrimahazo, where an existing meetinghouse is located in Fokontany Andranoro, Commune Ambohibao, Antehiroka, Antananarivo. The temple will be a single-story building of approximately 10,000 square feet, featuring patron housing and arrival facilities. This temple will be the first in Madagascar, where nearly 13,000 Church members are part of over 40 congregations. The announcement for its construction was made by President Russell M. Nelson during the October 2021 General Conference.

name: Antofagasta Chile Temple
description: The Antofagasta Chile Temple is the third temple established in Chile, following the Santiago Chile Temple in 1983 and the Concepción Chile Temple in 2018. It was announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 7, 2019, during the Sunday Afternoon Session of General Conference. Prior to this temple, members in Antofagasta traveled 830 miles to the Santiago temple for ordinances. The temple's location was confirmed on October 2, 2020, on a 2.2-acre site on Avenida de Las Palmeras, featuring a two-story, 23,000-square-foot design in Spanish Colonial style. The temple will serve the local stakes and is set to hold a public open house from May 14 to May 24, 2025, with dedication by Elder Gary E. Stevenson on June 15, 2025.

name: Apia Samoa Temple
description: The Apia Samoa Temple is located on the western outskirts of Apia in Pesega, next to the Church College of Western Samoa. The temple grounds are open to the public and feature lush greenery and a prominent water feature. It was the first temple constructed in Samoa and the third in Polynesia, following the Laie Hawaii Temple and the Hamilton New Zealand Temple. The temple was destroyed by fire in July 2003 during renovations and was subsequently rebuilt, with its rededication occurring on September 4, 2005. The new structure retains the original design while offering additional space and improved materials.

name: Arequipa Peru Temple
address: Calle Cusco 380 Carmen Alto Distrito De Cayma
description: The Arequipa Peru Temple is situated three miles north of Arequipa's city center, near the village of Carmen Alto, on a bluff overlooking the Chili River. This temple is the third in Peru, following the Lima Peru Temple and the Trujillo Peru Temple. Announced by President Thomas S. Monson on October 6, 2012, the temple's groundbreaking took place on March 4, 2017, led by Elder Carlos A. Godoy. The temple was dedicated on December 15, 2019, by Elder Ulisses Soares, after a public open house that attracted over 80,000 visitors. The temple features a blend of local flora in its landscaping and incorporates the Flor de Texao Arequipa in its design elements.

name: Asunción Paraguay Temple
description: The Asunción Paraguay Temple is situated in the Mariscal López neighborhood of Asunción, at the intersection of Avenida España and Avenida Brasilia. The temple complex includes a meetinghouse, known locally as Capilla Moroni, which was built as an extension of a former residential mansion. This temple, dedicated in 2002 by President Gordon B. Hinckley, was the first in Paraguay and marked a significant milestone, as it ensured that every Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking nation in South America had an operating temple. The temple underwent a major renovation from October 29, 2017, to November 3, 2019, when it was rededicated. The exterior features light gray Asa Branca Brazilian granite and includes a single spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Atlanta Georgia Temple
description: The Atlanta Georgia Temple is situated on a hillside in Sandy Springs, just west of the Turner McDonald Parkway in the northern part of the Atlanta metro area. Its striking stained glass wall illuminates the temple at night, complemented by a single spire. This temple was the first in the Southeastern United States and was dedicated by President Gordon B. Hinckley on June 1, 1983. The temple underwent a significant renovation from July 1, 2009, to 2011, enhancing its interior and exterior features. The original angel Moroni statue was replaced, and elements from the original construction were incorporated into the remodeled design.

name: Auckland New Zealand Temple
description: The Auckland New Zealand Temple is a prominent structure located along the Auckland Southern Motorway, situated between a stake center and the New Zealand Missionary Training Center. This temple, announced on October 7, 2018, by President Russell M. Nelson, is the second temple in New Zealand, following the Hamilton New Zealand Temple. Groundbreaking for the temple took place on June 13, 2020, amidst the global COVID-19 pandemic, with Elder Ian S. Arden highlighting its significance as a beacon of hope. The temple is designed as a two-story building with a granite exterior and is set to be dedicated on April 13, 2025. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has a rich history in Auckland, dating back to the arrival of missionaries in 1854, and continues to serve a diverse membership through various community initiatives.

name: Austin Texas Temple
description: The Austin Texas Temple will be constructed following its groundbreaking ceremony led by Elder Michael A. Dunn on August 17, 2024. This temple will span approximately 30,000 square feet and is situated on a 10.6-acre site next to an existing meetinghouse at 1801 East Park Street in Cedar Park. The official exterior rendering was made public on September 5, 2023. Plans for the temple were announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the April 2022 General Conference, marking it as the seventh temple in Texas, which has over 362,000 Latter-day Saints. Missionary efforts in Texas began in 1843, and the state capital is Austin.

name: Bacolod Philippines Temple
description: The Bacolod Philippines Temple will be built on a 12.3-acre site at the intersection of Bacolod Airport Access Road and Buri Road. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on December 11, 2021, led by Elder Taniela B. Wakolo, president of the Philippines Area, alongside his counselors and local dignitaries. This single-story temple will cover approximately 26,700 square feet, with an additional 18,000-square-foot ancillary building for patron housing, an arrival center, and a distribution center. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 5, 2019, this temple is the seventh in the Philippines and the second in the Visayas region, following the Cebu City Philippines Temple. Currently, members from Negros Island travel to Cebu for temple ordinances, making this new temple a significant addition for the local Church community.

name: Bahía Blanca Argentina Temple
address: 3200 Avenida Alberto Pedro Cabrera Aldea Romana
description: The Bahía Blanca Argentina Temple is set to hold a public open house from October 16 to November 1, 2025, excluding Sundays. Prior to this, a media day will occur on October 14, followed by tours for invited guests. Elder Ulisses Soares from the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles will dedicate the temple on November 23, 2025, with the session broadcast to local congregations. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on April 9, 2022, presided over by Elder Joaquin E. Costa of the Quorum of the Seventy. This temple, located on an 8.14-acre site in the Aldea Romana neighborhood, will be approximately 19,000 square feet and will include a 25,000-square-foot ancillary building for patron housing and a distribution center.

name: Bakersfield California Temple
description: The Bakersfield California Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The temple's location is a 13.07-acre site northwest of Stockdale Highway and Jewetta Avenue in Bakersfield, announced on July 25, 2023. An exterior rendering was released on January 8, 2024, showcasing a single-story design of approximately 30,000 square feet, which will include a distribution center and meetinghouse. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the April 2023 General Conference, marking it as the 12th temple for California. Bakersfield, home to nearly 400,000 residents, is situated about 100 miles northwest of Los Angeles.

name: Bangkok Thailand Temple
description: The Bangkok Thailand Temple showcases design elements inspired by traditional Thai architecture, featuring diamond shapes, lotus motifs, and herringbone patterns. Its distinctive silhouette enhances the Bangkok skyline, complemented by a Christus statue in the courtyard connecting to the annex building, which includes the Thailand MTC, meetinghouses, and mission offices. This temple, the first in mainland Southeast Asia, was announced by President Thomas S. Monson during the 185th Annual General Conference and serves Latter-day Saints across the region. Groundbreaking took place on January 26, 2019, and the temple was dedicated on October 22, 2023, after a public open house from September 1 to 16. The temple complex also features an annex for Church offices and a FamilySearch center for genealogical research.

name: Barcelona Spain Temple
address: Avinguda de la Vía Augusta y Avinguda de la Clota
description: The Barcelona Spain Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date confirmed yet. The official exterior rendering was unveiled on November 20, 2023. The temple will be situated on a 5.4-acre site at the intersection of Avinguda de la Vía Augusta and Avinguda de la Clota in Sant Cugat del Vallès, north of Barcelona. It will feature a two-story structure of about 27,500 square feet, along with a 13,600 square foot ancillary building for patron housing, an arrival center, and a distribution center. This temple will be the second in Spain, following the Madrid Spain Temple, which was dedicated in 1999.

name: Barranquilla Colombia Temple
address: Carrera 46 via Al Mar PR 107 Sentido
description: The Barranquilla Colombia Temple is located in the scenic coastal area of Puerto Colombia, about two kilometers west of Barranquilla, near Colegio Alemán. Situated on a hillside along the highway to Cartagena, it offers stunning views of the Magdalena River and the ocean. This temple, the second in Colombia after the Bogotá Colombia Temple, was announced by President Thomas S. Monson during the October 2011 General Conference. The groundbreaking ceremony occurred on February 20, 2016, marking the Church's 50th anniversary in Colombia, with Elder Juan A. Uceda presiding. The temple was dedicated on December 9, 2018, by President Dallin H. Oaks, who emphasized blessings for the nation and its leaders in his dedicatory prayer.

name: Baton Rouge Louisiana Temple
description: The Baton Rouge Louisiana Temple is located behind the stake center for the Baton Rouge Louisiana Stake, set against a scenic 103-acre wetlands nature reserve in South Baton Rouge. Its French-inspired interior design reflects the local heritage, while the surrounding gardens feature a prominent magnolia tree. This temple was the first to be built in Louisiana, with the Church's presence in the state beginning in January 1841. The groundbreaking took place on May 8, 1999, led by Elder Monte J. Brough, and the temple was dedicated in four sessions by President Gordon B. Hinckley, attended by over 4,600 members. After closing for extensive renovations in January 2018, the temple was updated with new landscaping, art glass windows, and refinished interiors.

name: Beira Mozambique Temple
description: The Beira Mozambique Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location officially announced. Renderings and site plans have not yet been made public. This temple will be the first of its kind in Mozambique and was announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the 191st Annual General Conference. Mozambique is home to over 15,000 Latter-day Saints, organized into 40 congregations. The city of Beira, where the temple will be located, has a population exceeding half a million and is situated along the Indian Ocean coast.

name: Belo Horizonte Brazil Temple
address: Rua Professor Jose Vieira de Mendonça 1485 Engenho Nogueira
description: The Belo Horizonte Brazil Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on June 17, 2023, led by Elder Juan A. Uceda from the Brazil Area presidency, alongside his wife, Maria Isabel, and Elder Luciano Sankar, an Area Seventy. Around 500 attendees, including government officials, were present. Elder Uceda offered a dedicatory prayer for the temple site, seeking divine protection and guidance for the construction. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 4, 2021, the temple will be located on an 11.8-acre site on Rua Professor Jose Vieira de Mendonça and will feature a single-story design of approximately 27,000 square feet. This temple will be the twelfth in Brazil and the first in the state of Minas Gerais.

name: Belém Brazil Temple
address: Av. Centenário da Assembleia de Deus 2200 Parque Verde
description: The Belém Brazil Temple is a significant landmark located on Avenida Centenário in Belém, a major city in northern Brazil with over two million residents. Situated near the Pará River, the temple was announced in 2016, coinciding with the 400th anniversary of Belém's founding, and was dedicated on November 20, 2022. This temple, the ninth in Brazil, features a striking design with Brazilian granite and a central spire that reaches 89 feet, reflecting local architectural styles. The temple grounds include extensive landscaping, providing a serene environment for visitors. Prior to the temple's construction, members of the Church traveled long distances to attend other temples, making this facility a welcomed addition to the community.

name: Bengaluru India Temple
address: 2-B ITPL Main Road Garudachar Palya Mahadevapura
description: The Bengaluru India Temple is set to be the first temple constructed in India. A groundbreaking ceremony took place on December 2, 2020, led by Elder Robert K. William, an Area Seventy. The temple will occupy a 1.62-acre site at 2-B Whitefield Main Road, Garudachar Palya, Mahadevapura, Bengaluru, and will feature a 38,670-square-foot structure with a prominent central spire and four smaller spires. In addition to the temple, the site will include a two-level meetinghouse, administrative offices, a distribution center, and a patron housing facility. The announcement for this temple was made by President Russell M. Nelson during the 188th Annual General Conference, marking a significant milestone for the Church in India.

name: Benin City Nigeria Temple
description: The Benin City Nigeria Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony presided over by Elder Adeyinka A. Ojediran, First Counselor in the Africa West Area Presidency, on Saturday, May 24, 2025. This temple will be built on a 2.17-acre site at 16 Commercial Avenue in Benin City. The design includes a two-story structure of approximately 30,700 square feet, featuring an arrival center and patron housing. The temple's location was announced on September 11, 2023, and the official exterior rendering was released on March 24, 2025. This temple will be Nigeria's third, following the Aba Nigeria Temple, dedicated in 2005, and the Lagos Nigeria Temple, which has been announced.

name: Bentonville Arkansas Temple
description: The Bentonville Arkansas Temple is the first temple established in Arkansas. Plans for its construction were announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 5, 2019, during the 189th Semiannual General Conference. The temple will be situated on an 8.8-acre site behind the Bentonville Arkansas Stake center, near I-49 and Highway 72, ensuring convenient access for local members. A groundbreaking ceremony took place on November 7, 2020, presided over by Elder David A. Bednar. The temple, which spans 25,000 square feet, was dedicated on September 17, 2023, and will serve Latter-day Saints in both Arkansas and Missouri.

name: Bern Switzerland Temple
description: The Bern Switzerland Temple is located in Zollikofen, on a hill near a national forest. It is a short four-minute walk from the Zollikofen railroad station and streetcar terminal. This temple was the first built in Europe and Switzerland, dedicated by President David O. McKay on September 11, 1955. It underwent extensive remodeling and was rededicated in 1992, adding more endowment and sealing rooms. In 2005, a statue of the angel Moroni was placed on the spire to commemorate the temple's 50th anniversary.

name: Billings Montana Temple
description: The Billings Montana Temple is the first temple established in Montana. Located in Billings, the state's largest city, it serves as a significant religious center for eastern Montana and northern Wyoming. The temple features a distinctive exterior, including a spire topped with a statue of Angel Moroni and a stained-glass bay window. Inside, it efficiently incorporates amenities typical of larger temples, such as ordinance rooms and a chapel, all within a compact design. The temple's dedication was a momentous occasion for many local members, who previously faced long travel times to attend other temples.

name: Birmingham Alabama Temple
description: The Birmingham Alabama Temple is situated in the picturesque suburb of Gardendale, just north of Birmingham, on a hillside east of I-65. Its grounds are beautifully landscaped with mature trees and shrubs, and during Christmas, Nativity-themed statues are displayed and illuminated at night. This temple was the first to be established in Alabama. Prior to its dedication, the temple welcomed over 21,000 visitors during a public open house. The temple features an exterior of Imperial Danby White Marble from Vermont and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Birmingham England Temple
description: The Birmingham England Temple had its groundbreaking ceremony on March 22, 2025, led by Elder Scott D. Whiting, a member of the Seventy and president of the Europe North Area. The temple will serve as a symbol of faith and community, benefiting both its visitors and the surrounding area. The official exterior design was unveiled on February 26, 2024, and the temple will be located on a 2.7-acre site at 185-187 Penns Lane, which also houses the Wylde Green Ward meetinghouse and the England Birmingham Mission offices. Plans include a single-story structure of about 10,800 square feet, along with patron housing and arrival facilities. This temple will be the third in England, following the London England Temple and the Preston England Temple.

name: Bismarck North Dakota Temple
description: The Bismarck North Dakota Temple is the first temple established in the Dakotas and in North Dakota. Its completion significantly reduced travel times for members in the temple district, who previously journeyed long distances to attend other temples. For instance, residents of Grand Forks faced a 16-hour drive to Chicago, while those in Minot traveled 14 hours to Cardston, Alberta. The temple's first president, Robert B. Dahlgren, highlighted the dedication of the members, including a retired couple who relocated to Bismarck to serve full-time. President Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated the temple during his first visit to North Dakota, marking a notable moment in his extensive travels.

name: Bogotá Colombia Temple
description: The Bogotá Colombia Temple is the first temple constructed in Colombia and the fifth in South America. The time from its announcement to the groundbreaking ceremony spanned over nine years due to challenges in securing a suitable location and property. It is the 57th temple dedicated for operation. The exterior is finished with Brazilian granite known as Asa Branca. Notable architectural features include a single attached end spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Boise Idaho Temple
description: The Boise Idaho Temple is a prominent landmark for travelers on Interstate 84, located at the I-84 Cole Road Exit. Its design features a light granite exterior, a large sloping roof, and six tall spires, complemented by a water feature and mature trees on the grounds. This temple, dedicated in 1984, was the second built in Idaho, following the Idaho Falls Idaho Temple, and was the first six-spire temple constructed since the Washington D.C. Temple. The Boise Idaho Temple underwent significant renovations, reopening in May 1987 and again in February 2012, which included updates to its facilities and landscaping. It is recognized for its high usage, operating at full capacity shortly after its dedication.

name: Boston Massachusetts Temple
description: The Boston Massachusetts Temple is located on a wooded granite hillside in Belmont, a northwest suburb, and serves as a notable landmark along Concord Turnpike. Visitors can explore the temple grounds and the adjacent meetinghouse, which are surrounded by beautifully landscaped areas and winding walkways. This temple was the first built in New England and marked the 100th operational temple of the Church, fulfilling President Gordon B. Hinckley's goal of having 100 temples by the end of 2000. Originally, the site was intended for a meetinghouse, but the design ultimately allowed for the temple's construction on the upper portion of the property. The temple features a 139-foot steeple, added after a legal dispute, and an angel Moroni statue was installed on September 21, 2001, commemorating a significant anniversary in Church history.

name: Bountiful Utah Temple
description: The Bountiful Utah Temple is situated in the foothills of Bountiful's east bench, providing stunning views of the valley and the Great Salt Lake. It boasts a striking circular columned atrium that connects the lower and main parking levels, along with an elegant portico adorned with columns and arches. A water feature cascades on the east side, located beneath the Holiness to the Lord plaque. This temple, the eighth in Utah and the first in Davis County, had its floor plan adapted for the Mount Timpanogos Utah Temple. Notably, it was dedicated by President Howard W. Hunter and saw a record attendance of 201,655 members during its dedicatory sessions.

name: Brasília Brazil Temple
description: The Brasília Brazil Temple is the tenth temple in Brazil and the first in the Federal District. Announced by President Thomas S. Monson on April 2, 2017, during the 187th Annual General Conference, it aims to serve the over 1.3 million Church members in Brazil. The temple, which features a single-level design of 25,000 square feet, is located on a six-acre site near Paranoá Lake and includes a patron housing facility and meetinghouse. The temple was dedicated on September 17, 2023, by Elder Neil L. Andersen, with its design showcasing white Brazilian marble, stained glass windows, and landscaped gardens. The interior features Brazilian materials and artwork, enhancing its spiritual ambiance.

name: Brazzaville Republic of the Congo Temple
address: Avenue de la Republique (formerly 103 and 109 Rue Lamonthé) Bacongo
photoCaption: Brazzaville Republic of the Congo Temple
description: The Brazzaville Republic of the Congo Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on August 23, 2025, led by Elder Thierry K. Mutombo, the Africa Central Area President. The temple will be situated on a 1.5-acre site on Avenue de la Republique in the Bacongo neighborhood of Brazzaville, which is the capital of the Republic of the Congo. The design includes a single-story structure of about 10,000 square feet, along with patron housing and arrival facilities. Plans for the temple were first announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the April 2022 General Conference. This temple will be the first in the Republic of the Congo, where the Church has over 8,000 members across 29 congregations.

name: Brigham City Utah Temple
description: The Brigham City Utah Temple had its gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni installed on July 12, 2011, between 1:40 and 2:30 p.m., after weather delays pushed back the original noon schedule. Approximately 5,000 spectators gathered as all surrounding streets were closed for the event. The temple's groundbreaking took place on July 31, 2010, led by President Boyd K. Packer, who expressed a vision of the temple reflecting the design of earlier temples, particularly the Salt Lake Temple. The site, located on Main Street known as Central Square, was previously home to Central Elementary School and was officially purchased on November 5, 2009. The temple, which features a 9,000-square-foot footprint and three above-ground levels, won the PCI Design Award for Best Religious Structure in 2014.

name: Brisbane Australia South Temple
description: The Brisbane Australia South Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for the temple during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the second in the Brisbane area and the sixth in Australia, joining the existing Brisbane Australia Temple, which was dedicated in June 2003. At the time of the announcement, there were over 155,000 Church members in more than 300 congregations across Australia. The Brisbane Australia South Temple will mark Brisbane as the eleventh city worldwide to have multiple temples, and it will be the eighth metropolitan area outside the United States with more than one temple.

name: Brisbane Australia Temple
description: The Brisbane Australia Temple is situated on the scenic Kangaroo Point cliffs, providing views of the Brisbane River and the central business district. This striking granite structure is located next to a meetinghouse that was constructed simultaneously. An underground parking facility is available for visitors. The temple's landscaped grounds are accessible to the public, allowing them to enjoy the beautiful architecture and stunning vistas. As the fifth temple established in Australia, it follows the Sydney (1984), Adelaide (2000), Melbourne (2000), and Perth (2001) temples, and it was the second temple announced for the country.

name: Brussels Belgium Temple
description: The Brussels Belgium Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The location for the temple has been confirmed as an existing building at Ave des Arts 52 in Brussels, which will undergo interior renovations. The temple will feature a multistory design of approximately 25,500 square feet, along with a meetinghouse and arrival facilities. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021. This temple will be the first for the Church in Belgium, serving around 7,000 Latter-day Saints across various congregations.

name: Budapest Hungary Temple
address: Kocsis Sándor út and Borsikaf? utca Harsánylejt?
description: The Budapest Hungary Temple is a significant project for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, with groundbreaking taking place on June 21, 2025. The temple will be located on a 5.92-acre site at the intersection of Kocsis Sándor út and Borsikafū utca in the Harsánylejtő neighborhood. It will feature a one-story structure of approximately 18,000 square feet, along with an arrival center and patron housing. The official exterior rendering was unveiled on March 4, 2024, and construction is expected to last three years. This temple will be the first in Hungary and the sixteenth in Europe, serving the local Latter-day Saint community, which currently travels to the Freiberg Germany Temple for worship.

name: Buenos Aires Argentina Temple
description: The Buenos Aires Argentina Temple is situated on the western edge of Buenos Aires in Ciudad Evita, accessible via the Teniente General Pablo Ricchieri Freeway. The temple features prominent sloping roofs, six tall spires, and three wings extending from a central foyer. The site also includes a Missionary Training Center and housing for temple workers and patrons, all set within beautifully landscaped grounds that feature a grand plaza with a water feature. Groundbreaking for the temple occurred on April 20, 1983, and it was dedicated shortly after the Lima Perú Temple. The temple underwent significant renovations starting on November 1, 2009, which included the addition of two new wings and a new angel Moroni statue placed atop the tallest spire on August 1, 2011.

name: Buenos Aires City Center Argentina Temple
photoCaption: Buenos Aires City Center Argentina Temple
description: The Buenos Aires City Center Argentina Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple's location was announced on December 16, 2024, at a 1.56-acre site at the intersection of Avenida Córdoba and Reconquista in the San Nicolás neighborhood of Downtown Buenos Aires. An exterior rendering was released on June 9, 2025, showcasing a multistory building that will include a replica of the Christus statue. This temple will be the sixth in Argentina and the tenth in Buenos Aires, joining the existing Buenos Aires Argentina Temple dedicated in 1986. Argentina has approximately 475,000 Latter-day Saints and 725 congregations within its population of over 45 million.

name: Burley Idaho Temple
description: The Burley Idaho Temple's open house and dedication dates have been set. The public open house will occur from November 6 to November 22, 2025, excluding Sundays, following a media day on November 3 and tours for invited guests on November 4 and 5. The temple will be dedicated on January 11, 2026, with the dedicatory session broadcast to congregations in the temple district. Groundbreaking took place on June 4, 2022, led by Elder Brent H. Nielson, who has ties to Burley. This temple will be the seventh in Idaho, featuring a two-story structure of approximately 38,600 square feet on a 10.1-acre site.

name: Busan Korea Temple
description: The Busan Korea Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for the Busan Korea Temple during the October 2022 General Conference, marking it as the second temple in South Korea, following the completion of the first in Seoul in 1985. The country is home to nearly 90,000 Latter-day Saints across 100 congregations. Busan, known as Korea's busiest port, has a significant history with the Church, dating back to the introduction of its teachings by Latter-day Saint service members in the 1940s.

name: Cagayan de Oro Philippines Temple
address: Lot 2163-c and Lot 2163-d Rosario Limketkai Avenue
description: The Cagayan de Oro Philippines Temple is set to begin construction following a groundbreaking ceremony on August 31, 2024, attended by leaders from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and local community representatives. Elder Carlos G. Revillo Jr., President of the Philippines Area, presided over the event. This temple will be the second on Mindanao, joining the Davao Philippines Temple, which is currently being built. Located on a 4.9-acre site on Rosario Limketkai Avenue in Cagayan de Oro City, the two-story temple will encompass approximately 18,449 square feet and include an ancillary building with an arrival center, patron housing, and a distribution center. The Cagayan de Oro Philippines Temple will be the seventh temple in the Philippines, complementing existing temples in Manila and Cebu City, with additional temples planned for Urdaneta and the greater Manila area.

name: Calabar Nigeria Temple
description: The Calabar Nigeria Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for the temple during the October 2023 General Conference. Calabar, a port city in southern Nigeria, has a population exceeding 657,000. This temple will be the fifth in Nigeria, joining the existing temples in Aba, Benin City, Eket, and Lagos. As of the announcement, there were about 225,000 Latter-day Saints in Nigeria, which established its first stake in 1988, following the Church's arrival in the country in 1978.

name: Caldwell Idaho Temple
description: The Caldwell Idaho Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the third in the Boise metropolitan area, joining the Boise Idaho Temple, dedicated in 1984, and the Meridian Idaho Temple, dedicated in 2017. The Caldwell Idaho Temple will be the 11th temple in Idaho, which has over 475,000 Church members across more than 1,225 congregations. Other temples in the state include the Burley, Coeur d'Alene, Idaho Falls, Meridian, Montpelier, Pocatello, Rexburg, Teton River, and Twin Falls Idaho Temples.

name: Calgary Alberta Temple
description: The Calgary Alberta Temple was the site of a significant event on January 12, 2012, when numerous members gathered at the Royal Oak Chapel to witness the installation of the angel Moroni statue. The atmosphere was filled with excitement as hot chocolate was served, and various activities took place, including media interviews and singing by seminary students. The statue was successfully raised and secured by 9:20 a.m. Groundbreaking for the temple occurred on May 15, 2010, during a ceremony attended by around 1,600 individuals, including Elder Donald L. Hallstrom, who emphasized the temple's purpose of connecting individuals with God. Announced by President Thomas S. Monson on October 4, 2008, the Calgary Alberta Temple is Alberta's third temple, joining those in Cardston and Edmonton.

name: Cali Colombia Temple
address: Calle 50 Norte and Avenida 4a Norte Barrio La Flora
description: Elder Jorge T. Becerra, president of the South America Northwest Area, will lead the groundbreaking ceremony for the Cali Colombia Temple on March 1, 2025. This temple will be situated on a 3.14-acre site in the La Flora neighborhood of Cali, Colombia, and will feature a single-story design of approximately 9,500 square feet. It will be the third temple in Colombia, following the Bogotá Colombia Temple, dedicated in 1999, and the Barranquilla Colombia Temple, dedicated in 2018. Plans for the Cali Colombia Temple were announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021. Colombia has around 210,000 Latter-day Saints across nearly 250 congregations, with missionary work beginning in the country in 1966.

name: Campinas Brazil Temple
address: Rua James Esdras Faust 400 Notre Dame
description: The Campinas Brazil Temple is situated on a hillside and can be seen from various locations throughout the city of Campinas, which has a population exceeding two million. Its location near three major highways ensures easy access for both cars and buses. This temple is the fourth to be constructed in Brazil and the second in São Paulo, following the São Paulo Brazil Temple, which was completed in 1978. The temple features a light gray Asa Branca granite exterior sourced from Ceará and includes a single attached central spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni. It was dedicated as the 111th temple in operation.

name: Campo Grande Brazil Temple
description: The Campo Grande Brazil Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for this temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. It will be the 24th temple in Brazil. At the time of the announcement, nine other temples were also recently announced for the country, while eleven temples were already in operation and three were under construction. Brazil has over 1.5 million Latter-day Saints, making it the third-largest population of Latter-day Saints outside the United States.

name: Cancún Mexico Temple
description: The Cancún Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the October 2023 General Conference. This temple will be the first in Quintana Roo and the 24th in Mexico. Currently, there are dedicated temples in various cities, including Mexico City and Guadalajara, along with others under construction or announced. Mexico has approximately 1.5 million Latter-day Saints across more than 1,800 congregations, with missionary work beginning in 1875.

name: Cape Coast Ghana Temple
description: The Cape Coast Ghana Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the October 2023 General Conference. Cape Coast, located in south-central Ghana, is recognized as one of the nation's historic areas. This temple will be the third in Ghana, following the Accra Ghana Temple, dedicated in 2004, and the Kumasi Ghana Temple, announced in April 2021. The country is home to over 100,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 350 congregations.

name: Cape Town South Africa Temple
description: The Cape Town South Africa Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony presided over by Elder Carlos A. Godoy, Africa South Area President, on Saturday, October 25, 2025. This single-story temple will cover approximately 9,500 square feet and will be built on a 3.79-acre site adjacent to the mission office in the Observatory neighborhood of Cape Town. In addition to the temple, an arrival center and meetinghouse will also be constructed on the property. The announcement for the temple's location was made on December 7, 2021, following President Russell M. Nelson's announcement of its construction plans during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021. This temple will be the third in South Africa, joining the Johannesburg South Africa Temple and the Durban South Africa Temple.

name: Caracas Venezuela Temple
address: Urb Caurimare Avenida. C con Calle C-1
description: The Caracas Venezuela Temple is the first temple established in Venezuela. Announced on May 23, 1998, it was designed as part of a new generation of smaller temples initiated by President Gordon B. Hinckley. This temple serves approximately 85,000 members across sixteen stakes and eleven districts, significantly reducing the distance to a temple from the previous closest one, the Lima Peru Temple, which is about 2,000 miles away. The groundbreaking ceremony was led by Elder Francisco J. Viñas, who emphasized the importance of personal preparation and the responsibility of members to maintain the temple. The Caracas Venezuela Temple, featuring a granite exterior and a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue, is the 96th temple dedicated by the Church.

name: Cardston Alberta Temple
description: The Cardston Alberta Temple is a significant landmark located on elevated ground in Cardston, Alberta. Established in 1887 by settlers of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, it is situated just 15 miles north of the U.S.-Canada border. This temple was the first in Canada and the first built outside the United States, featuring a design that was open to bids from architects. Notably, it lacks a steeple and priesthood assembly room, marking a shift in temple design. The temple was dedicated in 1923 after a decade of construction, which included a three-year renovation completed in 1991, and it was designated a Canadian Historic Site in 1995.

name: Casper Wyoming Temple
description: The Casper Wyoming Temple will hold an open house for the public from Thursday, August 29, to Saturday, September 14, 2024, excluding Sundays. Prior to this, a media day is scheduled for Monday, August 26, followed by tours for invited guests. The dedication, presided over by Elder Quentin L. Cook of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, will take place on Sunday, November 24, at 10 a.m. This temple, the second in Wyoming, will be located on a 9.5-acre site at the intersection of Wyoming Boulevard Southwest and Eagle Drive. The temple's design includes a single-story structure of approximately 10,000 square feet, with landscaping that reflects the local prairie environment.

name: Cebu City Philippines Temple
description: The Cebu City Philippines Temple is the second temple established in the Philippines, following the Manila Philippines Temple, which was completed in 1984. It was announced to Filipino priesthood leaders in a letter dated April 18, 2006. A gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni was installed on top of the temple on November 5, 2009. The temple experienced movement of the angel Moroni due to the 2013 Bohol earthquake on October 15, causing it to shift from facing east to south. The statue was realigned to face east again on January 22, 2014. The temple features mountain grey granite from China and has a single attached central spire.

name: Cedar City Utah Temple
description: The Cedar City Utah Temple is located on Leigh Hill, west of the city center, offering stunning views of the surrounding valley and mountains. This three-story temple features an exterior design reminiscent of the historic Box Elder Stake Tabernacle in Brigham City, Utah. It was the seventeenth temple constructed in Utah and the first in Iron County, with groundbreaking taking place on August 8, 2015. The temple was dedicated by President Henry B. Eyring on December 10, 2017, after a youth cultural celebration that highlighted the area's pioneer history. The temple's design incorporates local flora in its glasswork and landscaping, reflecting the natural environment of southern Utah.

name: Charlotte North Carolina Temple
description: The Charlotte North Carolina Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The site, announced on May 30, 2023, is a 5.9-acre property located at 345 Providence Rd S in Weddington, south of Charlotte. The temple will be a single-story structure, approximately 30,000 square feet in size. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the April 2023 General Conference, marking it as North Carolina's second temple. Charlotte, the state's largest city, has a population of nearly 900,000 and is home to over 94,000 Latter-day Saints across nearly 180 congregations.

name: Chicago Illinois Temple
description: The Chicago Illinois Temple is situated on an 80-acre nature sanctuary in Glenview, a northern suburb of Chicago, near I-294. This temple features six white-tipped spires, with the tallest spire reaching 112 feet and topped by a gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni. It is the first operating temple in the Midwest and the second built in Illinois, following the Nauvoo Temple. The temple underwent significant remodeling after its closure on September 3, 1988, which expanded its size and added new facilities while maintaining its exterior appearance. In December 2008, the temple experienced extensive water damage due to a burst pipe, leading to a swift restoration effort.

name: Chiclayo Peru Temple
description: The Chiclayo Peru Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the October 2022 General Conference. It will be the sixth temple in Peru, a country with approximately 625,000 Latter-day Saints across 780 congregations. Chiclayo is situated in northern Peru, a short distance from the Pacific coast. Other temples either in operation or under construction include the Arequipa Peru Temple, Cusco Peru Temple, Lima Peru Temple, Trujillo Peru Temple, and Lima Peru Los Olivos Temple.

name: Chihuahua Mexico Temple
address: Avenida de la Cantera and Avenida Real Escondido Reserva Territorial la Hacienda
description: The Chihuahua Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. On June 9, 2025, the temple's exterior rendering was made public, and its location was confirmed as a 5.87-acre site at the intersection of Avenida de la Cantera and Avenida Real Escondido in the Reserva Territorial la Hacienda neighborhood. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the 25th in Mexico, which has over 1.5 million Latter-day Saints across more than 1,875 congregations. The country is home to several dedicated temples and others that are either under construction or announced.

name: Chorrillos Peru Temple
description: The Chorrillos Peru Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the tenth dedicated to the Lord in Peru. Chorrillos, situated along the Pacific Ocean, is known for its popular beaches. In Peru, there are nearly 650,000 Latter-day Saints organized into about 800 congregations.

name: Cincinnati Ohio Temple
address: Mason-Montgomery Road and Cedar Village Drive
description: The Cincinnati Ohio Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple's location was announced on April 29, 2024, as a 35-acre site at the intersection of Mason-Montgomery Road and Cedar Village Drive in Mason. An official exterior rendering was made public on December 23, 2024. The temple will be a single-story structure, approximately 29,630 square feet in size. Once completed, it will be one of three operating temples in Ohio, joining the Columbus Ohio Temple and the Cleveland Ohio Temple.

name: Ciudad Juárez Mexico Temple
address: Calle Paraguay #290 Esq. José Borunda Col. Partido Romero
description: The Ciudad Juárez Mexico Temple is the third temple established in Mexico and the second in Chihuahua, following the Colonia Juárez Chihuahua Mexico Temple, which was completed in 1999. The groundbreaking ceremony took place simultaneously with that of the Villahermosa Mexico Temple. President Gordon B. Hinckley led the first of six dedicatory sessions on February 26, 2000, before departing to dedicate the Hermosillo Sonora Mexico Temple. Located in a bustling border city near El Paso, Texas, the temple serves approximately 12,000 members organized into five stakes. The temple's construction was inspired and approved by President Hinckley, emphasizing the importance of temples in the faith and community.

name: Cleveland Ohio Temple
description: The Cleveland Ohio Temple is set to be constructed following a groundbreaking ceremony led by Elder Vaiangina Sikahema on June 1, 2024. He acknowledged the contributions of early pioneers in the area during his dedicatory prayer. The temple will be located on Brecksville Road in Independence, Cuyahoga County, with plans for a single-story structure of approximately 9,000 square feet and a 100-foot spire. An ancillary building of 2,200 square feet will provide facilities for waiting, restrooms, and maintenance storage. This temple will be Ohio's second operating temple, joining the Columbus Ohio Temple, which was dedicated in 1999.

name: Cobán Guatemala Temple
description: The Cobán Guatemala Temple is the third temple established in Guatemala. President Russell M. Nelson announced its construction on October 5, 2019, during the 189th Semiannual General Conference. The temple's location was revealed on May 25, 2020, in the southeastern part of Cobán, next to the Cobán 2nd Ward meetinghouse. The temple will be a single-level structure covering approximately 8,800 square feet, with plans for a patron housing facility on the site. Elder Dale G. Renlund of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles is scheduled to dedicate the temple on June 9, 2024.

name: Cochabamba Bolivia Temple
address: Av. Melchor Urquidi 1500 Alto Queru Queru
description: The Cochabamba Bolivia Temple is the first temple established in Bolivia. Prominently visible from its grounds is the Cristo de la Concordia statue on San Pedro hill, which is the largest statue of Christ globally, slightly taller than the Cristo Redentor in Rio de Janeiro. Both statues stand at 33 meters, symbolizing the years of Christ's life. During the groundbreaking ceremony, President Gordon B. Hinckley encouraged members to obtain a temple recommend and prepare for the temple's dedication. The temple, featuring a blend of hand-hewn Comanche granite and plaster, includes a central tower with four smaller towers and an angel Moroni statue.

name: Cody Wyoming Temple
description: The Cody Wyoming Temple is set to be built following a groundbreaking ceremony on September 27, 2024, led by Elder Steven R. Bangerter, First Counselor in the North America Central Area Presidency. Elder Kevin R. Duncan, Executive Director of the Temple Department, also attended the event. The temple, announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 3, 2021, will be approximately 9,950 square feet and feature a multi-tiered steeple topped with a gold pyramidal spire. The site is located northwest of Skyline Drive and Cody Canal in Cody, Wyoming, which is home to a significant population of members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. This temple will be the third in Wyoming, following the Star Valley Wyoming Temple and the Casper Wyoming Temple, which is currently under construction.

name: Coeur d'Alene Idaho Temple
description: The Coeur d'Alene Idaho Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the tenth in Idaho, joining others such as the Boise Idaho Temple and the Idaho Falls Idaho Temple. Coeur d'Alene, located in northern Idaho, has a population exceeding 50,000. Idaho is home to over 475,000 members of the Church, with a rich history dating back to early pioneers in 1855.

name: Colonia Juárez Chihuahua Mexico Temple
description: The Colonia Juárez Chihuahua Mexico Temple is the second temple constructed in Mexico and the first in Chihuahua. It is notable for being the first of the smaller temples designed by President Gordon B. Hinckley, located outside the United States. This temple is the 55th to be dedicated and is characterized by its exterior of gleaming white marble. It features a single attached spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Colorado Springs Colorado Temple
address: Flying Horse Club Drive and Barossa Valley Road
description: The Colorado Springs Colorado Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. An official exterior rendering was made public on May 5, 2025. The temple will be situated on an 18.6-acre site in the Northgate neighborhood, near the intersection of Flying Horse Club Drive and Barossa Valley Road. It is designed as a single-story structure of about 45,000 square feet, accompanied by a meetinghouse and a grounds maintenance building. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 1, 2023, this temple will be the fourth in Colorado, joining the existing Denver and Fort Collins temples, while the Grand Junction temple is under construction.

name: Columbia River Washington Temple
description: The Columbia River Washington Temple is the third temple established in Washington, following the Seattle Washington Temple in 1980 and the Spokane Washington Temple in 1999. The groundbreaking ceremony was led by Elder Stephen A. West, who emphasized the importance of homes being places where the Lord feels welcome. This temple holds special significance for many second and third generation Latter-day Saints who relocated to Richland during the Hanford site's development in World War II. The temple provides these long-time residents with closer access to temple worship, similar to what many in Utah experience. The temple features an exterior of Bethel white granite from Vermont and Italy, along with a single attached spire topped by a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Columbia South Carolina Temple
description: The Columbia South Carolina Temple is the first temple established in South Carolina. Its groundbreaking took place on the same day as the Hermosillo Sonora Mexico Temple. During the ten-day open house, approximately 20,000 visitors explored the temple's interior. The temple is situated in a picturesque wooded area in southeastern Columbia, surrounded by native loblolly pine and oak, and landscaped with various local flora. The temple features an exterior of Imperial Danby White variegated marble from Vermont and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Columbus Ohio Temple
description: The Columbus Ohio Temple is situated 150 miles south of Kirtland, Ohio, where the first temple of the restored Church of Jesus Christ was dedicated in 1836. Nestled in a wooded area of western Columbus, it is adjacent to a meetinghouse in the Columbus Ohio Stake. The temple's exterior is adorned with white marble from Spain, and the magnolia blossom is a prominent design element both inside and out. It was the second temple established in Ohio, following the Kirtland Temple, which ceased operations in the late 1830s. The Columbus Ohio Temple underwent extensive renovations starting August 15, 2020, and reopened with significant updates, including improved climate control and enhanced natural lighting, culminating in the reinstallation of the angel Moroni statue on December 9, 2021.

name: Concepción Chile Temple
description: The Concepción Chile Temple is situated in the Quinta Junge residential area, adjacent to the Biobío River. This striking temple serves as a notable landmark, particularly illuminated at night along Avenida Pedro de Valdivia. It includes a patron housing facility for visitors traveling from afar and is surrounded by lush gardens featuring palm trees and vibrant flowers. As the second temple established in Chile, following the Santiago Chile Temple in 1983, it was built with a floating foundation to withstand seismic activity. The temple was dedicated on October 28, 2018, by President Russell M. Nelson, marking it as the 160th operating temple of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

name: Copenhagen Denmark Temple
description: The Copenhagen Denmark Temple is the ninth temple established in Europe and the second in the Nordic region, following the Stockholm Sweden Temple (1985). It is the second temple constructed from an existing building, after the Vernal Utah Temple (1997). The temple underwent a complete renovation of the Priorvej chapel, originally built in 1931, with Elder John A. Widtsoe dedicating it. The groundbreaking took place simultaneously with the San José Costa Rica Temple, but construction faced delays due to issues with the building's dimensions and the area's high water table. The temple features a copper dome over the Celestial Room and a baptismal font illuminated by a skylight, while a new meetinghouse, the Nitivej Chapel, was built nearby for tours during the temple's open house.

name: Cuernavaca Mexico Temple
address: Calle Hernán Cortes and Calle Santa Prisca Colonia Vista Hermosa
description: The Cuernavaca Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The temple will be situated on a 5.36-acre site in the Colonia Vista Hermosa neighborhood, southeast of Calle Hernán Cortes and Calle Santa Prisca. An exterior rendering was made public on December 23, 2024, and the temple is designed to be a single-story structure of about 19,000 square feet. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the October 2022 General Conference. Cuernavaca, located approximately 50 miles south of Mexico City, is the capital of Morelos and has a population of around 350,000.

name: Culiacán Mexico Temple
description: The Culiacán Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The temple will be situated on a 5-acre site near the Culiacán River, off Avenida Milenium, between Miguel Tamayo Espinoza de los Monteros and Boulevard José María Figueroa Díaz. It is designed to be a one-story structure of approximately 10,000 square feet, accompanied by a patron housing facility. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the October 2021 General Conference, marking it as the 17th temple in Mexico. Culiacán, officially known as Culiacán Rosales, is located in northwestern Mexico and has a population of around 850,000.

name: Curitiba Brazil Temple
address: Rua Deputado Heitor Alencar Furtado 3641 Mossunguê
description: The Curitiba Brazil Temple is situated in the Campo Comprido district of western Curitiba, surrounded by trees and beautiful landscaping, including a large water feature and gardens. It is conveniently located near the Unidade Saúde Campo Comprido bus stop and the Barigui Shopping Center, with public access to the grounds. This temple was the fifth to be built in Brazil, with its design also used for the Vancouver British Columbia Temple and Manaus Brazil Temple. The temple's gold-leafed angel Moroni statue was placed on the spire on January 11, 2008, following a two-week public open house that attracted over 42,000 visitors. The dedication of the temple was presided over by President Thomas S. Monson, marking a significant moment for the local community and the Church.

name: Cusco Peru Temple
description: The Cusco Peru Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple will be situated on a 2.48-acre site at Avenida Arcopata 452 in Cusco, as announced on January 29, 2024. It is designed to cover approximately 9,950 square feet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the construction plans during the April 2022 General Conference, marking it as the fifth temple in Peru. The country has around 625,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 775 congregations.

name: Córdoba Argentina Temple
description: The Córdoba Argentina Temple was officially announced by President Thomas S. Monson during the 178th Semiannual General Conference of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on October 30, 2010, led by Elder Neil L. Andersen, along with other church leaders and local dignitaries. The temple, located near the Villa Belgrano meetinghouse, is Argentina's second temple, following the Buenos Aires Argentina Temple. The construction site was acquired in February 2010, after negotiations for a former sports complex. The temple features a light grey granite exterior and a gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni atop its spire, with its dedication marking a significant milestone for church members in northern Argentina.

name: Dallas Texas Temple
description: The Dallas Texas Temple features six spires that rise above the trees in a residential area of northern Dallas. Its striking architecture, including a large sloping roof, reflects its sacred purpose. The temple grounds are beautifully landscaped with trimmed hedges and colorful flowers. As the first temple established in Texas, it serves as a sister building to the Boise Idaho Temple and the Chicago Illinois Temple. The temple has undergone significant renovations, including a remodeling in 1987 that expanded its facilities and a grounds renovation completed in June 2006, enhancing accessibility and aesthetics.

name: Davao Philippines Temple
address: Ma-a Road and Anahaw Road Barangay Ma-a
description: The Davao Philippines Temple is being constructed in Barangay Ma-a, with groundbreaking taking place on November 14, 2020. Elder Taniela B. Wakolo, president of the Philippines Area, emphasized the significance of the temple in his remarks during the ceremony. The two-story temple will cover approximately 18,450 square feet and will be built on a 2.7-acre site at the intersection of Ma-a Road and Anahaw Road, replacing an existing meetinghouse. This temple will be the fifth in the Philippines and the first in Mindanao, contributing to the growing presence of over 780,000 Church members in the country. Plans for the Davao Philippines Temple were announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the 188th Semiannual General Conference on October 7, 2018.

name: Denver Colorado Temple
description: The Denver Colorado Temple is situated in the suburb of Centennial, south of Denver, within a picturesque residential area. Its striking white exterior is complemented by vibrant flowers during the growing season, a serene water feature with benches, a colorful stained glass wall at the entrance, and a gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni atop its spire. This temple was the first built in Colorado, with its site history dating back to the S. M. Rooker family's settlement in 1858. The construction faced challenges, including initial site rejections and community concerns about floodlighting, but ultimately gained local support. The temple's dedication saw over 28,000 attendees, and it originally served a wide district across several states before undergoing renovations in 2011.

name: Des Moines Iowa Temple
description: The Des Moines Iowa Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple's location was announced on April 29, 2024, as a 19.576-acre site at 9050 NW 62nd Avenue in Johnston. An official exterior rendering was made public on December 23, 2024. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the first in Iowa, a state with over 29,000 Latter-day Saints across approximately 70 congregations.

name: Deseret Peak Utah Temple
description: The Deseret Peak Utah Temple is the twenty-third temple constructed in Utah and the first in Tooele County. Announced on April 7, 2019, it is located in the Tooele Valley, which has twelve organized stakes. The temple site was confirmed on September 25, 2019, in Erda, and it will feature a three-story building of about 70,000 square feet alongside a 20,000-square-foot meetinghouse. Groundbreaking took place on May 15, 2021, with the temple dedicated by President Russell M. Nelson on November 10, 2024. The temple's design incorporates local flora in its art glass and features a unique exterior finish of glass fiber reinforced concrete.

name: Detroit Michigan Temple
description: The Detroit Michigan Temple is the first temple established in Michigan. Its groundbreaking took place on October 10, 1998, coinciding with the Spokane Washington Temple's groundbreaking, marking a unique event in temple history. During the dedication, cold weather brought winds and freezing rain, yet local leaders expressed optimism about the temple's significance. President Hinckley acknowledged the gratitude of the members for this sacred structure and its historical connection to early Church figures. The temple, located on Woodward Avenue in Bloomfield Hills, benefits from its visibility while maintaining a serene environment due to its landscaped surroundings.

name: Draper Utah Temple
description: The Draper Utah Temple is situated on a ridgeline near Draper's Corner Canyon, offering stunning views of the Salt Lake Valley across its 1,021 acres of open space. This granite temple shares its site with a meetinghouse and a parking lot, both built concurrently. Visitors can explore the beautifully landscaped grounds and appreciate the temple's spiritual ambiance. As the twelfth temple in Utah and the third in the Salt Lake Valley, it features unique art-glass windows created by Tom Holdman, which survived a fire that damaged the artist's studio. Groundbreaking for the temple occurred on August 5, 2006, and it includes the largest sealing room in Utah, accommodating up to 80 guests.

name: Dubai United Arab Emirates Temple
description: The Dubai United Arab Emirates Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date announced yet. Renderings and site plans have not been publicly shared. This temple will be situated in District 2020, the venue for Expo 2020 Dubai. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 5, 2020, during the 190th Annual General Conference, it will be the first temple in the Middle East. The temple aims to serve members from two stakes in the Gulf States and smaller congregations across a broad region, including parts of the Middle East and Northern Africa.

name: Dublin Ireland Temple
description: The Dublin Ireland Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the first of its kind in Ireland. The capital city, Dublin, is where the restored gospel of the Church of Jesus Christ was first introduced in 1840. Currently, approximately 4,000 Latter-day Saints in Ireland worship in 13 congregations and travel to England for temple services.

name: Durban South Africa Temple
description: The Durban South Africa Temple is located in the Izinga development, north of the Umhlanga city center. Perched on a grassy knoll, it offers views of the ocean and surrounding sugar cane fields, while being bordered by a residential area characterized by earthy tones and red clay tile roofs. Announced by President Thomas S. Monson on October 1, 2011, the temple was the fifth built in Africa and the second in South Africa, following the Johannesburg South Africa Temple. The groundbreaking took place on April 9, 2016, and the temple was dedicated in three sessions on February 16, 2020, by Elder Ronald A. Rasband. The temple's design reflects local architecture, featuring a pitched red clay tile roof and indigenous landscaping, with over 800 trees and various art pieces celebrating African themes.

name: Edinburgh Scotland Temple
description: The Edinburgh Scotland Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the first in Scotland and the fourth in the United Kingdom, which includes England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. Edinburgh has served as Scotland's capital since the 15th century. At the time of the announcement, there were approximately 185,000 Latter-day Saints in over 300 congregations across the UK.

name: Edmonton Alberta Temple
description: The Edmonton Alberta Temple is the fifth temple established in Canada and the second in Alberta, following the Cardston Alberta Temple built in 1923. Located in Alberta's capital city, the temple features designs inspired by the province's wild rose and wheat, visible from Whitemud Freeway. Although the Church had a presence in Edmonton since 1920, the first official meeting occurred in 1933, with the first dedicated building following in 1951. The temple was announced on August 11, 1998, and its dedication marked a significant milestone for the local community, fostering unity among Church members across northern Alberta. The temple, constructed with light gray granite from Quebec, includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Eket Nigeria Temple
description: The Eket Nigeria Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple will be situated on a 7-acre site along Eket/Oron Road in Ikot Ibiok, within the Eket local government area of Akwa Ibom State. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 2, 2022, the temple will feature a single-story design of approximately 18,850 square feet, along with an on-site meetinghouse. This temple will be the fourth in Nigeria, joining the operational Aba Nigeria Temple and the planned Benin City and Lagos Nigeria Temples. Nigeria is home to over 211,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 750 congregations.

name: El Paso Texas Temple
description: The El Paso Texas Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the tenth in Texas, which already has several others, including the Austin Texas Temple and the Dallas Texas Temple. El Paso, the sixth-largest city in Texas, is situated in the state's westernmost region. Texas has a significant Latter-day Saint community, with over 385,000 members across more than 750 congregations.

name: Elko Nevada Temple
description: The Elko Nevada Temple's open house and dedication dates have been confirmed. A media day is set for Wednesday, August 27, followed by tours for invited guests over two days. Public tours will be available from Saturday, August 30, to Saturday, September 13, excluding Sundays. Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles will dedicate the temple on Sunday, October 12, 2025, with the session broadcast to all local units. The temple, which will be approximately 10,000 square feet, is located on a 5.2-acre site adjacent to the Ruby View Golf Course.

name: Ephraim Utah Temple
description: The Ephraim Utah Temple is being constructed under the direction of President Russell M. Nelson, who led the groundbreaking ceremony on August 27, 2022. He has personal ties to the area, with family roots in Ephraim and Manti. The temple will be a two-story structure covering approximately 39,000 square feet, featuring four endowment rooms, three sealing rooms, and one baptismal font. The site, located at the intersection of 200 North and 400 East, was announced on October 22, 2021. This temple will be the twenty-seventh in Utah and the second in Sanpete County, following the Manti Utah Temple.

name: Fairbanks Alaska Temple
description: The Fairbanks Alaska Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony presided over by Elder Peter M. Johnson, First Counselor in the North America West Area Presidency, on September 27, 2025. This temple will be approximately 10,000 square feet and will include a meetinghouse and an ancillary building on a 7.59-acre site along Geist Road. The announcement for the temple's construction was made by President Russell M. Nelson during the October 2023 General Conference. The Fairbanks Alaska Temple will be the second temple in Alaska, following the Anchorage Alaska Temple, and will be the northernmost temple of the Church. As of the announcement, Alaska had around 35,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 80 congregations.

name: Fairview Texas Temple
description: The Fairview Texas Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. An official exterior rendering was made public on February 26, 2024. The temple will be situated on an 8.16-acre site along Stacy Road, just east of an existing meetinghouse at 651 East Stacy Road in Fairview, Texas, as announced on December 4, 2023. Originally proposed for Prosper, Texas, the temple will be the eighth in the state, joining seven others, including the Dallas Texas Temple and the Houston Texas Temple. Texas has a significant Latter-day Saint community, with over 370,000 members across 737 congregations.

name: Farmington New Mexico Temple
description: The Farmington New Mexico Temple will be the second temple in New Mexico, following the Albuquerque New Mexico Temple, which was dedicated in 2000. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans on April 4, 2021, during the 191st Annual General Conference. The temple will be located on a 6.62-acre site where the Farmington New Mexico Stake center currently stands, across from San Juan College. Groundbreaking took place on April 30, 2022, with Elder Anthony D. Perkins presiding. The temple is set to feature a single-story design of approximately 25,000 square feet, incorporating local Native American influences in its architecture and landscaping.

name: Feather River California Temple
description: The Feather River California Temple is the eighth temple established in California. Initially announced for Yuba City, President Russell M. Nelson revealed the construction plans during the 188th Semiannual General Conference. The temple, located at 1470 Butte House Road, was built on the site of the former Yuba City California Stake Center, which was demolished to make way for the new structure. A groundbreaking ceremony took place on June 18, 2020, and the temple was dedicated on October 8, 2023, by Elder Ulisses Soares. The temple features design elements inspired by the local almond blossom and incorporates materials that reflect the region's agricultural heritage.

name: Flagstaff Arizona Temple
description: The Flagstaff Arizona Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. An official rendering has not yet been made public. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the ninth in Arizona, which has about 450,000 Latter-day Saints across approximately 925 congregations.
