Flagstaff is situated around 150 miles north of Phoenix, surrounded by one of the largest ponderosa pine forests and near Humphreys Peak, the state's tallest mountain.

name: Fort Collins Colorado Temple
description: The Fort Collins Colorado Temple is located on Majestic Drive at the intersection of Timberline Road and Trilby Road in southeast Fort Collins. The property includes a small distribution center and a Church meetinghouse nearby. The temple grounds feature a serene entrance plaza with a water feature and landscaped planters, welcoming the public to enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. Announced by President Thomas S. Monson on April 2, 2011, this temple is the second in Colorado, serving Latter-day Saints in northern Colorado and southern Wyoming. The temple was dedicated by President Dieter F. Uchtdorf on October 16, 2016, after a three-week open house that attracted 105,000 visitors.

name: Fort Lauderdale Florida Temple
description: The Fort Lauderdale Florida Temple reached a significant milestone on October 24, 2012, with the placement of the angel Moroni statue on its spire. Construction began after the groundbreaking ceremony on June 18, 2011, led by Elder Walter F. González and Elder William R. Walker. This temple is the second in Florida, following the Orlando Florida Temple, and serves members in South Florida and the Bahamas. The site, located on a 30-acre parcel in Davie, was previously intended for a middle school before the Church acquired it. The temple features a Neoclassical design and includes a sun and palm tree motif in its interior.

name: Fort Worth Texas Temple
description: The Fort Worth Texas Temple's groundbreaking took place on October 28, 2023, with Elder Jose L. Alonso presiding. The temple is set to be built on a 9.37-acre site in Burleson, north of SW Hulen Street and Greenridge Drive. It will be a single-story structure covering approximately 30,000 square feet. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the October 2021 General Conference, this temple will be the sixth in Texas, joining the Dallas, Houston, Lubbock, San Antonio, and McAllen temples. Texas is home to over 360,000 Latter-day Saints, and missionary work in the state began in 1843.

name: Fortaleza Brazil Temple
address: Avenida Santos Dumont 7771 Bairro de Lourdes
description: The Fortaleza Brazil Temple is located in the scenic Dunas neighborhood, opposite FANOR, a higher education institution. This elegantly designed temple features a single domed tower and is situated on a gently sloping site that offers stunning city views. The complex includes an arrival center, missionary housing, a meetinghouse, and landscaped grounds. Announced by President Thomas S. Monson on October 3, 2009, the temple is the seventh in Brazil and the first in Ceará. Elder Ulisses Soares dedicated the Fortaleza Brazil Temple on June 2, 2019, emphasizing its role as a beacon of hope for the community.

name: Frankfurt Germany Temple
description: The Frankfurt Germany Temple is located in Friedrichsdorf, a historic city north of Frankfurt. It features a prominent spire visible from a nearby highway and includes several auxiliary buildings such as a residence for the temple president, missionary housing, a patron housing facility, and a stake center. The temple grounds are beautifully landscaped and open to the public. This temple was the fifth in Europe and the second in Germany, following the Freiberg Germany Temple, and faced significant opposition during its planning stages. Dedicated in 1987 by President Gordon B. Hinckley, the temple underwent renovations starting in 2015, which extended the construction timeline due to foundation issues.

name: Freetown Sierra Leone Temple
description: The Freetown Sierra Leone Temple, the first temple to be built in the country, had its groundbreaking ceremony on March 19, 2022. This temple will cover approximately 18,000 square feet and will include a two-story ancillary building on a 2.9-acre site in the Kossoh Town area of Freetown. Elder Hugo E. Martinez, president of the Africa West Area, led the ceremony, highlighting the positive impact the temple will have on local Church members. The temple's location on Jui Road will be visible to those traveling the Masiaka-Yonibana Highway. Currently, members in Sierra Leone must travel over 1,240 miles to access the nearest temple in Accra, Ghana.

name: Freiberg Germany Temple
description: The Freiberg Germany Temple is located in the historic city of Freiberg, in the northwest region. It is cherished by residents of various faiths, who often refer to it as "our" temple. The temple, originally named Freiberg DDR Temple, was the first built in a communist country and the third in Europe. After its dedication, it became a significant site, attracting nearly 90,000 visitors during its open house. The temple underwent extensive renovations and expansions, including the addition of an angel Moroni statue in 2001 and further enhancements completed in 2016, which doubled its size and improved its facilities.

name: Fresno California Temple
description: The Fresno California Temple is the fourth temple established in California and the first in the Central Valley. Its groundbreaking took place on March 20, 1999, alongside the Fukuoka Japan Temple, Melbourne Australia Temple, and Tuxtla Gutiérrez Mexico Temple. Elder John B. Dickson, who presided over the ceremony, highlighted California's significant role in the history of the Church. He emphasized the importance of families in God's plan and the temple's purpose in supporting eternal family connections. The temple features an exterior of White Sierra granite and includes a single spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Fukuoka Japan Temple
description: The Fukuoka Japan Temple is situated on the southern island of Kyushu, nestled into a hillside with the Fukuoka Municipal Zoo and Botanical Garden providing a verdant backdrop. The temple, constructed with white granite, occupies the upper level of a two-story structure, while the lower level, made of darker grey granite, contains a mission office, mission home, and parking facilities. This temple was the second in Japan, following the Tokyo Japan Temple, and its groundbreaking took place alongside ceremonies for three other temples on the same day. Originally, the site was remote, with an unpaved road leading to it, and a former restaurant served as a meetinghouse before the temple's construction. The Fukuoka Japan Temple was dedicated by President Gordon B. Hinckley, marking it as the first of four temples he dedicated during a significant tour of Asia and the Pacific.

name: Gilbert Arizona Temple
description: The Gilbert Arizona Temple was the site of a significant event on May 15, 2012, when a large crowd gathered to see the gold-leafed angel Moroni statue placed atop its central spire. Students from a nearby grade school, along with their families, participated in the occasion, creating a memorable moment by singing a beloved temple song. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on November 13, 2010, led by Elder Claudio R. M. Costa, with thousands attending to witness the initial construction steps. The temple's design, overseen by Gregory B. Lambright of Architekton, features a height of 195 feet, with a detailed exterior and landscaped grounds. The Gilbert Arizona Temple, the fourth in Arizona, was dedicated by President Thomas S. Monson, following a month-long public open house that attracted over 400,000 visitors.

name: Goiânia Brazil Temple
description: The Goiânia Brazil Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for the temple during the October 2023 General Conference. Goiânia, the capital of Goiás, has a population of approximately 2.9 million and will be the 21st temple in Brazil. Prior to this announcement, eight other temples were in the planning stages across various Brazilian cities. Additionally, there are ten dedicated temples in Brazil and two more under construction in Belo Horizonte and Salvador.

name: Grand Junction Colorado Temple
description: The Grand Junction Colorado Temple's open house and dedication dates have been set. A media day is scheduled for Monday, September 8, followed by tours for invited guests on September 9 and 10. Public tours will take place from September 11 to September 27, excluding Sundays. President Jeffrey R. Holland will dedicate the temple on October 19, 2025, with the session broadcast to all local congregations. This temple, which will be the third in Colorado, is located on a 6.94-acre site at the intersection of Horizon Drive and North 12th Street and features design elements inspired by the region's natural environment.

name: Grand Rapids Michigan Temple
description: The Grand Rapids Michigan Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on December 7, 2024, led by Elder Mathias Held of the North America Northeast Area Presidency. He offered a dedicatory prayer for the site, seeking divine protection and strength for the future temple. The official exterior rendering was unveiled on November 6, 2023, with an updated design released on November 11, 2024. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the October 2022 General Conference, this temple will be situated on a 10.5-acre site at 2400 Forest Hill Avenue in Grand Rapids, covering approximately 20,000 square feet. It will serve as the second temple in Michigan, following the Detroit Michigan Temple, which was dedicated in 1999.

name: Greenville South Carolina Temple
description: The Greenville South Carolina Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the second in South Carolina, following the Columbia South Carolina Temple, which has been operational since October 1999. South Carolina has approximately 46,000 Latter-day Saints across around 85 congregations.

name: Guadalajara Mexico Temple
description: The Guadalajara Mexico Temple is situated in Mexico's second-largest city, which has a population of four million. The temple district comprises seventeen stakes and nine districts, with plans for a new stake center to be built adjacent to the temple. Elder Eran A. Call, a member of the Seventy and president of the Mexico North Area, presided over the groundbreaking ceremony and reflected on his history with the Church in Guadalajara. He noted the growth from four branches to eight stakes since his time as a mission president nearly three decades ago. The temple, the 105th dedicated by the Church, features an exterior of Blanco Guardiano white marble from Torreón, Mexico, and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Guatemala City Guatemala Temple
description: The Guatemala City Guatemala Temple is situated on an elevated site in the Vista Hermosa neighborhood, overlooking Guatemala's capital. The temple complex includes a missionary training center and housing for patrons, with six prominent spires adorning the structure. It was the first temple established in Central America and the third in a Spanish-speaking nation, following the Santiago Chile Temple and the Mexico City Mexico Temple, both completed in 1983. The temple's dedication occurred during a period of civil unrest in Guatemala, prompting President Gordon B. Hinckley to pray for peace in his dedicatory prayer. The temple features a natural white Guatemalan marble exterior and an angel Moroni statue atop its spires.

name: Guayaquil Ecuador Temple
description: The Guayaquil Ecuador Temple is the first temple established in Ecuador. It experienced a lengthy delay of over 14 years from its announcement to the groundbreaking, the longest for any temple. Located in a serene hillside area of northern Guayaquil, it is regarded as one of the most beautiful buildings in the country. During the construction, President Gordon B. Hinckley shared his experience of selecting the site, which he felt was divinely inspired. After the public open house, which saw significant attendance, the temple opened for service, welcoming members from the Otavalo region, known for their distinctive traditional attire.

name: Halifax Nova Scotia Temple
description: The Halifax Nova Scotia Temple was dedicated on the same day as the Regina Saskatchewan Temple, marking a historic occasion with two dedications occurring simultaneously. Due to a mechanical issue with President Gordon B. Hinckley's flight, Elder Boyd K. Packer dedicated the Regina temple, while President Hinckley presided over the Halifax dedication. Local members demonstrated their commitment by traveling long distances, with some driving up to eight hours to attend. The temple's impact extended beyond members, touching the hearts of non-members as well. The dedication process highlighted the community's dedication to detail and perfection, exemplified by members' willingness to address last-minute issues before the ceremony.

name: Hamburg Germany Temple
description: The Hamburg Germany Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the April 2023 General Conference. This temple will be the third House of the Lord in Germany, following the Frankfurt Germany Temple and the Freiberg Germany Temple. Hamburg is situated approximately 175 miles northwest of Berlin. It will be the first temple constructed in Germany since reunification, serving a community of nearly 40,000 Latter-day Saints across about 150 congregations.

name: Hamilton New Zealand Temple
description: The Hamilton New Zealand Temple is located on a prominent hill in the rural outskirts of Hamilton, sharing 86 acres with the now-closed Church College of New Zealand. It was the first temple established in the Southern Hemisphere and the second in Polynesia, following the Laie Hawaii Temple. Originally named the New Zealand Temple, it features a unique design with 75 rooms across three levels, including a Celestial Room adorned with murals. The temple was dedicated in April 1958, with President David O. McKay presiding over the ceremonies. After extensive renovations beginning in 2018, the temple was rededicated on October 16, 2022, by Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf.

name: Harare Zimbabwe Temple
description: The Harare Zimbabwe Temple will open for public tours from January 22 to February 7, 2026. A media day is scheduled for January 19, followed by two days of tours for invited guests. Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles will dedicate the temple on March 1, 2026, with the session broadcast to local congregations. The groundbreaking took place on December 12, 2020, presided over by Elder Edward Dube, with the attendance of Zimbabwe's President Emmerson Mnangagwa. This temple, the first in Zimbabwe and the eighth in Africa, will serve the growing Church membership in the region, which currently numbers 26,000 members across six stakes and two districts.

name: Harrisburg Pennsylvania Temple
description: The Harrisburg Pennsylvania Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. On October 30, 2023, the temple's location was confirmed as a 5.36-acre site at 605 Rutherford Road in Harrisburg. An exterior rendering was made public on December 16, 2024, showcasing a single-story structure of approximately 20,000 square feet. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the April 2023 General Conference, marking it as the third temple for Pennsylvania. Harrisburg, the state capital, is located in the Susquehanna Valley, a region significant to the early history of the Church.

name: Hartford Connecticut Temple
description: The Hartford Connecticut Temple is located on an 11-acre site at the intersection of Farmington Avenue and Melrose Drive in Farmington, Connecticut, the birthplace of Wilford Woodruff, the fourth president of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. This temple, clad in white granite, features an entrance portico with Ionic columns and a steeple that reaches 115 feet. It was the first temple constructed in Connecticut and the second in New England, following the Boston Massachusetts Temple. President Thomas S. Monson announced its construction during the 180th Semiannual General Conference, with the groundbreaking ceremony taking place on August 17, 2013. The temple was dedicated on November 20, 2016, by President Henry B. Eyring, who emphasized its significance as a sacred space for worship and community.

name: Heber Valley Utah Temple
description: The Heber Valley Utah Temple is being constructed under the direction of President Russell M. Nelson, leader of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The groundbreaking took place on October 8, 2022, for this 88,000-square-foot temple, which will occupy a 17.9-acre site southeast of 1400 East Center Street in Heber City, Utah. President Nelson announced the temple during the October 2021 General Conference. The official exterior rendering was revealed on September 19, 2022. This temple will be the 28th in Utah and the first in Wasatch County.

name: Helena Montana Temple
description: The Helena Montana Temple is the second temple established in Montana, following the Billings Montana Temple, which was completed in 1999. It is notable for being the first temple constructed using modular methods. The temple was announced on April 4, 2021, by President Russell M. Nelson during the 191st Annual General Conference, serving over 50,000 Latter-day Saints in the central region of Montana. The temple, located on a 4.8-acre site at 1230 Otter Road, was dedicated on June 18, 2023, by Elder Gary E. Stevenson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. Its design incorporates local natural elements and Native American geometric patterns, with a focus on creating a harmonious connection to the surrounding landscape.

name: Helsinki Finland Temple
description: The Helsinki Finland Temple is situated on a rocky hillside near the highway to Turku, in the suburb of Espoo, about 7 miles northwest of downtown Helsinki. The site also includes a patron housing facility for members of the extensive temple district. The temple grounds are beautifully landscaped and open to visitors throughout the year. It was the tenth temple established in Europe and the third in the Nordic region, following the Stockholm Sweden Temple and the Copenhagen Denmark Temple. Dedicated on January 27, 2008, by President Gordon B. Hinckley, the temple features an exterior of Olympia white granite from Italy and brown granite from Finland, along with a distinctive spire topped by a gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Hermosillo Sonora Mexico Temple
address: General Pedro Garcia Conde No 303 Esquina Con Juan José Ríos Colonia Pitic
description: The Hermosillo Sonora Mexico Temple is situated in the Pitic neighborhood on the eastern side of Hermosillo, directly north of the Hermosillo Mexico Pitic Stake center. It faces Avenida Pedro García Conde, a well-landscaped boulevard adorned with flowers, trees, benches, and red pavers. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on December 5, 1998, with approximately 1,200 attendees, presided over by Elder Eran A. Call. The temple was dedicated by President Gordon B. Hinckley on February 27, 2000, in four sessions, with 5,898 members present. This temple, the 72nd dedicated by the Church, features a white marble veneer exterior and a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Hong Kong China Temple
description: The Hong Kong China Temple is situated in Kowloon Tong, a peaceful residential area on the Kowloon Peninsula of Hong Kong. The temple's design reflects colonial architecture, featuring art glass columns, decorative exterior walls, and an attractive water feature. It was the first temple established in China and the second in mainland Asia, following the Seoul Korea Temple in 1985. The temple is unique in that it opens quarterly on Sundays to serve members, particularly Filipino domestic workers. Originally dedicated in 1996, the temple underwent significant renovations from 2019 to 2022, which included updates to its exterior and interior while maintaining its original design elements.

name: Honolulu Hawaii Temple
description: The Honolulu Hawaii Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the construction plans during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the fourth in Hawaii, joining the Laie Hawaii Temple, Kahului Hawaii Temple, and Kona Hawaii Temple. Honolulu, located on the island of Oahu, is the capital and most populous city of Hawaii. At the time of the announcement, there were about 75,000 Latter-day Saints organized into 145 congregations across the state.

name: Houston Texas South Temple
description: The Houston Texas South Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the construction plans during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the second in the Houston area and the ninth in Texas. The existing Houston Texas Temple was dedicated in August 2000 and rededicated in April 2018 after Hurricane Harvey. With the addition of the Houston Texas South Temple, Houston will become the twelfth city globally to have more than one temple.

name: Houston Texas Temple
description: The Houston Texas Temple is the second temple established in Texas, following the Dallas Texas Temple, which was dedicated in 1984. On August 26, 2017, Hurricane Harvey caused severe flooding that breached the temple, leading to extensive damage, including a flooded baptistry and waist-deep water in parts of the basement. The temple was closed for repairs and was rededicated in a private ceremony on April 22, 2018. It serves members from twenty-eight stakes, with the nearest temple prior to its dedication located five hours away in Dallas. The temple features an exterior of Luna pearl granite and includes a single attached end spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Huancayo Peru Temple
description: The Huancayo Peru Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the October 2023 General Conference. This temple will be the first in the Junín Region and the ninth in Peru. Huancayo, the capital of Junín, is situated in the Peruvian highlands approximately 190 miles east of Lima. The name Huancayo translates to "place of the rock" in Quechua, and the first missionaries arrived in Peru in 1956.

name: Huehuetenango Guatemala Temple
description: The Huehuetenango Guatemala Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The official exterior rendering was made public on May 13, 2024. The temple's location was revealed on March 20, 2023, situated on a long, narrow parcel across from the Barrio Sión meetinghouse. It will feature a single-story structure of about 10,787 square feet. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 2, 2022, this temple will be the fifth in Guatemala, joining the existing Cobán, Guatemala City, Miraflores, and Quetzeltenango temples.

name: Huntsville Alabama Temple
address: Gillespie Road and Browns Ferry Road
description: The Huntsville Alabama Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple's location was revealed on January 21, 2025, as a 21-acre site southeast of Gillespie Road and Browns Ferry Road in Madison, Alabama. An official exterior rendering was made public on April 22, 2025. The temple will be a single-story structure, approximately 30,000 square feet in size. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024, this temple will be the second in Alabama, complementing the Birmingham Alabama Temple.

name: Idaho Falls Idaho Temple
description: The Idaho Falls Idaho Temple is prominently located along the Snake River, near the waterfall that inspired the city's name. Adjacent to the temple, visitors can explore a public center featuring films, displays, and a replica of Thorvaldsen's Christus statue. This temple, the first in Idaho, was dedicated by President George Albert Smith and was designed with a central spire, marking a return to this architectural feature. Originally named the Idaho Falls Temple, it underwent significant renovations, including the addition of a waterfall feature in 2011 and a comprehensive update completed in 2017. The temple is known for its hand-painted murals and is one of seven temples where patrons progress through multiple ordinance rooms before reaching the Celestial Room.

name: Iloilo Philippines Temple
description: The Iloilo Philippines Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the April 2023 General Conference, marking it as the 12th temple for the Philippines. Iloilo City serves as the capital of Iloilo province, located approximately 400 miles south of Manila. Since the Church began missionary work in the Philippines in 1961, membership has grown rapidly, with over 850,000 Latter-day Saints in nearly 1,275 congregations at the time of the announcement. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public.

name: Indianapolis Indiana Temple
description: The Indianapolis Indiana Temple is located at the intersection of West 116th Street and Spring Mill Road in Carmel, Indiana, a suburb of Indianapolis. It is the first temple established in Indiana, with its groundbreaking ceremony held on September 29, 2012, presided over by Elder Donald L. Hallstrom. The temple features a design inspired by notable Indianapolis monuments and is constructed from structural steel and concrete, clad in Aero Cream limestone from Turkey. The interior includes various marble finishes and decorative elements reflecting the tulip poplar, Indiana's state tree. The temple shares its site with a meetinghouse, and both facilities will operate on noncompeting schedules.

name: Iquitos Peru Temple
address: Calle San Marcos 117?137 San Juan Bautista
description: The Iquitos Peru Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple will be situated on a 1.75-acre site at Calle San Marcos 117–137 in the San Juan Bautista District of Iquitos, where the Secoya Ward meetinghouse is located. Announced on April 2, 2023, by President Russell M. Nelson during the April General Conference, this temple will cover approximately 20,000 square feet and will be the seventh temple in Peru. Iquitos, one of the largest cities in the country, is located in Northeast Peru along the Amazon River. Peru has around 630,000 Latter-day Saints across nearly 780 congregations, with the first missionaries arriving in 1956.

name: Jacksonville Florida Temple
description: The Jacksonville Florida Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date announced yet. The temple's location was revealed on February 20, 2024, as a 6.6-acre site at 3323 Loretto Road in Jacksonville. An exterior rendering was made public on December 16, 2024, showcasing a single-story building of about 29,000 square feet. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction of the Jacksonville Florida Temple during the October 2022 General Conference, marking it as the fifth temple in Florida. The state is home to over 160,000 Latter-day Saints and more than 280 congregations.

name: Jakarta Indonesia Temple
address: Synthesis Square Jalan Gatot Subroto No. 177A Tebet District South Jakarta City
description: The Jakarta Indonesia Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date announced yet. The temple will be situated on a 1.33-acre site at Synthesis Square, Jalan Gatot Subroto, No. 177a in the Tebet District of South Jakarta. It is designed to be a four-story structure covering approximately 40,350 square feet. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the April 2023 General Conference, marking it as the first temple in Indonesia. As of the announcement, there were over 7,500 Latter-day Saints in nearly 25 congregations across the country.

name: Johannesburg South Africa Temple
description: The Johannesburg South Africa Temple stands prominently on Parktown Ridge, marked by its six white-tipped spires that are visible from the M1 highway north of Johannesburg's city center. Situated on Jubilee Road, the temple's grounds also include family history, employment, and distribution services offices, along with a secure underground parking facility for visitors. As the first temple established in Africa, its announcement followed the 1978 revelation by President Spencer W. Kimball, which allowed all worthy men to receive priesthood and temple blessings. The temple's nearly two-week open house drew over 19,000 visitors, including local leaders and government officials, while approximately 3,500 of the 12,000 members in the temple district attended its dedication. The Johannesburg South Africa Temple is the 36th temple of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and features a masonry exterior with a gray slate roof and six detached spires topped by an angel Moroni statue.

name: Jordan River Utah Temple
description: The Jordan River Utah Temple is located in the southern Salt Lake Valley, two miles west of I-15. Named after the nearby Jordan River, the temple features a prominent water fountain surrounded by vibrant flowers and shrubs at its entrance. It was the seventh temple constructed in Utah and the second in the Salt Lake Valley, following the Salt Lake Temple. Dedicated by President Marion G. Romney, it is notable for having an angel Moroni statue holding the gold plates and for being one of four temples with six instruction rooms. The temple underwent extensive renovations starting on February 15, 2016, which included updates to its interior and exterior, as well as improvements to its mechanical systems and landscaping.

name: João Pessoa Brazil Temple
address: Rua Paulino Pinto and Avenida Ministro José Américo de Almeida Cabo Branco
description: The João Pessoa Brazil Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The official exterior rendering was made public on July 8, 2024. The temple will be situated on a 3.9-acre site at the intersection of Rua Paulino Pinto and Avenida Ministro José Américo de Almeida in the Cabo Branco neighborhood. It is designed to be approximately 18,850 square feet. This temple will be the 22nd in Brazil, a country with nearly 1.5 million members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

name: Juchitán de Zaragoza Mexico Temple
description: The Juchitán de Zaragoza Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the 26th house of the Lord in Mexico, which currently has several dedicated temples, including the Ciudad Juárez Mexico Temple and the Mexico City Mexico Temple. Additionally, there are multiple temples either under construction or in planning stages across the country. Mexico is home to over 1.5 million Latter-day Saints organized into nearly 1,900 congregations, with missionary efforts beginning in 1875.

name: Kahului Hawaii Temple
description: The Kahului Hawaii Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the October 2023 General Conference, marking it as the first temple to be constructed in Maui. At the time of the announcement, Hawaii had two existing temples: the Kona Hawaii Temple, dedicated in 2000 and undergoing renovation, and the Laie Hawaii Temple, dedicated in 1919. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has a significant presence in Hawaii, with nearly 75,000 members across 145 congregations, including over 4,500 on Maui. The Church has also provided extensive support for relief efforts following the devastating wildfire in Lahaina in August.

name: Kampala Uganda Temple
description: The Kampala Uganda Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the first in Uganda, situated in east-central Africa, where over 22,000 Latter-day Saints gather in approximately 40 congregations. Kampala, the capital city, is located on the East African Plateau. The first official congregation in Uganda was established in the early 1990s, following earlier meetings held by expatriate Latter-day Saints in the 1960s.

name: Kananga Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple
photoCaption: Kananga Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple
description: The Kananga Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date yet set. The official site for the temple, announced on April 15, 2024, is a 1.6-acre plot at Avenue Ilunga and N1 in Kananga. The design includes a one-story temple of about 11,000 square feet, along with facilities for patrons and arrivals. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for this temple during the October 2021 General Conference, marking it as the third temple in the country, alongside the Kinshasa and Lubumbashi temples. The Democratic Republic of the Congo has over 68,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 200 congregations.

name: Kansas City Missouri Temple
description: The Kansas City Missouri Temple features distinctive double towers that rise prominently over I-435 in Kansas City's Northland, near the Liberty Jail Historic Site in Liberty, Missouri. A meetinghouse was built alongside the temple, and the grounds are adorned with trees and colorful flowers, welcoming public visitors. This temple is the second in Missouri, following the St. Louis Missouri Temple, with its site announced on October 12, 2008. The temple was dedicated in three sessions by President Thomas S. Monson on May 6, 2012, after a public open house that attracted nearly 91,000 visitors. The Kansas City Missouri Temple won the PCI Design Award for Best Religious Structure in 2012 and is recognized as the 137th dedicated temple in operation.

name: Kaohsiung Taiwan Temple
address: Dachang Road and Dehua Street Niaosong District
description: The Kaohsiung Taiwan Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on Saturday, November 25, 2023, presided over by Elder Benjamin M. Z. Tai, president of the Asia Area. Around 500 Church members and local officials, including the mayor of Niaosong District, attended the event, with many others joining via broadcast. This temple, the second in Taiwan, will be built on a 1.26-acre site near the Kaohsiung Taiwan North Stake center and will cover approximately 10,900 square feet. The temple's location was announced on November 28, 2022, and its official rendering was released on December 19, 2022. The first temple in Taiwan, the Taipei Taiwan Temple, was dedicated in 1984, and there are over 61,000 Latter-day Saints in the country.

name: Kinshasa Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple
address: 51 Avenue de L?OUA Quartier Basoko GB Commune de Ngaliema
photoCaption: Kinshasa Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple
description: The Kinshasa Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple is located adjacent to the Kinshasa Stake center on land designated for a temple for several years. The temple grounds feature a guardhouse and a driveway lined with royal palm trees, along with an institute and seminary building, and a patron housing facility. This temple is the first in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the fourth in Africa. Groundbreaking took place on February 12, 2016, with Elder Neil L. Andersen presiding, and the temple was dedicated on April 14, 2019, by Elder Dale G. Renlund. The temple serves as a significant blessing for local Church members, who previously faced long travel distances to reach the nearest temple in Johannesburg, South Africa.

name: Kirtland Temple
description: The Kirtland Temple is located on a bluff in northeastern Ohio, approximately 25 miles east of Cleveland, overlooking the Chagrin Valley. This historic site is open for free tours to individuals of all faiths and is part of the restored Historic Kirtland, which highlights the early Kirtland Saints' history. As the first temple built in this dispensation, it was dedicated on April 3, 1836, during which significant spiritual manifestations occurred. The temple served various purposes after the Saints left Kirtland, including functioning as a public school. In 1880, the Community of Christ regained ownership and restored the temple, which was later transferred to The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on March 5, 2024, with plans for public tours to resume on March 25, 2024.

name: Knoxville Tennessee Temple
description: The Knoxville Tennessee Temple will be built on a 4.99-acre site at 13001 Kingston Pike in Farragut, Tennessee. Groundbreaking services were led by Elder Shayne M. Bowen on January 27, 2024. The temple will feature a single-story structure of approximately 30,000 square feet. The location was announced on October 31, 2022, and the official rendering was released on December 19, 2022. This temple will be the third in Tennessee, following the Memphis Tennessee Temple and the Nashville Tennessee Temple, both dedicated in 2000.

name: Kona Hawaii Temple
description: The Kona Hawaii Temple is undergoing a significant renovation that began in October 2023, which will expand its size from 9,500 to approximately 12,000 square feet and update its exterior. During this period, members of the temple district are invited to attend the Laie Hawaii Temple. Located in Kailua-Kona on the Big Island, the temple is a notable landmark along Queen Ka'ahumanu Highway, characterized by its bright white marble and surrounding palm trees. It was the sixth temple established in Polynesia and the second in Hawaii, following the Laie Hawaii Temple, which was dedicated in 1919. The groundbreaking for the Kona Hawaii Temple coincided with that of the Nashville Tennessee Temple and Oaxaca Mexico Temple.

name: Kumasi Ghana Temple
description: The Kumasi Ghana Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony presided over by Elder Isaac K. Morrison, Second Counselor in the Africa West Area Presidency, on Saturday, October 18, 2025. The temple will be located on a 2.08-acre site at Y11 Suntreso Road, sharing the area with the Bantama meetinghouse. Plans include a two-story structure of approximately 22,750 square feet, along with an arrival center. The announcement for the temple's construction was made by President Russell M. Nelson during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021. This temple will be the second in Ghana, following the Accra Ghana Temple, which was dedicated in 2004.

name: Kyiv Ukraine Temple
description: The Kyiv Ukraine Temple is the first temple established in Ukraine and the former Soviet Union, and it is the eleventh temple in Europe. Elder Boyd K. Packer offered a prayer of dedication for Ukraine on September 12, 1991. President Thomas S. Monson dedicated the temple on August 29, 2010, marking a significant moment for the Church in Eastern Europe. The temple received an award for the best religious building in Ukraine in 2010, presented by the Ministry of Regional Development. Groundbreaking occurred on June 23, 2007, and the temple features a single spire topped with a statue of Moroni.

name: La Paz Bolivia Temple
address: Avenida Los Sauces and Calle 8 de Calacoto Calacoto
description: The La Paz Bolivia Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The official exterior rendering was made public on January 22, 2024. The temple will be situated on a 3.8-acre site near Avenida Los Sauces and Calle 8 de Calacoto in the Calacoto neighborhood of La Paz. It is designed to be approximately 18,850 square feet. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the October 2021 General Conference, this temple will be the third in Bolivia, serving members in La Paz and El Alto.

name: Lagos Nigeria Temple
address: Rumens Road and Bourdillon Road Ikoyi
description: The Lagos Nigeria Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony on May 10, 2025, presided over by Elder Alfred Kyungu, Africa West Area President. This temple will be built on a 2.7-acre site at the intersection of Rumens Road and Bourdillon Road in the Ikoyi neighborhood of Lagos. It will feature a single-level structure of approximately 19,800 square feet, along with an arrival center and patron housing. The announcement of the temple was made by President Russell M. Nelson during the 188th Semiannual General Conference, marking it as Nigeria's second temple after the Aba Nigeria Temple, which was dedicated in 2005. The Lagos Nigeria Temple will serve the growing community of 174,000 Latter-day Saints in Nigeria.

name: Laie Hawaii Temple
description: The Laie Hawaii Temple is located on a gently rising hill surrounded by vibrant Hawaiian vegetation, just half a mile from the Pacific Ocean on Oahu's north shore. Accessed via Hale Laa Boulevard from Kamehameha Highway, the temple grounds include a public visitors' center and are near Brigham Young University–Hawaii and the Polynesian Cultural Center. Originally named the Hawaii Temple, it was the first temple built in the Pacific islands and outside the continental United States. The temple features hand-painted murals in its progressive-style ordinance rooms and has undergone significant renovations since its dedication on Thanksgiving Day in 1919. The Laie Hawaii Temple is constructed from concrete made with crushed rock and coral, showcasing unique architectural elements, including carved friezes that represent four dispensations of time.

name: Laoag Philippines Temple
description: The Laoag Philippines Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the October 2023 General Conference. Once completed, it will be the 13th temple in the Philippines, which has over 850,000 Latter-day Saints across approximately 1,275 congregations. The existing 12 temples are located in Alabang, Bacolod, Cagayan de Oro, Cebu City, Davao, Iloilo, Manila, Naga, Santiago, Tacloban, Tuguegarao, and Urdaneta. The Church has experienced rapid growth in the Philippines since the start of missionary work in 1961.

name: Las Vegas Nevada Temple
description: The Las Vegas Nevada Temple serves as a spiritual landmark on the eastern edge of Las Vegas, away from the bustling Strip. Its six prominent spires reflect the nearby Sunrise Mountain's striking red peaks, while the temple grounds are beautifully landscaped with flowers and trees. Open to visitors, the temple's pathways offer a serene atmosphere. As the first temple in Nevada, it features an angel Moroni statue facing east, symbolizing the Second Coming of Jesus Christ. The temple was dedicated in December 2000 after a successful fundraising effort by local members, and it includes a family history center that opened in 2012.

name: Layton Utah Temple
description: The Layton Utah Temple is the twenty-second temple constructed in Utah and the second in Davis County, following the Bountiful Utah Temple. The groundbreaking took place on May 23, 2020, a week earlier than planned, due to COVID-19 restrictions. President Russell M. Nelson announced the temple's construction during the 188th Annual General Conference. The temple was dedicated on June 16, 2024, by Elder David A. Bednar, with a public open house held from April 19 to June 1, 2024. The design incorporates elements from the area's agricultural heritage and Art Nouveau style, featuring motifs of fruit trees and flowers throughout its architecture and landscaping.

name: Lehi Utah Temple
description: The Lehi Utah Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The official rendering, showcasing a multi-level design with a central spire, was made public on February 24, 2025. The temple will be located on a 22.48-acre site northwest of the intersection of 3950 North and Center Street in Lehi, as announced on April 22, 2024. Plans include a temple of approximately 85,000 square feet and a new meetinghouse. This temple will be the 30th in Utah, situated in northern Utah County, an area known for its technology sector, Silicon Slopes.

name: Lethbridge Alberta Temple
description: The Lethbridge Alberta Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony presided over by Elder Randall K. Bennett, the North America Central Area President, on April 26, 2025. This temple will be built on a nine-acre site at the intersection of Whoop Up Drive West and Mauretania Road West. The design includes a multistory structure of approximately 45,000 square feet, along with a distribution center. The official exterior rendering was made public on April 29, 2024, following the announcement of the temple's construction by President Russell M. Nelson during the April 2023 General Conference. This temple will be the tenth in Canada, serving a community of around 100,000 residents in Lethbridge.

name: Lima Peru Los Olivos Temple
address: Av. Eloy Espinoza 680 Urb. Palao San Martin de Porres
description: The Lima Peru Los Olivos Temple is the fourth temple established in Peru and the third in Lima, alongside the Lima Peru Temple, which was dedicated in 1986. This temple is notable for being the first outside the United States to be located in the same metropolitan area as another operating temple. The announcement for its construction occurred on April 3, 2016, during the General Conference, marking the 30th anniversary of the Lima Peru Temple. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on June 8, 2019, and the temple was dedicated on January 14, 2024. The temple features a white granite exterior, art deco design elements, and beautifully landscaped gardens with olive trees and the national flower of Peru, the cantua.

name: Lima Peru Temple
address: Av. Javier Prado Este 6420 Urb. Santa Patricia La Molina
description: The Lima Peru Temple, located in the affluent La Molina district of eastern Lima, features six prominent spires and stands above the busy Avenida Javier Prado. Its beautifully landscaped grounds provide a serene environment for visitors and those seeking solace. The temple complex includes an accommodation center with living quarters, a cafeteria, and a family history center, as well as the nearby Peru Missionary Training Center. Dedicated by President Gordon B. Hinckley, the Lima Peru Temple was the first temple in Peru and the third in South America, following the São Paulo Brazil Temple and the Santiago Chile Temple. Since its dedication, attendance has significantly increased, with renovations in 2013 introducing a new north-facing angel Moroni atop the main spire.

name: Lindon Utah Temple
description: The Lindon Utah Temple's groundbreaking took place on April 23, 2022, in Lindon, Utah. Elder Kevin W. Pearson, president of the Utah Area, led the event, which included a dedicatory prayer for the temple's construction to benefit the community. The temple will be a three-story structure, approximately 81,000 square feet, featuring double spires and a granite exterior. It will include various ordinance spaces, a baptistry, and landscaping designed to reflect the area's agricultural heritage. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 4, 2020, this temple will be the twenty-fifth in Utah and the seventh in Utah County.

name: Lisbon Portugal Temple
address: Avenida Dom João II Nº75 Parque Das Nações
description: The Lisbon Portugal Temple is located in the northeastern part of the city, near the Moscavide station of the Lisbon Metro, close to the parish of Parque das Nações. This area was transformed for the 1998 Lisbon World Exposition and has since become a vibrant center for leisure and commerce along the Tagus River. The temple is the first in Portugal and the fourteenth in Europe. Groundbreaking took place on December 5, 2015, and the temple was dedicated by Elder Neil L. Andersen on September 15, 2019. Its design incorporates Portuguese Moleanos limestone and features colors and patterns inspired by traditional azulejo tiles, reflecting the region's cultural heritage.

name: Liverpool Australia Temple
description: The Liverpool Australia Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the seventh in Australia and the second in Greater Sydney. At the time of the announcement, several temples were operational, including the Adelaide, Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth, and Sydney Australia Temples, while the Brisbane Australia South Temple was in planning. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has a significant presence in Australia, with nearly 160,000 members in around 300 congregations.

name: Logan Utah Temple
description: The Logan Utah Temple is situated on an elevated terrace, making it visible across northern Utah's Cache Valley. The temple occupies a full city block and includes beautiful gardens and an oval reflecting pool to the east, along with a large grassy hill to the west. It was the second temple constructed in Utah Territory and the first to feature progressive-style ordinance rooms designed for live presentations of the endowment ceremony. Dedicated by President John Taylor, the temple originally showcased hand-painted murals in its ordinance rooms, though these were removed during a significant interior reconstruction in the 1970s. The temple grounds were renovated in 2009, introducing a new reflecting pool and heated sidewalks to accommodate the area's snowfall.

name: London England Temple
description: The London England Temple is situated on a picturesque estate in the southern English countryside, approximately 25 miles south of London and near Gatwick Airport. The site includes several buildings, notably the Manor House, an Elizabethan-style mansion that has served various functions for the Church, including housing for patrons and a missionary training center. The temple is surrounded by 10 acres of beautifully landscaped grounds, featuring Eden Brook and notable oak trees, including the "David O. McKay Oak." As the first temple built in the United Kingdom and the second in Europe, it was dedicated in six sessions in September 1958, attended by many Church leaders. The temple underwent significant renovations from 1990 to 1992 and celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2008 with the addition of an angel Moroni statue to its spire.

name: Londrina Brazil Temple
address: Avenida Harry Prochet Jardim São Jorge
description: The Londrina Brazil Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on Saturday, August 17, with Elder Ciro Schmeil, First Counselor in the Brazil Area Presidency, presiding. He offered a dedicatory prayer, expressing hope that all individuals in the temple district would feel divine love and desire to draw closer through temple covenants. The temple will be a single-story structure covering approximately 32,000 square feet, located on Avenida Harry Prochet in the Jardim São Jorge neighborhood of Londrina. The temple was announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the October 2022 General Conference, and its exterior rendering was released on January 8, 2024. This temple will be the second in Paraná, joining the existing temple in Curitiba, and is part of a broader expansion of Latter-day Saint temples in Brazil.

name: Lone Mountain Nevada Temple
description: The Lone Mountain Nevada Temple is set to be built in Northwest Las Vegas, with groundbreaking taking place on September 25, 2025, presided over by Elder Michael A. Dunn. The temple will be a three-story structure located on a 20-acre site near Lone Mountain. The official exterior rendering was made public on February 26, 2024. This temple will be the fourth in Nevada, joining the Las Vegas Nevada Temple, dedicated in 1989, the Reno Nevada Temple, dedicated in 2000, and the Elko Nevada Temple, which is currently under construction. With nearly 6% of Nevada's population being members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, the Lone Mountain Nevada Temple will be the ninth temple in a city that already has another operating temple.

name: Los Angeles California Temple
description: The Los Angeles California Temple, standing 257 feet tall, is prominently located along Santa Monica Boulevard in Westwood. Its expansive grounds feature a variety of trees, including Canary Island Pines, palm trees, Bird of Paradise trees, olive trees, and Chinese Ginkgo trees, complemented by fountains and a reflection pool. The temple, which was the first built in California, includes a priesthood assembly room and a statue of the angel Moroni, both of which were added after its initial design. Construction began after purchasing the land from Harold Lloyd Motion Picture Company on March 23, 1937, but was delayed due to World War II. The temple underwent several renovations over the years, including a significant seismic overhaul completed in July 2006, coinciding with its 50th anniversary.

name: Louisville Kentucky Temple
description: The Louisville Kentucky Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place alongside those for the Adelaide Australia Temple and Veracruz Mexico Temple. Elder John K. Carmack, a member of the Seventy and president of the North America East Area, led the services and emphasized the significance of temples for eternal families. He noted Joseph Smith's deep interest in temple work during his later years, highlighting the construction of the Kirtland Temple and efforts on two Missouri temples and the Nauvoo Temple. Elder Carmack remarked on the impact of our actions in this life on the next, referencing Hugh Nibley's view that ordinances bring order from chaos. The temple, the 76th dedicated by the Church, features an exterior of Imperial Danby White marble from Vermont and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Luanda Angola Temple
description: The Luanda Angola Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the October 2023 General Conference. This temple will be the first in Angola, a Portuguese-speaking country in southwestern Africa. Luanda, the capital and largest city, has an estimated population of 9.3 million. As of the announcement, there were nearly 5,000 Latter-day Saints in Angola, organized into about 20 congregations since the first was established in 1996.

name: Lubbock Texas Temple
description: The Lubbock Texas Temple is located behind the Lubbock Texas Stake Center on Frankford Avenue in Southwest Lubbock. The temple features symbolic stained glass windows and intricately etched granite walls. Visitors can explore the temple's exterior and attend services at the nearby meetinghouse. It was the third temple established in Texas, following the Dallas Texas Temple in 1984 and the Houston Texas Temple in 2000. The groundbreaking for the Lubbock Texas Temple occurred simultaneously with the Monterrey Mexico Temple, and it is the 109th temple dedicated in operation, showcasing Empress white and majestic gray granite from China and a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Lubumbashi Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple
photoCaption: © 2022, Intellectual Reserve, Inc. Concept site plan
description: The Lubumbashi Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple is set to be constructed on Av. Kashobwe, opposite the École Privée Belge de Lubumbashi and near Lac Kipopo. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on August 20, 2022, led by Elder Matthew L. Carpenter, president of the Africa Central Area. This temple will be the second in the country, following the Kinshasa Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple, which was dedicated in 2019. The single-story temple will cover approximately 16,700 square feet and feature a steeple at the entrance, along with additional facilities for patrons, missionaries, and support services. The establishment of this temple will significantly benefit the nearly 63,000 Church members in the region, who currently travel nearly 1,500 miles to the Kinshasa temple.

name: Maceió Brazil Temple
address: Av. Durval de Góes Monteiro Jardim Petropolis
description: The Maceió Brazil Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The official exterior rendering was made public on May 13, 2024, following the announcement of its location on March 6, 2023. This 19,000-square-foot temple will be situated on Avenida Durval de Góes Monteiro in the Jardim Petropolis neighborhood of Maceió. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the April 2022 General Conference. The Maceió Brazil Temple will be the 15th temple in Brazil, joining others in cities such as Campinas, Curitiba, and São Paulo.

name: Madrid Spain Temple
description: The Madrid Spain Temple is the first temple constructed in Spain and the seventh in Europe. It is part of a complex that includes a stake center and patron housing, often called the "Temple Square of Madrid." Missionary efforts in Spain began following the passage of a religious liberty law in 1967, which allowed the Church to gain official recognition. Among the first missionaries sent to Spain was Clark Hinckley, the son of President Gordon B. Hinckley. The temple features an exterior of Italian Carrara Marble and includes a single central spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Managua Nicaragua Temple
description: The Managua Nicaragua Temple is set to be the first temple in Nicaragua and the seventh in Central America. Elder Taylor G. Godoy, the first counselor in the Central America Area presidency, led the groundbreaking ceremony on November 26, 2022. The event included speakers from the youth and pioneering members, a youth choir, and remarks from Elder Godoy, who emphasized the importance of strengthening testimonies of Jesus Christ. The temple will occupy an 8.9-acre site in southern Managua and will be a single-level structure of approximately 25,000 square feet. The official announcement of the temple was made by President Russell M. Nelson during the April 2018 General Conference, fulfilling a promise made to Nicaraguan Saints six years prior.

name: Manaus Brazil Temple
description: The Manaus Brazil Temple is situated on the western edge of Manaus, alongside the Rio Negro. Manaus serves as the capital of Amazonas and is approximately 11 miles upstream from where the Rio Negro meets the Amazon River. This temple, the sixth in Brazil, was announced on May 23, 2007, and was a significant blessing for many members in northern Brazil who previously traveled long distances to reach other temples. Groundbreaking for the Manaus Brazil Temple took place on June 20, 2008, with Elder Charles A. Didier overseeing the ceremony. The temple was dedicated on October 5, 2011, and features a single spire topped with a gold-leafed angel Moroni statue.

name: Manhattan New York Temple
description: The Manhattan New York Temple closed on March 2, 2024, for significant renovations expected to take around three years. Updates will also be made to the meetinghouse located on the third floor. During this period, members of the Church in the temple district are advised to visit the Philadelphia Pennsylvania Temple or the Hartford Connecticut Temple. The temple, situated at the intersection of West 65th Street, Broadway, and Columbus Avenue, is notable for its proximity to landmarks like Lincoln Center and Central Park. Originally completed in 1976, the Manhattan New York Temple was the second temple built in New York and is designed to be soundproofed from the city's noise.

name: Manila Philippines Temple
address: 13 Temple Drive corner Whiteplains Avenue Greenmeadows Subdivision UGONG NORTE
description: The Manila Philippines Temple is situated on a hilltop overlooking the Marikina Valley and is part of a complex that includes a temple annex, patron housing, a missionary training center, and area offices. The temple grounds, which are accessible to the public, feature beautiful palm trees and vibrant vegetation. It was the first temple established in the Philippines and the second in Asia, with the street renamed Temple Drive during its construction. Groundbreaking took place despite concerns from an approaching typhoon, which changed direction after a missionary's prayer. The temple was dedicated in nine sessions by President Gordon B. Hinckley and features six detached spires topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Manti Utah Temple
description: The Manti Utah Temple is situated on Temple Hill, overlooking the Sanpete Valley in Central Utah. Easily visible from Highway 89, the temple is near the Pioneer Heritage Center and Gardens, a 2.5-acre park that includes a reflecting pool, walkways, and an amphitheater. This temple, originally called the Manti Temple, was the third constructed in Utah Territory and features unique architectural elements, such as twin spiral staircases and hand-painted murals in its ordinance rooms. After closing for major renovations on October 2, 2021, the temple was rededicated on April 21, 2024, following updates to its systems and restoration of its historic features. The recent open house attracted 230,665 visitors eager to see the refreshed interior.

name: Maputo Mozambique Temple
description: The Maputo Mozambique Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the second in Mozambique, following the announcement of the Beira Mozambique Temple in April 2021. Mozambique has nearly 25,000 Latter-day Saints across about 70 congregations. The capital city, Maputo, has a population exceeding 1 million, and missionary work began in the country in 1999.

name: Maracaibo Venezuela Temple
description: The Maracaibo Venezuela Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced. On April 7, 2024, President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Annual General Conference, marking it as the second temple in Venezuela. The Caracas Venezuela Temple was dedicated in 2000 by President Gordon B. Hinckley. At the time of the announcement, Venezuela had over 175,000 Latter-day Saints in 230 congregations. The first official congregation was established in 1966, and the first baptism occurred in 1967.

name: Mbuji-Mayi Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple
photoCaption: Mbuji-Mayi Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple
description: The Mbuji-Mayi Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for this temple during the October 2023 General Conference. Mbuji-Mayi, the capital of Kasai-Oriental Province and the second largest city in the country, will host the fourth temple in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The Kinshasa temple was dedicated in 2019, while a temple in Lubumbashi is under construction and another for Kananga was announced in October 2021. The Democratic Republic of the Congo has over 100,000 Latter-day Saints in approximately 270 congregations, with the first members joining the Church in Europe during the 1960s.

name: McAllen Texas Temple
description: The McAllen Texas Temple is situated near the southern tip of Texas, creating a striking outline in the Rio Grande Valley. Its design draws inspiration from local citrus agriculture and Spanish colonial architecture, featuring motifs like citrus blossoms and barbed quatrefoils. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 5, 2019, it became the fifth temple in Texas, following the Dallas, Houston, Lubbock, and San Antonio temples. The temple, which spans nearly 30,000 square feet, includes a meetinghouse and was dedicated by Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf on October 8, 2023. The structure incorporates various artistic elements, including custom art glass and decorative features that reflect the local landscape.

name: Medellín Colombia Temple
description: The Medellín Colombia Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. Once completed, it will be the fourth temple in Colombia, joining the Barranquilla, Bogotá, and Cali temples. Medellín is Colombia's second largest city, and the country currently has over 215,000 Latter-day Saints across nearly 260 congregations. Missionaries first arrived in Colombia in 1966.

name: Medford Oregon Temple
description: The Medford Oregon Temple is the second temple established in Oregon, following the Portland Oregon Temple, which was completed in 1989. During the groundbreaking ceremony, Elder D. Lee Tobler emphasized its significance as a symbol of the gospel's restoration for both current and future generations. The temple serves not only its members but also the surrounding community. A minor renovation project began on July 11, 2021, and on October 18, 2021, the gold-leafed fiberglass statue of the angel Moroni was replaced atop the temple's spire. The temple features a gray granite exterior sourced from Mount Airy, North Carolina, and includes a single attached spire.

name: Melbourne Australia Temple
description: The Melbourne Australia Temple is located on a gently sloping site above the M3 freeway in Wantirna South, approximately 15 miles from Melbourne's city center. Built on the former grounds of the Melbourne Australia Maroondah Stake center, the granite temple is surrounded by trees and includes a semi-circular gathering plaza. It is the third temple established in Australia, following the Sydney Australia Temple in 1984 and the Adelaide Australia Temple in 2000. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on the same day as ceremonies for three other temples, and the temple was announced on October 30, 1998. The temple was dedicated by President Gordon B. Hinckley, marking a significant moment for local members who previously traveled long distances to attend other temples.

name: Memphis Tennessee Temple
description: The Memphis Tennessee Temple is located adjacent to the stake center for the Memphis Tennessee North Stake in Bartlett, a suburb northeast of Memphis. It was the first temple established in Tennessee, although plans for a Nashville temple had been announced earlier but faced delays. The groundbreaking for the Memphis Tennessee Temple occurred on January 16, 1999, coinciding with the Mérida Mexico Temple's groundbreaking. It was dedicated on the same day as the Reno Nevada Temple. Following a major renovation that began on September 29, 2017, the temple was rededicated on May 5, 2019, enhancing its entry and tower while addressing ventilation and layout improvements.

name: Mendoza Argentina Temple
description: The Mendoza Argentina Temple is the fourth temple established in Argentina, following the Buenos Aires Argentina Temple (1986), Córdoba Argentina Temple (2015), and Salta Argentina Temple (2024). President Russell M. Nelson announced its construction on October 7, 2018, during the October General Conference. The temple is located in the Champagnat neighborhood of Las Heras, north of Mendoza, and features a single-story design of approximately 21,000 square feet, with classical proportions and art glass windows depicting the native jarilla flower. Groundbreaking took place on December 17, 2020, led by Elder Allen D. Haynie. The temple opened for public tours from August 22 to September 7, 2024, and was dedicated by Elder Ronald A. Rasband on September 22, 2024.

name: Meridian Idaho Temple
description: The Meridian Idaho Temple is located at the northern end of Meridian, near the Boise River and North Linder Road. Its design is influenced by early Church temples, particularly the Cardston Alberta Temple. The temple shares its site with a meetinghouse and features well-maintained grounds that include two large ponds and a spacious east lawn. Announced on April 2, 2011, during the 181st Annual General Conference, it is the fifth temple in Idaho, following the Idaho Falls, Boise, Rexburg, and Twin Falls temples. The temple was dedicated on November 19, 2017, by President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, and it features a distinctive gold dome topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Mesa Arizona Temple
description: The Mesa Arizona Temple, situated east of the original Mesa Townsite established by pioneers of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, serves as a focal point in a historic district that has largely maintained its residential nature. The temple grounds include a public visitors' center, a cactus garden, and expansive reflection pools. Each Easter, the temple hosts thousands of visitors for Jesus the Christ, the world's largest outdoor Easter pageant, while Christmas transforms the area into a stunning Nativity display adorned with countless lights. Originally named the Arizona Temple, it was the first in Arizona and the first to offer the endowment in Spanish in 1945. The temple underwent significant renovations starting in May 2018, enhancing its facilities while preserving its historical character and murals.

name: Mexico City Benemérito Mexico Temple
address: Tenayuca-Chalmita 828 Colonia Zona Escolar Gustavo A. Madero
description: The Mexico City Benemérito Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. An exterior rendering was made public on December 16, 2024. The temple will be located at Tenayuca-Chalmita 828 in Colonia Zona Escolar, on a former recreational area of the Mexico City Missionary Training Center. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 3, 2022, this temple will be the 19th in Mexico and the second in Mexico City, covering approximately 29,000 square feet over two stories. The site has historical significance for Mexican Latter-day Saints, as it was previously home to a high school and later a Missionary Training Center.

name: Mexico City Mexico Temple
address: Avenida 510 N°90 Col. San Juan de Aragon
description: The Mexico City Mexico Temple is a prominent structure in northeastern Mexico City, situated near Bosque de Aragón. Its exterior showcases intricate Mayan-inspired designs, and the temple grounds include beautiful gardens and a water feature. The site also houses several Church facilities, including a missionary training center and a visitors' center featuring a replica of Thorvaldsen's Christus statue. This temple, the first in Mexico and the largest outside the United States, has undergone significant renovations, including a major update in 2007 and another in 2014. The temple has been a focal point for the local community, attracting thousands during its open houses and rededications.

name: Milan Italy Temple
description: The Milan Italy Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the second house of the Lord in Italy, following the Rome Italy Temple, which was dedicated in 2019. Italy has over 28,000 Latter-day Saints across nearly 100 congregations. The first Latter-day Saint congregation in Italy was established in 1966, the same year the first Italian mission was opened in Florence.

name: Milwaukee Wisconsin Temple
description: The Milwaukee Wisconsin Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the first in Wisconsin, which has over 28,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 65 congregations. Milwaukee is the state's largest city. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public.

name: Miraflores Guatemala City Guatemala Temple
description: The Miraflores Guatemala City Guatemala Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on December 3, 2022, led by Elder Patricio M. Giuffra. This temple will be built on a 1.5-acre site previously occupied by the Roosevelt Ward meetinghouse, located at the intersection of 13 Calle and 5A Avenida in Guatemala City. The two-story structure will cover approximately 30,000 square feet. Announced on July 1, 2022, it will be the fourth temple in Guatemala, joining the existing Guatemala City Guatemala Temple, Quetzaltenango Guatemala Temple, and the Cobán Guatemala Temple, which is currently under construction. The Miraflores temple will also make Guatemala City one of the few cities worldwide to have multiple temples.

name: Missoula Montana Temple
address: Old Bitterroot Road and Lower Miller Creek Road
description: The Missoula Montana Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. An exterior rendering was made public on December 23, 2024. The temple will be situated on a 5.08-acre site at the intersection of Old Bitterroot Road and Lower Miller Creek Road in southern Missoula. It will be a single-story structure, approximately 19,000 square feet, accompanied by an ancillary building. This temple will be the third in Montana, following the Billings Montana Temple, dedicated in November 1999, and the Helena Montana Temple, announced in April 2021.

name: Modesto California Temple
description: The Modesto California Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony on Saturday, October 7, 2023. Elder Gary B. Sabin, a General Authority Seventy, will conduct the dedicatory prayer for the site. This temple will cover 30,000 square feet and be built on a 17.63-acre site next to an existing meetinghouse on Dale Road. The temple's location was announced on October 10, 2022, and its official rendering was released on December 19, 2022. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the April 2022 General Conference, this will be California's tenth temple.

name: Monrovia Liberia Temple
description: The Monrovia Liberia Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. Renderings and site plans have not been publicly shared. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the October 2021 General Conference, marking it as the first temple in Liberia. The country is home to approximately 15,000 Latter-day Saints and over 50 congregations. Monrovia, the capital city, has seen missionary work since 1987.

name: Monterrey Mexico Temple
address: Carretera Nacional #7860 Esq. Privada Valle de la Estanzuela Colonia Valle Alto
description: The Monterrey Mexico Temple is situated in Valle Alto, in the southeastern part of Monterrey, near the National Highway and the iconic Cerro de la Silla. Alongside the temple is a stake center that welcomes visitors for Sunday worship services. The temple grounds are open to the public for peaceful walks. This temple is the twelfth in Mexico and was announced as the second for the country. The site was finalized in March 2000, with groundbreaking occurring on November 4, 2000, and features a white granite exterior from Vermont and a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Montevideo Uruguay Temple
description: The Montevideo Uruguay Temple is situated on a Church-owned city block in the upscale Carrasco neighborhood of Montevideo. This site includes a meetinghouse, patron housing, two mission homes, a regional service center, and a Distribution Services store. The temple grounds are adorned with palm trees, shrubs, and vibrant flowers. It was the first temple established in Uruguay, with the property acquired by the Church in the 1960s. The temple features a single attached spire topped with an angel Moroni statue and is the 103rd temple dedicated by the Church.

name: Monticello Utah Temple
description: The Monticello Utah Temple is situated approximately 60 miles south of Moab, Utah, in the town of Monticello. It is framed by the scenic Abajo Mountains and shares a parking lot with an adjacent meetinghouse. This temple was the first of the smaller temples envisioned by President Gordon B. Hinckley and is the eleventh temple built in Utah. Constructed in just over eight months, it holds the record for the fastest construction time among temples of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Originally topped with a white angel Moroni statue, it was replaced on May 25, 1999, with a taller, gold-leafed version to enhance visibility.

name: Montpelier Idaho Temple
description: The Montpelier Idaho Temple had its groundbreaking ceremony on June 17, 2023, presided over by Elder Ryan K. Olsen, a General Authority Seventy. The event attracted over 600 attendees and featured speakers along with a children's choir from local congregations. An official exterior rendering of the temple was released on April 24, 2023, following the announcement of its location on May 20, 2022, which is a 2.6-acre site on Washington Street. This temple will be the eighth in Idaho, joining others such as the Idaho Falls Idaho Temple and the Boise Idaho Temple. The Montpelier Idaho Temple was announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the April 2022 General Conference.

name: Montreal Quebec Temple
description: The Montreal Quebec Temple is the sixth temple established in Canada and the first in Quebec. It was dedicated on the same day as the San José Costa Rica Temple. On June 2, 2014, the temple closed for extensive renovations, which included reinforcing the structure with concrete and steel, addressing mold issues, and updating the interior and exterior aesthetics. The temple was rededicated on November 22, 2015. Its exterior features granite from Quebec, with art glass designed by VCBO Architecture, and the baptismal font is made of Crema Marfil stone with Jerusalem Gold accents.

name: Moses Lake Washington Temple
description: The Moses Lake Washington Temple is the fourth temple established in Washington, following the Seattle Washington Temple (1980), Spokane Washington Temple (1999), and Columbia River Washington Temple (2001). Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 7, 2019, this temple is located in Moses Lake, where local members previously traveled to the Columbia River Washington Temple for services.
