The official site for the temple was revealed on October 29, 2019, on a 17-acre property near Yonezawa Park and Moses Lake High School. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on October 10, 2020, and the temple was dedicated on September 17, 2023. The temple features a single-story design with a central spire, constructed with Branco Cristal granite and includes various artistic elements reflecting the region's heritage.

name: Mount Timpanogos Utah Temple
description: The Mount Timpanogos Utah Temple is situated in northeast American Fork, adjacent to the impressive 11,750-foot Mount Timpanogos. The temple grounds are open to visitors, who can enjoy the scenic beauty and peaceful atmosphere. This temple, the ninth in Utah and the second in Utah County, was announced without a specific location, which was later revealed to be a former Church welfare farm. Groundbreaking took place a year after the announcement, with around 12,000 attendees present. The temple features a Sierra white granite exterior, art glass windows, and a central spire topped with a gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Mérida Mexico Temple
description: The Mérida Mexico Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place simultaneously with that of the Memphis Tennessee Temple. Situated in Yucatán, this temple is on the northern end of the Yucatán Peninsula, near the Gulf of Mexico, an area rich in Mesoamerican history and archaeological sites like Uxmal and Chichén Itzá. Elder Carl B. Pratt, a member of the Seventy and president of the Mexico South Area, presided over the event and expressed joy at the announcement of the temple's construction. He emphasized the importance of temple attendance for strengthening families and communities. The temple, the 92nd in operation, features an exterior of Blanco Guardiano white marble from Torreón, Mexico, and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Naga Philippines Temple
description: The Naga Philippines Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for this temple during the October 2022 General Conference, marking it as the ninth temple to be announced in the Philippines. Naga City is situated approximately 250 miles southeast of Manila, where the first temple was dedicated in 1984. The Philippines has over 833,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 1,250 congregations, experiencing rapid growth since the introduction of missionary work in 1961. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public.

name: Nairobi Kenya Temple
description: The Nairobi Kenya Temple is a significant landmark located in the Mountain View neighborhood of Nairobi along Waiyaki Way, a key highway in Southwest Kenya. The temple's design incorporates the African lily, prominently featured in the art glass and interior decor. It shares its grounds with a large building that includes a meetinghouse and facilities for patrons. This temple, the first in East Africa and the ninth in Africa, was announced by President Thomas S. Monson during the 187th Annual General Conference. The temple was officially dedicated on May 18, 2025, by Elder Ulisses Soares, following an open house that began on April 14, 2025.

name: Nashville Tennessee Temple
description: The Nashville Tennessee Temple is located 15 miles south of Nashville in the suburb of Franklin, adjacent to the Franklin Tennessee Stake Center. The temple is surrounded by two large horse farms and the historic Battle Ground Academy. It was the second temple established in Tennessee, following the Memphis Tennessee Temple, and was intended to serve much of the Upper South. After initial plans for a different site were abandoned, the groundbreaking took place on a rainy day in 1998, attended by about 1,500 members. The temple was dedicated on May 21, 2000, by President James E. Faust, and features an exterior of Imperial Danby white marble with a single spire topped by an angel Moroni statue.

name: Natal Brazil Temple
address: Av. Senador Salgado Filho (BR-101) Nova Parnamirim
description: The Natal Brazil Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony presided over by Elder Mark D. Eddy, Second Counselor in the Brazil Area Presidency, on Saturday, May 17, 2025. This temple will be built on a 5.53-acre site on Avenida Senador Salgado Filho (BR-101) in the Nova Parnamirim neighborhood of Parnamirim. It is designed as a single-level structure, covering approximately 19,800 square feet. The official exterior rendering was made public on February 12, 2024, following the announcement of the temple's location on August 28, 2023. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the Natal Brazil Temple during the April 2023 General Conference, marking it as the 20th temple announced for Brazil.

name: Nauvoo Illinois Temple
description: The Nauvoo Illinois Temple is situated on a prominent bluff that overlooks a bend in the Mississippi River. This temple is a faithful reconstruction of the original Nauvoo Temple, which was built in the 1840s and destroyed by fire and severe weather shortly thereafter. The temple grounds feature a statue of Church founder Joseph Smith and his brother Hyrum, who were martyred in Carthage Jail. The temple is a significant site in Church history, attracting thousands of visitors annually, especially during the summer when it operates an extended schedule. The Nauvoo Illinois Temple is notable for its beautiful murals and is one of only seven temples where patrons progress through multiple ordinance rooms before reaching the Celestial Room.

name: Nauvoo Temple
photoCaption: Remaining West Facade following the Fire and Tornado
description: The Nauvoo Illinois Temple, originally constructed in the 1840s, is situated on a bluff overlooking the Mississippi River. It was built on a city block bordered by Woodruff, Mulholland, Knight, and Wells streets. The temple was destroyed by an arson fire in 1848, just two years after its dedication, and was further damaged by a tornado in 1850, leading to its eventual demolition. The Nauvoo Temple was notable for being the first temple in Illinois and the first to feature an angel on its tower. It was also the site where significant practices, such as baptisms for the dead and the organization of the Relief Society, were restored through Joseph Smith.

name: Neiafu Tonga Temple
description: The Neiafu Tonga Temple is being constructed on Tu’i Road in Neiafu, Tonga, at the site of the Church-owned Saineha High School. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on September 11, 2021, with King ʻAhoʻeitu Tupou VI and Queen Nanasipau'u in attendance. Elder Inoke Kupu, Area Seventy, emphasized the significance of having a temple on Vava’u Island. This temple, announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 7, 2019, will be the second in Tonga, following the Nuku'alofa Tonga Temple built in 1983. The Neiafu Tonga Temple will feature a single-story design of nearly 17,000 square feet, along with an ancillary building for various support services.

name: Newport Beach California Temple
description: The Newport Beach California Temple is the sixth temple established in California and the second in the Los Angeles Metropolitan Area, following the Los Angeles California Temple built in 1956. It was announced on April 21, 2001, alongside the Redlands and Sacramento California Temples. The Newport Beach Planning Commission approved the temple on October 3, 2002, despite local opposition, leading to compromises such as adjusting the building's color and reducing the spire height. Final approval was granted by the Newport Beach City Council on November 12, 2002, after further reducing the steeple height to 90 feet. Groundbreaking took place on August 15, 2003, and the temple was topped with a statue of the angel Moroni on January 13, 2005, during which a solar halo was observed.

name: Norfolk Virginia Temple
description: The Norfolk Virginia Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans for the Norfolk Virginia Temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the fourth in Virginia, joining the Richmond Virginia Temple, dedicated in May 2023, as well as the Roanoke and Winchester Virginia Temples, both announced in 2023. Virginia is home to approximately 100,000 Latter-day Saints across about 210 congregations.

name: Nouméa New Caledonia Temple
description: The Nouméa New Caledonia Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the first for New Caledonia, which is home to over 2,500 members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Nouméa, the capital, has a population of around 100,000. The first stake in New Caledonia was established in 2012, following the arrival of the first church members from Tahiti.

name: Nuku'alofa Tonga Temple
description: The Nuku'alofa Tonga Temple is located in Nuku'alofa, the capital of the Kingdom of Tonga, on the northern coast of Tongatapu, several miles south of the city at the site of Liahona High School. It was the fourth temple established in Polynesia, following the Laie Hawaii Temple, Hamilton New Zealand Temple, and Apia Samoa Temple, and is the first temple in Tonga. The temple's groundbreaking occurred just before that of the Apia Samoa Temple, and both were constructed simultaneously. Dedicated shortly after the Apia Samoa Temple, the Nuku'alofa Tonga Temple underwent significant renovations and expansion, reopening in 2007 with over 5,000 additional square feet. The rededication event featured a cultural celebration attended by the king of Tonga and was marked by a nationwide clean-up campaign to prepare for the influx of visitors.

name: Oakland California Temple
description: The Oakland California Temple, standing at 170 feet, is a prominent landmark overlooking the San Francisco Bay Area. Its grounds feature beautiful rooftop gardens, a cascading waterfall, and a creek-style water feature, complemented by colorful gardens and palm trees. The temple showcases relief sculptures depicting Christ teaching His disciples and appearing to the Nephites. Opened in 1964, it was the second temple built in California and the first with five spires, reflecting the area's diverse population. The temple underwent significant renovations in 1990 and 2018 to enhance its functionality and preserve its historical significance.

name: Oaxaca Mexico Temple
address: Avenida Universidad #139 Fracc. Real de Candiani
description: The Oaxaca Mexico Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place alongside those for the Kona Hawaii Temple and Nashville Tennessee Temple. Elder Carl B. Pratt, a member of the Seventy and president of the Mexico South Area, presided over the event. He referenced a statement by President Brigham Young from 1863 about the future proliferation of temples worldwide, noting that this vision is being realized today. Elder Pratt emphasized the significance of the day and the sacrifices made by early saints for temple construction. He encouraged members to prepare for increased missionary efforts and to strengthen their spiritual practices. The Oaxaca Mexico Temple is the 74th temple dedicated, featuring an exterior of white marble from Torreón, Mexico, and a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Ogden Utah Temple
description: The Ogden Utah Temple is a prominent religious site located in downtown Ogden, occupying a full city block on Washington Boulevard (US Highway 89). It shares its grounds with the historic Ogden Tabernacle, the last tabernacle constructed by the Church, completed in 1956. As the fifth temple built in Utah and the first dedicated in the state, it features six instruction rooms, making it one of only four temples with this capacity. The temple underwent a significant renovation that was completed in 2014, enhancing its exterior and landscaping while preserving much of the original interior layout. The temple's spire, originally gold, was painted white, and an angel Moroni statue was added in 2002 as part of an exterior renovation project.

name: Okinawa Japan Temple
description: The Okinawa Japan Temple is situated in Okinawa City, close to the Kadena Air Base. Its design showcases Japanese architectural elements, including floral motifs inspired by local trees and details reminiscent of traditional Shibi roof tiles. This temple, the fourth in Japan, was announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 7, 2019, and ground was broken on December 5, 2020. The temple spans 12,437 square feet and is designed to harmonize with its surroundings, providing a peaceful space for worship. It will be dedicated on November 12, 2023, serving the Latter-day Saints in Okinawa and nearby islands.

name: Oklahoma City Oklahoma Temple
description: The Oklahoma City Oklahoma Temple was the first temple established in Oklahoma. It closed on October 15, 2017, for significant renovations that changed its exterior and upgraded the interior. The temple was rededicated on May 19, 2019, by President Henry B. Eyring, the second counselor in the First Presidency. During the groundbreaking, Elder Rex D. Pinegar emphasized the symbolic nature of the ceremony and the temple's role in strengthening faith and families in the community. He also acknowledged the resilience of the local population following tragedies, including the May 3 tornado and the 1995 federal building bombing.

name: Oquirrh Mountain Utah Temple
description: The Oquirrh Mountain Utah Temple is located on a scenic bluff west of Bangerter Highway, at the base of the Oquirrh Mountains. It offers a view of the Wasatch Mountains and is positioned near three other temples: the Salt Lake Temple, Jordan River Utah Temple, and Draper Utah Temple. The temple grounds feature walkways and are accessible to the public, while an adjacent meetinghouse hosts Sunday worship services. This temple, dedicated by President Thomas S. Monson on August 23, 2009, was the thirteenth built in Utah and the first in South Jordan, which is notable for having two operating temples. The temple's spire was completed in July 2008, and a gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni was installed shortly thereafter.

name: Orem Utah Temple
description: The Orem Utah Temple is situated between the Wasatch Mountains and Utah Lake, on land originally settled by Norwegian immigrants in 1864. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints acquired the 15-acre site in 2004, which was previously homesteaded by the Williamsen family. The temple's interior design prominently features cherry blossoms, reflecting the area's agricultural history, while the overall aesthetic emphasizes simplicity and natural materials. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 5, 2019, the temple is the nineteenth built in Utah and was dedicated on January 21, 2024. The structure includes a three-story building with a central spire, granite cladding, and various artistic elements inspired by local flora and wetlands.

name: Orlando Florida Temple
description: The Orlando Florida Temple, which has been in operation for 30 years, announced a significant renovation on February 12, 2024. The temple closed on July 1, 2024, and will reopen at a later date to be determined. It is located in Windermere, overlooking a series of lakes, and is known for its white exterior, elegant columns, arched windows, and water features. The Orlando Florida Temple was the first temple established in Florida and is one of only two dedicated by President Howard W. Hunter. The temple grounds are open to the public and feature numerous palm trees and shrubs.

name: Osaka Japan Temple
description: The Osaka Japan Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple's location was announced on March 4, 2024, as a 16.74-acre site at 3-50-1 Sugi, Hirakata City, Osaka Prefecture. An official exterior rendering was made public on September 8, 2025. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the October 2023 General Conference, marking it as the fifth temple in Japan. The temple will be a single-story structure covering approximately 29,630 square feet.

name: Oslo Norway Temple
description: The Oslo Norway Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. On May 1, 2023, the official exterior rendering was made public, and the temple will be situated on an 8-acre site at the intersection of Smedsvingen and Ravnsborgveien roads in Hvalstad, Norway. The design includes a single-story structure of approximately 10,800 square feet, featuring patron housing and arrival facilities. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021. This temple will be the first in Norway, which has around 5,000 Latter-day Saints.

name: Pachuca Mexico Temple
description: The Pachuca Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build the temple during the October 2022 General Conference. This temple will be the first in the state of Hidalgo. Pachuca, the capital and largest city of Hidalgo, is situated approximately 75 miles northeast of Mexico City and has a population of around 277,000. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public.

name: Pago Pago American Samoa Temple
description: The Pago Pago American Samoa Temple, the second temple in the Samoan Islands, had its groundbreaking ceremony on October 30. Elder K. Brett Nattress from the Pacific Area presidency led the event, attended by Church officials and local leaders, which took place next to the stake center in the Ottoville neighborhood of Pago Pago. The temple will be built on Ottoville Road and will feature a single-story structure of nearly 17,000 square feet, along with a distribution center and housing for temple leaders. Announced on August 14, 2020, this temple will serve the Latter-day Saints in American Samoa, where the population includes a significant number of Church members. The temple is expected to be completed by late 2025 to early 2026.

name: Palmyra New York Temple
description: The Palmyra New York Temple is located on a ridge near the Sacred Grove, where Joseph Smith experienced his First Vision in 1820. This temple, the first in New York, serves as a significant landmark in Church history, surrounded by sites like the Hill Cumorah Visitors' Center. It was the 100th temple announced by the Church and is situated on the eastern end of the original Smith Family Farm. Dedicated on April 6, 2000, the temple's design includes stained-glass windows inspired by the Sacred Grove, created by artist Tom Holdman. The dedicatory services were broadcast across North America, marking a historic moment for the Church.

name: Panama City Panama Temple
address: Calle Rufina Alfaro #3172 Hacia La Villa de Cardenas Corozal
description: The Panama City Panama Temple is situated on a verdant hillside that overlooks the renowned Panama Canal. It is located next to the remodeled Cárdenas meetinghouse and features a large facility for the temple presidency, missionaries, and patrons. The temple, which is the first in Panama and the third in Central America, was dedicated on August 10, 2008, following a public open house that attracted nearly 33,000 visitors. Groundbreaking took place on October 30, 2005, under the guidance of Elder Spencer V. Jones, despite Hurricane Beta's nearby threat. The dedication ceremony included a cornerstone sealing and was attended by Church leaders, including President Thomas S. Monson, who later met with Panamanian President Martin Torrijos to discuss the Church's humanitarian efforts in the country.

name: Papeete Tahiti Temple
description: The Papeete Tahiti Temple, situated in Pirae near Papeete, the capital of French Polynesia, is noted for its distinctive blue roof and well-kept gardens. Visitors can explore the temple grounds and appreciate its beauty and lush surroundings. This temple was the fifth constructed in Polynesia and the first in Overseas France, dedicated in October 1983 by President Gordon B. Hinckley. Prior to its opening, Tahitian members traveled 2,500 miles to the Hamilton New Zealand Temple. After a significant renovation and expansion, the temple was rededicated in November 2006, enhancing its facilities and grounds.

name: Paris France Temple
description: The Paris France Temple is located in Le Chesnay, a suburb of Paris, near the historic Palace of Versailles. The temple grounds feature a marble replica of Thorvaldsen's Christus statue and include water features, a visitors' center with a model of the temple, and facilities for the temple president and matron, as well as patrons and missionaries. This temple, dedicated on May 21, 2017, is the first of its kind in mainland France and the twelfth in Europe. Construction began after the site was cleared of two buildings previously leased by a state-owned utility, with the official announcement made on July 15, 2011. The temple's design is notable for not including an angel Moroni statue, a departure from most other temples built since 1964.

name: Payson Utah Temple
description: The Payson Utah Temple was officially announced by President Thomas S. Monson on January 25, 2010, to serve the growing membership in southern Utah County. A ceremonial groundbreaking took place on October 8, 2011, attended by several thousand people, with Elder Dallin H. Oaks presiding. The temple site, located near the intersection of 930 West and 1550 South, was officially conveyed to the Church on August 6, 2010. Construction plans included a conditional-use permit allowing the temple to exceed height restrictions and utilize shared parking with an adjacent meetinghouse. The temple, featuring a central spire topped with an angel Moroni statue, was dedicated as the fifteenth temple in Utah and the third in Utah County.

name: Perth Australia Temple
description: The Perth Australia Temple is the fourth temple established in Australia, following the Sydney Australia Temple (1984), Adelaide Australia Temple (2000), and Melbourne Australia Temple (2000). Located approximately 1,400 miles from its nearest major city, Adelaide, the temple serves 6,865 members from four stakes and the Australia Perth Mission. Construction took place on property adjacent to the Dianella Stake Centre in Yokine, about six miles north of Perth. The groundbreaking was presided over by Elder Kenneth Johnson, who emphasized the divine guidance in temple construction. The temple features an exterior of Italian Olympia white granite and includes a single attached spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Philadelphia Pennsylvania Temple
description: The Philadelphia Pennsylvania Temple, a neoclassical structure, stands 208 feet tall in Center City Philadelphia along the Benjamin Franklin Parkway. It is situated at the northeast corner of Logan Square, opposite the Cathedral Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul. The temple complex includes a distribution center, meetinghouse, and various service facilities, all surrounded by a landscaped plaza with gardens and a reflecting pool. Announced on October 4, 2008, by President Thomas S. Monson, it is the first temple in Pennsylvania and the fourth in the Mid-Atlantic region. The temple was dedicated on September 18, 2016, by President Henry B. Eyring, marking a significant addition to the city’s architectural landscape.

name: Phnom Penh Cambodia Temple
description: The Phnom Penh Cambodia Temple, the first of its kind in the country, had its groundbreaking ceremony on September 18, 2021, led by President Veasna Kuonno Neang of the Cambodia Phnom Penh Mission. This temple will provide local Latter-day Saints, who previously traveled to Hong Kong or the Philippines for temple worship, with easier access to sacred ordinances. The 10,000-square-foot temple will be located on a 3.16-acre site on Russian Confederation Street, near the Royal University of Phnom Penh. The announcement for the temple's construction was made by President Russell M. Nelson on October 7, 2018, during a visit to Cambodia. The Phnom Penh Cambodia Temple will serve over 14,600 Latter-day Saints in the nation, marking a significant milestone for the local community.

name: Phoenix Arizona Temple
description: The Phoenix Arizona Temple had the angel Moroni statue placed on its spire on May 15, 2013, during a ceremony attended by workers and church members. The groundbreaking for the temple occurred on June 4, 2011, led by Elder Ronald A. Rasband. The Church submitted a rezoning application for the temple site in Phoenix on April 29, 2009, which included an 8.94-acre area. Following community meetings and discussions regarding concerns about the temple's height and impact, the Phoenix City Council approved the rezoning on December 2, 2009, allowing for a building height of 40 feet. The temple was redesigned to comply with residential zoning requirements, and construction began after the building permit was issued on October 17, 2011.

name: Pittsburgh Pennsylvania Temple
description: The Pittsburgh Pennsylvania Temple is situated in Cranberry Township, north of Pittsburgh, adjacent to the Pittsburgh Pennsylvania North Stake center. A footbridge connects the temple grounds to the stake center, symbolizing Pittsburgh's identity as the "City of Bridges." This temple, the second in Pennsylvania after the Philadelphia Pennsylvania Temple, was announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 5, 2020. It serves members from Western Pennsylvania, Northeast Ohio, and Northern West Virginia, who previously traveled to the Columbus Ohio Temple and Washington D.C. Temple for worship. The temple features a single-story design of approximately 32,000 square feet, with a center spire and distinctive gold accents, and was dedicated on September 15, 2024, by Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf.

name: Piura Peru Temple
description: The Piura Peru Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the October 2023 General Conference on October 1, 2023. This temple will be the first in the Piura Region and the eighth in Peru. At the time of the announcement, there were approximately 630,000 Latter-day Saints in over 775 congregations across the country. Existing temples in Peru include the Arequipa, Chiclayo, Cusco, Iquitos, Lima, Lima Los Olivos, and Trujillo temples.

name: Pocatello Idaho Temple
description: The Pocatello Idaho Temple, standing at 195 feet, is located on the east bench of Pocatello, near the stake center for the Pocatello Idaho Highland Stake. Its striking granite exterior is visible from Interstate 15 and Interstate 86, especially when illuminated at night. The temple grounds feature nearly 500 trees and thousands of plants, with a plaza for bridal parties on the north side. Dedicated on November 7, 2021, the Pocatello Idaho Temple is the sixth temple in Idaho, following the Idaho Falls Idaho Temple and others. The temple's design includes a white granite exterior and art glass that reflects local flora, enhancing its connection to the surrounding landscape.

name: Port Moresby Papua New Guinea Temple
photoCaption: Port Moresby Papua New Guinea Temple
description: The Port Moresby Papua New Guinea Temple is set to become a significant landmark for the local community. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on April 22, 2023, attended by notable figures including Sir Bob Dadae, the Governor General of Papua New Guinea. This temple will be the first in the country, serving over 28,000 Latter-day Saints across 80 congregations. It will feature a single-level building of approximately 9,550 square feet, along with accommodations for temple missionaries and a distribution center. Construction is expected to be completed between late 2025 and early 2026.

name: Port Vila Vanuatu Temple
description: The Port Vila Vanuatu Temple's groundbreaking ceremony is now set for Saturday, April 8, 2023, after being postponed from March 4 due to Cyclones Judy and Kevin. This temple will be built on a 1.62-acre site at the Blacksands meetinghouse and will feature a single-story structure of approximately 10,000 square feet with one spire. Additionally, a meetinghouse and an ancillary building will be constructed, which will include an arrival center, patron housing, and a distribution center. The temple's location was officially announced on May 19, 2021, and it will be the first temple in Vanuatu and the third in Melanesia. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple on October 4, 2020.

name: Port-au-Prince Haiti Temple
address: Route de Frères Frères 23 Impasse Saint-Marc # 20 & 22
description: The Port-au-Prince Haiti Temple is located behind the Route de Frères meetinghouse in the Pétion-Ville suburb, east of Port-au-Prince. An arrival center at the north end of the meetinghouse provides amenities such as bathrooms, showers, and dining tables. This temple is the first in Haiti and the second in the Caribbean, following the Santo Domingo Dominican Republic Temple. The temple was announced by President Thomas S. Monson during the 185th Annual General Conference on April 5, 2015, and dedicated by Elder David A. Bednar on September 1, 2019. The temple features decor inspired by Haiti's natural beauty, including palm-leaf patterns and vibrant colors, with luxurious lighting elements incorporated throughout.

name: Portland Oregon Temple
description: The Portland Oregon Temple, located about 8 miles south of downtown Portland in Lake Oswego, is distinguished by its six spires made of marble, creating a striking view for drivers on I-5. A reflection pool is situated on the east side, while an infinity pool is complemented by a fountain on the west. Visitors can explore the temple's beautiful gardens and learn more at the public visitors' center, which includes films, displays, and a replica of Thorvaldsen's Christus statue. This temple, the first in Oregon, was built on land originally intended for a Church junior college, with 7.3 acres designated for the temple. The Portland Oregon Temple was dedicated on May 11, 1989, and features a two-story Celestial Room, sealing rooms, and a grand assembly hall, all designed with elegant architectural details.

name: Porto Alegre Brazil Temple
address: Rua General Salvador Pinheiro 50 Vila Jardim
description: The Porto Alegre Brazil Temple is the third temple established in Brazil. It is situated on a hillside that provides a view of the city and the river for which it is named. During the groundbreaking ceremony, President Faust initiated the digging and was joined by a young boy and girl, the latter of whom later expressed her gratitude at a regional conference. He highlighted the importance of sacrifice in temple construction, sharing how members in Argentina contributed gold from dental work for the São Paulo Brazil Temple. The Porto Alegre Brazil Temple, the 102nd dedicated temple, features a cotton white granite exterior from Ceará State and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Porto Portugal Temple
description: The Porto Portugal Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for the Porto Portugal Temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. Porto, the second-largest city in Portugal with around 1.3 million residents, is home to nearly 48,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 60 congregations. This temple will be the second in Portugal, following the Lisbon Portugal Temple, which was dedicated in 1975.

name: Praia Cape Verde Temple
address: Templo da Igreja de Jesus Cristo Dos Santos Dos Últimos Dias Avenida Cidade de Lisboa Bairro Taiti
description: The Praia Cape Verde Temple is located in the capital city of Praia, specifically in the historic Plateau area, near the National Library of Cape Verde. The temple shares its site with a meetinghouse and is surrounded by beautifully landscaped grounds filled with tropical flora. This temple is notable for being the first in the Macaronesia islands and in Cape Verde. The groundbreaking took place on May 4, 2019, and the temple was dedicated on June 19, 2022, by Elder Neil L. Andersen. During its public open house from May 21 to June 11, 2022, over 10,000 visitors toured the temple, which features a two-toned exterior and a domed steeple.

name: Preston England Temple
description: The Preston England Temple serves as a central part of a large Church complex in Northern England, situated north of Liverpool and Manchester. This complex includes a stake center, missionary training center, family history center, distribution center, patron housing, and accommodations for temple missionaries. The temple, which was the sixth in Europe and the second in the United Kingdom after the London England Temple, features beautifully landscaped grounds with mature trees, flower gardens, and reflection pools at the entrance. Missionary efforts in the British Isles began in 1837, leading to the baptism of the first converts in Preston's River Ribble. The temple was announced by President Gordon B. Hinckley on October 19, 1992, and is the 52nd temple dedicated, showcasing an exterior of Olympia white granite from Italy and a distinctive architectural design with a single spire topped by an angel Moroni statue.

name: Price Utah Temple
description: The Price Utah Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the first in Carbon County, situated in eastern Utah. It will be the 31st temple in Utah, which has nearly 2.2 million Latter-day Saints, making up about two-thirds of the state's population.

name: Provo City Center Temple
description: The Provo City Center Temple is located in Provo's Central Business District on University Avenue, between Center Street and 200 South. This temple is a careful restoration of the former Provo Tabernacle, which was constructed in the 1880s and destroyed by a fire in 2010. The temple honors the tabernacle's heritage while enhancing the vision of the pioneers with its Victorian design. It features a pavilion with a basement for non-temple visitors and landscaped grounds for gatherings and reflection. Dedicated on March 20, 2016, the Provo City Center Temple is the 150th temple in operation worldwide and the second temple in Provo, following the Provo Utah Temple.

name: Provo Utah Rock Canyon Temple
address: 2200 Temple Hill Dr Provo UT 84604-1775 United States
description: The Provo Utah Temple will undergo demolition and reconstruction, as announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the October 2021 General Conference. The temple will close on February 24, 2024, after the completion of ordinance work, and members are encouraged to use nearby temples during the closure. The new structure will be named the Provo Utah Rock Canyon Temple and will be located on Provo's east bench, featuring beautiful landscaping and a backdrop of mountains. Originally dedicated in 1972, the Provo Temple was the first in Utah County and was renamed in 1999. The Provo Utah Rock Canyon Temple will not include an angel Moroni statue, differing from the original design.

name: Puebla Mexico Temple
address: Av. 15 de Mayo # 719 Col. Los  Cipreses
description: The Puebla Mexico Temple is the fourteenth temple established in Mexico. Its announcement occurred on October 7, 2018, by President Russell M. Nelson during the 188th Semiannual General Conference. Located in the Los Cipreses neighborhood of Puebla, the temple serves over 50,000 members and is situated on a landscaped boulevard named 15 de Mayo. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on November 30, 2020, presided over by Elder Arnulfo Valenzuela. The temple was dedicated by Elder Gerrit W. Gong on May 19, 2024, following an open house that welcomed over 60,000 visitors from March 29 to April 20, 2024.

name: Puerto Montt Chile Temple
description: The Puerto Montt Chile Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the sixth in Chile, where over 600,000 Latter-day Saints are part of more than 570 congregations. The first temple in Spanish-speaking South America was dedicated in Santiago in 1983. Other temples in Chile include the Antofagasta Chile Temple, Concepción Chile Temple, Santiago West Chile Temple, and Viña del Mar Chile Temple.

name: Queen Creek Arizona Temple
description: The Queen Creek Arizona Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the eighth in Arizona, which has nearly 443,000 Latter-day Saints across about 925 congregations. Queen Creek, originally known as "Rittenhouse," was settled by early homesteaders and incorporated in 1989. The area has a population exceeding 80,000 and is located in the southeastern part of the Phoenix Metropolitan Area.

name: Querétaro Mexico Temple
address: Prolongación Tecnológico Norte 150 Colonia San Pablo
description: The Querétaro Mexico Temple's groundbreaking took place on January 7, 2023, with Elder Adrián Ochoa presiding over the ceremony. This temple will be situated on a 3.58-acre site at Prolongación Tecnológico Norte, opposite the Instituto Tecnológico y de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey. The design includes a two-story building covering approximately 27,500 square feet. The temple's location was officially announced on December 7, 2021, following President Russell M. Nelson's announcement of its construction during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021. This temple will be the 15th in Mexico, a country with around 1.5 million Latter-day Saints and a rich history of missionary work since 1875.

name: Quetzaltenango Guatemala Temple
address: 9A Calle 4-03 Zona 9 Frente a Residenciales Los Cerezos 1
description: The Quetzaltenango Guatemala Temple is situated in the scenic Quetzaltenango Valley, on a knoll at the western edge of Quetzaltenango, also known as Xela. It is located near the city zoo, Parque Zoológico Minerva, and across from Los Cerezos condominiums. This temple, which was the second in Guatemala after the Guatemala City Guatemala Temple, shares its design with the Snowflake Arizona Temple and Winter Quarters Nebraska Temple. Groundbreaking took place on a spring morning with over 700 attendees, including church leaders and local officials. The temple was dedicated in 2011, marking the first dedication by President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, and has since served as a vital spiritual center for members in Western Guatemala.

name: Quito Ecuador Temple
address: Ruta Viva y Escalón Lumbisí Esq.
description: The Quito Ecuador Temple is situated in the Cumbayá suburb, at the intersection of Ruta Viva and Escalón Lumbisí in the Tumbaco valley, within the Andes mountains. This temple, dedicated on November 20, 2022, is the second in Ecuador, following the Guayaquil Ecuador Temple. Prior to its construction, members in Quito had to travel significant distances to attend the nearest temple. The temple features a striking exterior of white Turkish limestone and includes artistic stained glass windows that reflect Ecuador's floral diversity. Standing at 97 feet tall, it is topped with a golden statue of Moroni, symbolizing its significance to Latter-day Saints.

name: Raleigh North Carolina Temple
description: The Raleigh North Carolina Temple was the first temple established in North Carolina. It closed on January 7, 2018, for significant renovations, which included upgrades to mechanical and electrical systems, ADA compliance, and modifications to the floor plan. The temple was dedicated shortly before the 194th anniversary of Joseph Smith's birth, serving as a meaningful gift for local Latter-day Saints. The dedication was attended by notable figures, including Cecil Reese, the first stake president in North Carolina, and community members who expressed their emotional connection to the temple. The temple features a beige limestone exterior and a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Rapid City South Dakota Temple
description: The Rapid City South Dakota Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for this temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. It will be the first temple in South Dakota, serving over 11,500 members across approximately 30 congregations. Rapid City, the second-largest city in the state, has a population exceeding 80,000 and is near the famous Mount Rushmore National Memorial. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public.

name: Recife Brazil Temple
address: Rua Dr. José de Góes 280 Parnamirim
description: The Recife Brazil Temple is the second temple established in Brazil. Prior to its construction, members in Recife had to travel fifty hours to reach the São Paulo Brazil Temple. During the groundbreaking ceremony, President Hinckley emphasized the importance of the temple for the community, expressing hope that members would frequently visit and participate in sacred ordinances. The temple, which is the 101st dedicated temple, features an exterior finish of Asa branca granite from Ceará and includes a single central spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni. It is expected to serve many thousands of members in northern Brazil.

name: Red Cliffs Utah Temple
description: The Red Cliffs Utah Temple is prominently situated within a stunning desert landscape, framed by the Pine Valley Mountains and rust-colored hills. Its striking profile is visible from afar, enhanced by a palm-tree-lined entrance that leads visitors to the temple and its northern gardens. The temple features serene pools with waterfalls, surrounded by lush plantings and shaded areas, creating a tranquil environment for reflection. Announced on October 7, 2018, it is the twentieth temple in Utah and the second in Washington County, following the St. George Utah Temple. The Red Cliffs Utah Temple was dedicated on March 24, 2024, and showcases a blend of desert modern and neoclassical architectural styles, reflecting the natural beauty of its surroundings.

name: Redlands California Temple
description: The Redlands California Temple is the fifth temple established in California, the third in Southern California, and the first in the Inland Empire. It was announced alongside the Newport Beach and Sacramento California Temples. On March 13, 2003, a 13½-foot statue of the angel Moroni was placed atop the temple, witnessed by many onlookers. The temple is located on land originally held by the Church in the San Bernardino colony, founded in 1851. Today, it stands in a residential area of East Redlands, previously filled with orange groves, and features a beautiful art glass panel from a historic meetinghouse.

name: Regina Saskatchewan Temple
description: The Regina Saskatchewan Temple is the fourth temple established in Canada and the first in Saskatchewan. It was dedicated on the same day as the Halifax Nova Scotia Temple, marking a significant event as it was the first instance of two temples being dedicated simultaneously. President Packer led the dedication in Regina, while President Gordon B. Hinckley presided over the Halifax dedication. Due to mechanical issues with President Hinckley's flight, the Halifax dedication was postponed by one day, leading to the decision to hold both dedications on the same day. The temple features light gray granite and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Reno Nevada Temple
description: The Reno Nevada Temple is the second temple established in Nevada, after the Las Vegas Nevada Temple, which was completed in 1989. It was dedicated on the same day as the Memphis Tennessee Temple. Elder Rex D. Pinegar of the Seventy presided over the groundbreaking on Pioneer Day, emphasizing the importance of honoring the pioneers who faced significant challenges. He highlighted that the temple serves as a source of strength and a reminder of God's presence for Church members today. The temple features a gray granite exterior sourced from Sharon, Vermont, and includes a single spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: Retalhuleu Guatemala Temple
description: The Retalhuleu Guatemala Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The official exterior rendering was made public on March 31, 2025, along with the announcement of its location on a 5.51-acre site at Km. 182.5 RN-9, Caserío Puca I, Municipio de San Sebastian, Retalhuleu, Guatemala. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the April 2023 General Conference. This temple will be the sixth in Guatemala, following the Guatemala City Guatemala Temple, which was dedicated in December 1984, and the Quetzaltenango Guatemala Temple, dedicated in December 2011. Guatemala currently has 287,000 Latter-day Saints across nearly 440 congregations.

name: Rexburg Idaho Temple
description: The Rexburg Idaho Temple, located next to the Brigham Young University–Idaho campus, is a prominent five-story structure that serves as a notable landmark along the Highway 20 corridor. It is the third temple established in Idaho, following the Idaho Falls Idaho Temple and the Boise Idaho Temple. The temple features a public garden area and is adorned with murals by local artist Leon Parson, as well as a wheat motif symbolizing the region's agricultural heritage. The groundbreaking ceremony in 2005 attracted over 8,000 attendees, and the temple's open house in 2008 drew more than 200,000 visitors. The dedication was postponed due to the passing of President Gordon B. Hinckley, and President Thomas S. Monson dedicated the temple a week later.

name: Reynosa Mexico Temple
description: The Reynosa Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build the temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the 27th dedicated house of the Lord in Mexico. Currently, there are several operational temples in the country, along with others under construction or announced. Mexico has a Latter-day Saints membership exceeding 1.5 million, making it the second largest outside the United States.

name: Richmond Virginia Temple
description: The Richmond Virginia Temple is located on a 12-acre wooded property at the intersection of Staples Mill Road and Mountain Road in Henrico County. Its architectural style combines elements of Georgian, Federal, and Jeffersonian design, with landscaping inspired by the historic gardens of Williamsburg, Virginia. The temple grounds feature local flora, including dogwood, magnolia, and Virginia bluebells, with dogwood motifs incorporated throughout the temple. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson, the Richmond Virginia Temple is the first of its kind in Virginia and was dedicated on May 7, 2023, by President Dallin H. Oaks. The temple's design includes Moleanos stone, art glass from The Richardson Design Partnership, and various decorative elements reflecting early American aesthetics.

name: Rio de Janeiro Brazil Temple
city: Barra Da Tijuca - Rio De Janeiro
description: The Rio de Janeiro Brazil Temple is situated adjacent to a nature reserve on Avenida das Américas in the Barra da Tijuca neighborhood, part of Rio de Janeiro's West Zone. This area, known for its modern development along the Atlantic Ocean, was a key location for the 2016 Summer Olympics. The temple, which is the eighth in Brazil and the first in Rio de Janeiro state, was announced by President Thomas S. Monson on April 6, 2013. Groundbreaking took place on March 4, 2017, with Elder Claudio R. M. Costa presiding over the ceremony. After delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the temple opened for public tours from March 26 to April 30, 2022, and was dedicated by Elder Gary E. Stevenson on May 8, 2022.

name: Rivera Uruguay Temple
description: The Rivera Uruguay Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the second in Uruguay, following the Montevideo Uruguay Temple, which was dedicated in March 2001 by President Gordon B. Hinckley. Rivera serves as the capital of the Rivera Department and is adjacent to the Brazilian city of Santana do Livramento, together forming an urban area of approximately 200,000 residents. Uruguay is home to nearly 110,000 Latter-day Saints across about 130 congregations.

name: Roanoke Virginia Temple
description: The Roanoke Virginia Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced. An official rendering has not yet been made public. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for the temple during the October 2023 General Conference. This temple will be the third in Virginia, following the dedication of the Richmond Virginia Temple on May 7, 2023, and the announcement of the Winchester Virginia Temple on April 2, 2023. At the time of the announcement, Virginia had over 97,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 210 congregations.

name: Rome Italy Temple
description: The Rome Italy Temple is located on a 15-acre elevated site in northeast Rome, close to the Grande Raccordo Anulare. This scenic area, previously home to a quaint villetta, features Roman pines and olive trees. It includes a stake center, visitors' center, family history center, and accommodation center. As the first temple in Italy and the thirteenth in Europe, it was dedicated in March 2019 by President Russell M. Nelson, marking a historic gathering of the First Presidency and Quorum of the Twelve Apostles outside the United States. The temple's design incorporates Italian materials, including Bianco Sardo granite and Perlato Svevo marble, and features artistic elements inspired by Michelangelo.

name: Rosario Argentina Temple
description: The Rosario Argentina Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build the temple during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the seventh in Argentina, joining existing temples in Bahía Blanca, Buenos Aires, Buenos Aires City Center, Córdoba, Mendoza, and Salta. Rosario is situated in east-central Argentina, about 190 miles northwest of Buenos Aires. At the time of the announcement, there were over 480,000 Latter-day Saints in more than 725 congregations across the country.

name: Russia Temple
description: The Russia Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no date set for groundbreaking. Renderings and site plans have not been made public, and the specific city for the temple's location has not been disclosed. There are three cities in Russia with organized stakes: Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Saratov. President Russell M. Nelson announced the establishment of Russia's first temple during the 188th Annual General Conference, but did not specify a city. The Russia Temple will be the first temple in Russia and the fifteenth in Europe.

name: Sacramento California Temple
description: The Sacramento California Temple is situated on a significant piece of Church-owned land that also includes a meetinghouse in the Folsom California Stake, overlooking Lake Natoma. This site, located off Highway 50 in Rancho Cordova, was previously owned by Aerojet General Corp. and acquired by the Church in 1971. The temple, which is the seventh in California and the second in the Central Valley, was announced on December 21, 2001, and its design was adapted from the Redlands and Newport Beach California Temples. Groundbreaking took place on August 22, 2004, led by President Gordon B. Hinckley, and the temple features a light gray granite exterior with a single spire topped by an angel Moroni statue. The public open house attracted 168,367 visitors, highlighting the community's excitement for a temple in Sacramento.

name: Salt Lake Temple
description: The Salt Lake Temple, located in Salt Lake City, was announced to close for renovations on December 29, 2019, for an estimated four years. President Russell M. Nelson revealed on March 12, 2021, that changes to the temple's interior would enhance its capacity and potentially extend the closure. The temple, a significant symbol of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, features distinctive spires and is situated on Temple Square, surrounded by various church facilities. Originally dedicated on April 6, 1893, the Salt Lake Temple is the largest temple of the Church and has undergone multiple renovations since its completion. The ongoing restoration includes the addition of a second baptistry and aims to preserve the temple's historical and architectural significance.

name: Salta Argentina Temple
address: Av. Ingeniero Mario Saul Banchik Nº 6050 (ex RN 51 km 4)
description: The Salta Argentina Temple is the third temple established in Argentina, following the Buenos Aires Argentina Temple (1986) and the Córdoba Argentina Temple (2015). Announced during the April 2018 General Conference, it serves members in the Argentine Northwest who previously traveled to Córdoba for temple services. The temple is located on a large grassy area at the entrance to El Aybal Country Club, near the airport in southern Salta. Groundbreaking took place on November 4, 2020, with Elder D. Todd Christofferson dedicating the temple on June 16, 2024. Its architecture features local design elements, including the cardon cactus flower and guarda pampa patterns, with a color palette inspired by the region's landscape.

name: Salvador Brazil Temple
description: The Salvador Brazil Temple will be the eleventh temple established in Brazil. President Russell M. Nelson announced its construction on October 7, 2018, during the 188th Semiannual General Conference. At that time, Brazil had the third-largest population of Latter-day Saints, totaling 1.39 million members. The temple is situated on a knoll in the Patamares neighborhood, easily accessible from major routes and close to the Luís Eduardo Magalhães International Airport. The temple will feature Portuguese colonial-style architecture and is set to open for public tours from August 22 to September 7, 2024, with its dedication scheduled for October 20, 2024.

name: San Antonio Texas Temple
description: The San Antonio Texas Temple is the fourth temple established in Texas, following the Dallas Texas Temple (1984), Houston Texas Temple (2000), and Lubbock Texas Temple (2002). The groundbreaking took place on March 29, 2003, coinciding with the Helsinki Finland Temple's groundbreaking. A 13-foot gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni was installed atop the temple on September 21, 2004, marking the 181st anniversary of Moroni's first appearance to Joseph Smith. During its open house, over 50,000 visitors toured the temple, including missionaries from San Antonio-based Evidence Ministries. The dedication festivities included a cultural celebration at the Alamodome, attended by 20,000 people, featuring performances that highlighted Texas history and family values.

name: San Diego California Temple
description: The San Diego California Temple closed on July 31, 2023, for significant renovations. A public open house and rededication will be scheduled after the renovations are finished. During this period, Church members in Southern California are encouraged to visit other nearby temples. Located near La Jolla, the temple features two prominent towers and a star-shaped atrium with a vibrant garden. The San Diego California Temple, the third temple built in California, was dedicated by President Gordon B. Hinckley in 1993 after a widely attended open house.

name: San Jose California Temple
description: The San Jose California Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The location has been confirmed as a 4.73-acre site at 771 West Fremont Avenue in Sunnyvale, where an existing meetinghouse is situated. The temple will be a single-story structure, approximately 30,000 square feet, accompanied by a distribution center. Plans for the temple were announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the April 2023 General Conference, marking it as the 11th temple for California. San Jose, part of Silicon Valley and the third-largest city in California, has a significant Church presence with nearly 730,000 members across about 1,150 congregations.

name: San Jose del Monte Philippines Temple
photoCaption: San Jose del Monte Philippines Temple
description: The San Jose del Monte Philippines Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the 14th in the Philippines, where there are over 880,000 Latter-day Saints across approximately 1,325 congregations. The country currently has 13 other temples either announced, under construction, or in operation. Since the introduction of missionary work in 1961, the Church has experienced rapid growth in the Philippines.

name: San José Costa Rica Temple
address: Del Hotel Marriott 1.2 km al Oeste La Ribera
description: The San José Costa Rica Temple is the first temple in Costa Rica and the second in Central America, following the Guatemala City Guatemala Temple, which was completed in 1984. The groundbreaking ceremony took place simultaneously with the Copenhagen Denmark Temple's groundbreaking. This temple was dedicated on the same day as the Montreal Quebec Temple. It serves a district that encompasses five stakes and seventeen districts across Costa Rica, Nicaragua, and Panama, with approximately 32,000 members. The temple features an exterior of Blanco Guardiano white marble from Torreón, Mexico, and includes a single attached spire topped with a statue of the angel Moroni.

name: San Juan Puerto Rico Temple
description: The San Juan Puerto Rico Temple is situated on a small hill near the Expreso Trujillo Alto highway, making it a central point for the San Juan metropolitan area. This site has historically served as a center for Church activities, previously housing the offices for the Puerto Rico San Juan Mission and the Caribbean Area. The temple, which was built on the former site of the Trujillo Alto Ward meetinghouse, is the third temple in the Caribbean, following the Santo Domingo Dominican Republic Temple and the Port-au-Prince Haiti Temple. Groundbreaking took place on May 4, 2019, and the temple was dedicated on January 15, 2023, by Elder D. Todd Christofferson. The architectural style reflects Spanish Colonial influences, with a combination of local materials and design elements that honor the island's heritage.

name: San Luis Potosí Mexico Temple
description: The San Luis Potosí Mexico Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony on Saturday, March 9, 2024, presided over by Elder Sean Douglas, a General Authority Seventy. This temple will cover 9,300 square feet and be situated on a 3.87-acre site across from Parque Morales in San Luis Potosí. The announcement for the temple was made in April 2022, with the site location revealed in October 2022. The official exterior rendering was released on February 5, 2024, coinciding with the groundbreaking announcement. This temple will be the 18th in Mexico, joining 17 others already established in the country.

name: San Pedro Sula Honduras Temple
address: Blvd. Jose Antonio Peraza Frente a Academia Americana al lado de Torre Banco del País Rumbo al Hospital Catarino Rivas
description: The San Pedro Sula Honduras Temple is the eighth temple in Central America and the second in Honduras, following the Tegucigalpa Honduras Temple, which was completed in 2013. Groundbreaking took place on September 5, 2020, with Elder José Bernardo Hernández presiding over the ceremony. President Russell M. Nelson announced the temple's construction on April 7, 2019, during General Conference. The temple is located on Bulevar Mario Catarino Rivas in the northwest section of San Pedro Sula and features Moleanos limestone from Portugal. A public open house is scheduled from September 12 to September 28, 2024, with the dedication set for October 13, 2024, led by Elder Dale G. Renlund.

name: San Salvador El Salvador Temple
address: Avenida El Espino y Calle El Pedregal Colonia San Benito
description: The San Salvador El Salvador Temple is located in the affluent Antiguo Cuscatlán district, overlooking Avenida El Espino near the Multiplaza Panamericana Mall. It includes a meetinghouse, a patron housing facility, a residence for the temple president, a cafeteria, and Distribution Services. The temple is set amidst lush grounds that provide a peaceful retreat for the people of El Salvador. This temple was the first in El Salvador and the fourth in Central America, following the Guatemala City Guatemala Temple, the San José Costa Rica Temple, and the Panamá City Panamá Temple. Dedicated on the 84th birthday of President Thomas S. Monson, the temple features Spanish colonial architectural elements, including a central spire topped with an angel Moroni statue, and incorporates motifs of the Flor de Izote, the national flower of El Salvador.

name: Santa Ana El Salvador Temple
description: The Santa Ana El Salvador Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for this temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the second in El Salvador, following the dedication of the San Salvador El Salvador Temple in August 2011. Santa Ana, located in the northwestern part of the country, is the second-largest city in El Salvador. The nation has nearly 130,000 members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints across approximately 55 congregations.

name: Santa Cruz Bolivia Temple
address: Avenida Quinto Anilla y Santa Rosa
description: The Santa Cruz Bolivia Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on June 8, 2024, led by Elder Jorge F. Zeballos, President of the South America Northwest Area. The event was attended by the mayor of Santa Cruz and various civic and religious leaders. The temple, which will cover 29,000 square feet, is located at the intersection of Avenida Quinto Anilla and Santa Rosa (Avenida Radial 27). The announcement for the temple's construction was made by President Russell M. Nelson during the General Conference on October 4, 2020. Currently, members of the Church in Santa Cruz travel 10 hours to reach the Cochabamba Bolivia Temple.

name: Santiago Chile Temple
description: The Santiago Chile Temple is located in the Providencia district of Santiago, known locally as "Temple Square." The site includes a meetinghouse, area offices, a distribution center, mission headquarters, and patron housing, all surrounded by mature trees and beautiful gardens featuring a central water fountain. Notable aspects of the temple are the hand-carved wainscoting, copíhue motifs on door handles and art-glass windows, and the use of inlaid Chilean marble and lapislázuli in the baptistry and entryway. Dedicated on September 15, 1983, by President Gordon B. Hinckley, it was the first temple built in Chile and the first in a Spanish-speaking country, serving 140,000 members at that time. Following extensive renovations, the temple was rededicated in 2006, with attendance surpassing expectations, and it now serves over 535,000 members.

name: Santiago Dominican Republic Temple
description: The Santiago Dominican Republic Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. This temple will be the second in the Dominican Republic, which is home to nearly 150,000 Latter-day Saints across about 200 congregations. Santiago is the country's second largest city. The first temple, located in Santo Domingo, was dedicated in 2000.

name: Santiago Philippines Temple
description: The Santiago Philippines Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. An official rendering of the temple has not yet been made public. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build the Santiago Philippines Temple during the October 2022 General Conference. This temple will be the tenth for the Philippines, which already has nine temples that are either announced, under construction, or dedicated, including the Alabang, Bacolod, Cagayan de Oro, Cebu City, Davao, Manila, Naga, Tacloban City, and Urdaneta temples. The temple is situated approximately 225 miles northeast of Manila.

name: Santiago West Chile Temple
address: Primo de Rivera 1551 Comuna de Maipu
description: The Santiago West Chile Temple is set to be built following a groundbreaking ceremony led by Elder Alan R. Walker on August 17, 2024. The event was attended by around 200 Church members, community leaders, and invited guests. The temple's location was announced on December 19, 2022, at Primo de Rivera 1551 in the Comuna de Maipu neighborhood of Santiago. This temple will be approximately 12,500 square feet and is the fourth temple in Chile, following the Santiago Chile Temple, Concepción Chile Temple, and the Antofagasta Chile Temple. The announcement of the Santiago West Chile Temple coincided with the 38th anniversary of the Santiago Chile Temple.

name: Santo Domingo Dominican Republic Temple
description: The Santo Domingo Dominican Republic Temple is situated on a slightly elevated, tree-covered site in an upscale area just minutes from downtown Santo Domingo, adjacent to the National Music Conservatory. This public site provides a stunning view of the Caribbean Sea to the south. It was the first temple established in both the Caribbean and the Dominican Republic. During the groundbreaking ceremony, Elder Scott encouraged members to keep a temple recommend and to prioritize Christ in their lives. Elder F. Burton Howard highlighted the importance of family connections, referencing a group of missionaries who had traveled three miles to attend the ceremony, separated from their families by a rope barrier, which he used to illustrate the significance of temples in uniting families.

name: Santos Brazil Temple
description: The Santos Brazil Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date announced yet. The temple will cover 23,000 square feet and will be built at the site of the Jabaquara Ward meetinghouse, located at Avenida Doutor Waldemar Leão, 305, in Santos' Jabaquara neighborhood. The location was revealed on November 28, 2022, following President Russell M. Nelson's announcement of the temple's construction during the April 2022 General Conference. This temple will be the 16th in Brazil, where there are approximately 1.5 million Latter-day Saints across more than 2,100 congregations. At the time of the announcement, several other temples were either completed or under construction in various Brazilian cities.

name: Sapporo Japan Temple
description: The Sapporo Japan Temple serves as a central feature within a complex that includes an arrival center, patron housing, missionary housing, and future meetinghouse space. Its design reflects Japanese culture, showcasing unique trees, large stones, and a picturesque pond with a waterfall connected by a pedestrian bridge. This temple is the eighth in Asia and the third in Japan, following the Tokyo Japan Temple and the Fukuoka Japan Temple. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on October 22, 2011, with Elder Gary E. Stevenson presiding, and the temple was dedicated on August 21, 2016, by President Russell M. Nelson. The temple's location along the Atsubetsu River offers easy access and is near Hokusei Gakuen University.

name: Saratoga Springs Utah Temple
description: The Saratoga Springs Utah Temple is situated on a 22.71-acre site near Utah Lake, accessible via Founders Boulevard. Its design harmonizes with the tranquil mountains and wetlands nearby, featuring a tiered water feature and landscaped gardens. Announced by President Thomas S. Monson on April 2, 2017, it is the eighteenth temple in Utah and the fifth in Utah County. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on October 19, 2019, and the temple was dedicated on August 13, 2023, by President Henry B. Eyring. The temple's architecture includes beige concrete, art glass inspired by nature, and various decorative elements reflecting local flora and landscapes.

name: Savai'i Samoa Temple
description: The Savai'i Samoa Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple will be situated on a 5.5-acre site adjacent to Don Bosco College and Vocational Technical Center in Fataloa, Salelologa village, on Savai'i's southeast coast. Announced on October 1, 2023, by President Russell M. Nelson during the General Conference, this temple will be approximately 29,630 square feet and is the second in Samoa, following the Apia Samoa Temple, which was dedicated in 1983 and rededicated in 2005 after a fire. At the time of the announcement, Samoa was home to over 85,000 Latter-day Saints. The Pago Pago American Samoa Temple is also under construction in the nearby American Samoa.

name: Seattle Washington Temple
description: The Seattle Washington Temple is situated off I-90 on a gently sloping hill opposite Bellevue College in Bellevue, Washington. Its attractive landscaping includes a cascading water feature, family-themed statues, and vibrant flowers, hedges, and trees, all surrounded by a grove of Washington evergreens. This temple was the first to be established in the Pacific Northwest and was initially known simply as the Seattle Temple. It is one of only five temples that feature an angel Moroni statue holding the gold plates. The temple was dedicated by President Spencer W. Kimball, marking his last dedication before his passing in November 1985.

name: Seoul Korea Temple
description: The Seoul Korea Temple is situated on a hill that provides views of Ewha Womans University, Yonsei University, and Sogang University. To the north lies the expressway leading to Gimpo International Airport, the second largest airport in Korea. Visitors can utilize dormitory accommodations in an auxiliary building, and the temple is surrounded by serene gardens open to the public. This temple was the first to be constructed in mainland Asia and South Korea, with its land dedicated on August 2, 1955, by President Joseph Fielding Smith. Plans for the temple were announced in 1981, and it underwent multiple redesigns due to the significant contributions from Korean Saints, culminating in its dedication as the 37th temple in operation.

name: Shanghai People’s Republic of China Temple
Singapore Temple
description: The Singapore Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony presided over by Elder Kelly R. Johnson, First Counselor in the Asia Area Presidency, on June 28, 2025. It will be situated on a one-acre plot at 233 Pasir Panjang Road, where a previous building has been demolished. This temple marks the first of its kind in Singapore, which is home to over 3,200 Latter-day Saints. Plans for the temple were announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021. Additionally, a meetinghouse with an arrival center will be constructed behind the temple.

name: Smithfield Utah Temple
description: The Smithfield Utah Temple is set to be constructed in a beautiful valley surrounded by mountains. Elder Quentin L. Cook and Elder Gary E. Stevenson, both from the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles and raised in Cache Valley, attended the groundbreaking ceremony. This temple will be built on a 13.3-acre site at the intersection of N 800 West and W 100 North, where the LaMont Poulsen family farmed for over 160 years. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 4, 2021, the three-story temple will span approximately 81,000 square feet and will be the second temple in Cache County, joining the Logan Utah Temple, dedicated in 1884. The Smithfield Utah Temple is the 26th temple announced in Utah, where about two-thirds of the state's population are members of the Church.

name: Snowflake Arizona Temple
description: The Snowflake Arizona Temple is situated on a bluff known as "Temple Hill," adjacent to a golf course at the western edge of Snowflake. To create space for the two-level temple, approximately 8 feet of earth was removed from the knoll, with part of the structure set into the ground. The temple features a rustic water feature at the lower parking level, aligned with the entrance. Groundbreaking for the temple took place on September 23, 2000, and it is the second temple established in Arizona, following the Mesa Arizona Temple. The interior design incorporates elements reflecting local history and culture, including pioneer-style furniture and Native American motifs.

name: Spanish Fork Utah Temple
description: The Spanish Fork Utah Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date announced yet. An official site location and rendering for the temple have not been disclosed. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans on April 6, 2025, during the 195th Annual General Conference. This temple will be the ninth in Utah County and the thirty-second in the state. Spanish Fork, located in southern Utah Valley, was settled by Latter-day Saints in 1851 and has a population of about 50,000 residents.

name: Spokane Washington Temple
description: The Spokane Washington Temple is the second temple established in Washington, following the Seattle Washington Temple, which was completed in 1980. The groundbreaking for the Spokane Washington Temple took place on the same day as the Detroit Michigan Temple, marking a historic event. In April 1999, Brother Rush Hashid transported the angel Moroni statue and other items to the temple site, unaware of their significance until arrival. In March 2009, a new angel Moroni statue was installed, facing west, in contrast to the original statue's eastward orientation. On August 22, 2009, to celebrate the temple's 10th anniversary, members of the Spokane Washington East Stake filled every seat for the entire day.

name: Springfield Missouri Temple
description: The Springfield Missouri Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The temple's location was announced on June 24, 2024, on a 38-acre site at 2720 East Farm Road #188 in Springfield. An exterior rendering was made public on December 16, 2024. The temple will be a single-story structure, approximately 29,000 square feet in size. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the April 2023 General Conference, marking it as the third temple for Missouri.

name: St. George Utah Temple
description: The St. George Utah Temple, situated near the historic district of St. George, is a prominent white structure amidst the red sandstone buttes of Southern Utah. It features a public visitors' center that includes a replica of Thorvaldsen's Christus. As the first temple built in Utah Territory, it was dedicated on January 1, 1877, and is notable for being the first to perform endowments for the deceased. The temple underwent significant renovations, including a major project that began in November 2019, enhancing its facilities and grounds while preserving its historical elements. The St. George Utah Temple remains a vital site for members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, with a rich history and architectural significance.

name: St. Louis Missouri Temple
description: The St. Louis Missouri Temple is a notable site located on the North Outer Forty, near its intersection with I-270, in the suburb of Town and Country. The temple grounds are adorned with numerous trees and shrubs, leading to a serene entrance highlighted by a circular water feature. Visitors are encouraged to explore the landscaped gardens and experience the peaceful atmosphere surrounding this sacred building. As the first temple established in Missouri, its site was unanimously chosen by the First Presidency after reviewing six potential locations. The temple's groundbreaking attracted nearly 5,000 attendees, and its public open house welcomed around 260,000 visitors over four weeks, showcasing the community's strong interest and support.

name: St. Paul Minnesota Temple
description: The St. Paul Minnesota Temple is the first temple established in Minnesota. Elder Hugh W. Pinnock, president of the North America Central Area, presided over the groundbreaking ceremony, emphasizing the temple's significance to the community. Construction was set to begin immediately, with expectations for the temple to be operational within a year. Elder Thomas A. Holt, an Area Authority Seventy and St. Paul resident, noted the long history of Latter-day Saints in Minnesota, dating back to 1847. The temple features a light gray granite veneer and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Star Valley Wyoming Temple
description: The Star Valley Wyoming Temple is situated on a rise overlooking Highway 89, near Afton and Hale Canyon. A notable aspect of the temple's foyer is a stained-glass representation of Jesus Christ, originally made for a Presbyterian Church in New York City. This temple, the first in Wyoming, reflects classical architectural styles similar to those of the historic Star Valley Tabernacle located nearby. Plans for the temple were announced by President Thomas S. Monson during the October 2011 General Conference, generating excitement within the community. The temple was dedicated on October 30, 2016, by Elder David A. Bednar, marking a significant milestone for the Latter-day Saint community in the region.

name: Stockholm Sweden Temple
description: The Stockholm Sweden Temple closed on March 25, 2023, for a reconstruction project expected to take around three years. The temple's size will increase significantly from 16,366 square feet to approximately 31,000 square feet, including two instruction rooms with 40 seats each for endowment presentations. After renovations, the public will have the opportunity to tour the temple during an open house prior to its rededication.
