Located in Västerhaninge, about 20 miles south of Stockholm, the temple is designed to reflect local architectural styles and is surrounded by beautiful landscaping and facilities. The Stockholm Sweden Temple was the first in the Nordic countries and the fourth built in Europe, with its dedication marking a significant moment in the history of the Church in Scandinavia.

name: Summit New Jersey Temple
description: The Summit New Jersey Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build this temple during the 194th Semiannual General Conference on October 6, 2024. It will be the first temple in New Jersey, serving approximately 35,000 Latter-day Saints across more than 60 congregations. The earliest missionary efforts in New Jersey began in 1832. Currently, the nearest temples for local members are the Manhattan New York Temple and the Philadelphia Pennsylvania Temple.

name: Suva Fiji Temple
description: The Suva Fiji Temple is situated near the Samabula Chapel, just a short distance from downtown Suva, the capital of Fiji. Perched on one of the city's highest points, it offers views of the Pacific Ocean on three sides. This temple was the first to be established in Melanesia, serving the 12,000 members from Viti Levu and nearby islands who previously traveled to temples in Tonga, Samoa, or New Zealand. The groundbreaking took place on May 8, 1999, with Elder Earl M. Monson presiding. After significant renovations due to water damage, the temple was rededicated by President Henry B. Eyring on February 21, 2016, following an open house that attracted around 22,000 visitors.

name: Sydney Australia Temple
address: 756 Pennant Hills Road Corner Pennant Hills Rd & Moseley St.
description: The Sydney Australia Temple is situated in Carlingford, approximately 12 miles northwest of Sydney's city center. Its serene environment is enhanced by award-winning landscaping, featuring large eucalyptus trees that provide year-round beauty. This temple, the first in Australia, shares its grounds with Church administrative offices and a patron housing facility, and was built on land previously used as a boys' school. The groundbreaking ceremony was led by Elder Bruce R. McConkie of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, who later expressed hope for more temples in Australia, a vision that became reality with the construction of several others. During its public open house in September 1984, thousands of Australians visited, leading to significant interest in the Church.

name: Syracuse Utah Temple
description: The Syracuse Utah Temple is located on a 12-acre site amidst farmland, positioned between the Great Salt Lake and Interstate 15. The temple's design incorporates local flora, such as snowball sand-verbena and desert paintbrush, with art glass reflecting the lake's colors, highlighting Syracuse's identity as the "Gateway to Antelope Island." Announced at the General Conference on April 5, 2020, by President Russell M. Nelson, it is the 24th temple in Utah and the third in Davis County, following the Bountiful and Layton temples. Groundbreaking took place on June 12, 2021, and the temple was dedicated on June 8, 2025, by President Nelson. The structure features a steel frame with a White Moncini granite exterior and spans approximately 89,000 square feet.

name: São Paulo Brazil Temple
description: The São Paulo Brazil Temple is located in one of the world's largest cities, set on a beautifully landscaped site in the western part of São Paulo, close to a major shopping mall and Metro station. The temple grounds include a visitors' center, accommodation center, stake center, and offices for the Brazil Area, featuring a decorative fountain and vibrant flowerbeds. As the first temple established in South America, it was originally named the São Paulo Temple and was dedicated in 1978, when there were only 15 stakes and approximately 54,000 members in Brazil. Following its dedication, Church membership surged to over 300,000 within 12 years, leading to the establishment of South America's first missionary training center in São Paulo. The temple underwent significant renovations, culminating in its rededication in 2004, which coincided with a membership increase to over 867,000 in Brazil.

name: São Paulo East Brazil Temple
description: The São Paulo East Brazil Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date announced yet. The temple will be situated on a 10.7-acre site at Av. Guilherme Giorgi, 1091 in Vila Carrão. It is designed to be a two-story structure covering approximately 46,050 square feet. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 4, 2020, this temple will be the twelfth in Brazil and the third in São Paulo, joining the existing São Paulo Brazil Temple and the Campinas Brazil Temple. The announcement coincided with the 42nd anniversary of the São Paulo Brazil Temple.

name: Tacloban City Philippines Temple
description: The Tacloban City Philippines Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on January 18, 2025, led by Elder Michael B. Strong, Second Counselor in the Philippines Area Presidency. He highlighted the baptism of George Pamin, the first Church member in Tacloban, which occurred 56 years prior. The temple will be built on a scenic 6.99-acre site along Tacloban Bypass Road, featuring a two-story structure of about 21,407 square feet, along with an ancillary building for various services. The temple is part of a broader initiative, as President Russell M. Nelson announced its construction during the October 2021 General Conference. This will be the eighth temple in the Philippines, joining two existing temples and five others that are either announced or under construction.

name: Tacoma Washington Temple
description: The Tacoma Washington Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple's location was announced on September 16, 2024, as an 11.6-acre site at approximately 1405 South 364th Way in Federal Way. An official exterior rendering was made public on December 23, 2024, showcasing a multistory building of about 45,000 square feet, along with a utility building. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the October 2022 General Conference. This temple will be the fifth in Washington, which has over 280,000 Latter-day Saints across nearly 525 congregations.

name: Taipei Taiwan Temple
description: The Taipei Taiwan Temple is located just east of the National Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall on Ai-Kuo (Love of Country) Road. It is notable for its elegant design and tall spires, surrounded by mature trees, terraced landscaping, and a series of fountains. This temple was the first built in Taiwan and the third in Asia. During its open house, over 20,000 visitors, including government officials and religious leaders, toured the temple, which features a distinctive blue tile roof that harmonizes with the nearby memorial hall. At the time of its dedication, there were three stakes in Taiwan, which grew to ten stakes and two districts over the next twenty-five years.

name: Tallahassee Florida Temple
description: The Tallahassee Florida Temple of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints will host a public open house from November 4 to November 23, 2024, excluding Sundays. Prior to the public tours, a media day is scheduled for October 28, followed by two days for invited guests. The temple will be dedicated by Elder Patrick Kearon of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on December 8, 2024, at 9:00 a.m. local time. Located at 2440 Papillion Way, the temple spans 29,000 square feet on a 4.97-acre site and is the third temple in Florida, joining the Orlando and Fort Lauderdale temples. Groundbreaking for the temple took place on June 5, 2021, presided over by Elder James B. Martino.

name: Tampa Florida Temple
description: The Tampa Florida Temple will be constructed following a groundbreaking ceremony led by Elder Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on August 23, 2025. Elder Andersen offered a dedicatory prayer, seeking blessings for the temple and the surrounding community. An exterior rendering of the temple was made public on March 20, 2023, and a new site was announced on April 22, 2024, at 9445 Camden Fields Parkway in Riverview, Florida, covering 12 acres. This single-story temple will span approximately 29,000 square feet. The Tampa Florida Temple, the fourth in the state, was first announced by President Russell M. Nelson on April 3, 2022, during the General Conference.

name: Tampico Mexico Temple
address: Av. Ejercito Mexicano #74 Con 3A Av. Colonia Loma del Gallo
description: The Tampico México Temple is a response to the significant growth of membership in the region. Over the past 25 years, the number of stakes in Tampico has increased from one to four. The temple district serves approximately 18,000 members, organized into four stakes, three districts, and the Mexico Tampico Mission. This new temple will greatly lessen travel costs for members residing in Madero and Tampico, who previously faced a challenging 500-mile journey to the México City México Temple. The temple, which is the 83rd dedicated temple, features an exterior of Blanco Guardiano white marble from Torreón, Mexico, and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Tarawa Kiribati Temple
description: The Tarawa Kiribati Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on November 2, 2024, led by Elder Jeremy R. Jaggi, a General Authority Seventy. The event was attended by His Excellency Taneti Maamau, President of Kiribati, and First Lady Madam Teiraeng Maamau, and was broadcast live to allow member participation. The temple will be a single-story structure of about 10,000 square feet, featuring a single spire, with additional facilities planned 450 meters west of the site. Announced during the 190th Semiannual General Conference, this temple will be the first in Kiribati and the second in Micronesia, following the Yigo Guam Temple. Currently, nearly 21,000 Latter-day Saints in Kiribati travel over 1,000 miles to the Suva Fiji Temple for ordinance work.

name: Taylorsville Utah Temple
description: The Taylorsville Utah Temple is located on the west side of the Salt Lake Valley, along Interstate 215, on a site previously occupied by a Church meetinghouse and recreational field. Its design draws inspiration from local pioneer tabernacles, featuring exterior art glass that incorporates stylized local wildflowers and a color palette of deep burgundy, lavender, and gold, reflecting Gothic architectural influences. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 5, 2019, the temple is the twenty-first in Utah and the fifth in the Salt Lake Valley. The temple, which spans approximately 70,000 square feet, held its groundbreaking ceremony on October 31, 2020, and is set to open for public tours from April 13 to May 18, 2024, before its dedication on June 2, 2024. The architectural style is pioneer-era Gothic, with landscaping designed for water efficiency and a variety of decorative elements throughout the interior.

name: Tegucigalpa Honduras Temple
address: Residencial Roble Oeste Boulevard Roble Oeste 3ra Calle Sur.
description: The Tegucigalpa Honduras Temple is the first temple established in Honduras and the sixth in Central America. The First Presidency announced its construction in a letter dated June 9, 2006, which was shared with local members by Central America Area President Spencer V. Jones on June 18. Initially, groundbreaking took place on June 9, 2007, at a site near the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de Honduras, but construction was halted in January 2009 due to opposition from local officials regarding the temple's location. Following negotiations, the temple was relocated, and a new groundbreaking ceremony was held on September 12, 2009, near Toncontín International Airport. The temple features mountain gray granite from China and includes a single central spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Teresina Brazil Temple
address: Av. Raul Lopes and Rua Des. Pedro Conde Noivos
description: The Teresina Brazil Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. An official exterior rendering was made public on February 12, 2024. The temple will be situated on a 3.6-acre site at the intersection of Av. Raul Lopes and Rua Des. Pedro Conde in the Noivos neighborhood of Teresina. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the April 2023 General Conference, the temple will cover approximately 25,420 square feet. Teresina is the capital of Piauí and is part of a metropolitan area with nearly one million residents.

name: Teton River Idaho Temple
description: The Teton River Idaho Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony presided over by Elder Ricardo P. Giménez on June 1, 2024. This temple will be situated on a 16.6-acre site in Rexburg, northwest of Second East and 2000 North, and will feature a three-story building of approximately 100,000 square feet. The temple's location was announced on September 19, 2022, and its exterior rendering was revealed on February 20, 2024. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the October 2021 General Conference, the Teton River Idaho Temple will be the ninth temple in Idaho. Rexburg, with a population of around 39,500, will become the sixth city globally to host more than one temple, alongside the existing Rexburg Idaho Temple.

name: The Gila Valley Arizona Temple
description: The Gila Valley Arizona Temple is located at the base of Mount Graham in Central, Arizona, along Highway 70. This temple serves the faithful members of southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico, significantly reducing travel distances for many who previously attended the Mesa Arizona Temple or the Albuquerque New Mexico Temple. It was the third temple established in Arizona, following the Mesa Arizona Temple and the Snowflake Arizona Temple. The groundbreaking took place on February 14, 2009, coinciding with the 97th anniversary of Arizona's statehood, and was presided over by Elder Neil L. Andersen. The temple features a single spire topped with a gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni and is designed to accommodate approximately 32,000 members from seven stakes in the region.

name: The Hague Netherlands Temple
description: The Hague Netherlands Temple is the eighth temple established in Europe and the first in the Netherlands. To make way for its construction, an existing church building was demolished, as local regulations permitted only one structure on the site, which is situated in a city park. Located in Zoetermeer, which means "Sweet Lake," the temple is often referred to as the "Sweet Lake Temple." The temple is positioned below sea level, and due to the high value of land in the Netherlands, the Church acquired a parcel slightly larger than the building's footprint. A parking structure for 40 cars and bicycles was built underground to provide parking under the Church's control. President Gordon B. Hinckley dedicated the temple the day after rededicating the Freiberg Germany Temple.

name: Tijuana Mexico Temple
address: Paseo Del Rio 6832 Esquina Campestre Oriente Col 3 RA Etapa Rio Tijuana
description: The Tijuana Mexico Temple is located in southeastern Tijuana on Paseo del Río, near Cerro Colorado, which features the inscription "JESUCRISTO ES EL SEÑOR" at its peak. Its design showcases Spanish Colonial architecture, reminiscent of the Spanish missions in Mexico and the southwestern United States. The temple's striking white exterior, topped with a central tower, symbolizes its sacred purpose, while the grounds are adorned with palm trees, a tiered fountain, and vibrant landscaping. Announced by President Thomas S. Monson on October 2, 2010, the temple was the first in Baja California and the thirteenth in Mexico, with its groundbreaking held on August 18, 2012. President Dieter F. Uchtdorf dedicated the temple on December 13, 2015, during a ceremony that included thousands of participants across the country.

name: Tokyo Japan Temple
description: The Tokyo Japan Temple is situated in a beautiful residential area of Tokyo, directly across from the historic Arisugawa Memorial Park. This location was selected for its proximity to schools and embassies, with convenient access just a five-minute walk from Hiroo subway station. The temple, which was the first built in Japan and on the Asian continent, was originally named the Tokyo Temple until it was renamed in 1999. The temple features a four-story annex that serves multiple functions, including a meetinghouse and patron housing. After a significant renovation that began in 2017, the temple was rededicated on July 3, 2022, enhancing its facilities and design to reflect traditional Japanese aesthetics.

name: Toluca Mexico Temple
address: Calle Guadalupe Victória and Calle Uruapán Colonia Las Jaras
description: The Toluca Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The temple's location was announced on November 20, 2023, as a 4.87-acre site at the intersection of Calle Guadalupe Victoria and Calle Uruapan in the Colonia Las Jaras neighborhood of Metepec, southeast of Toluca. An official exterior rendering was made public on December 23, 2024. The design includes a single-story structure of approximately 19,000 square feet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the October 2022 General Conference.

name: Toronto Ontario Temple
description: The Toronto Ontario Temple is located in a picturesque residential area of Brampton, a suburb approximately 20 miles west of downtown Toronto. The temple features a striking 105-foot spire and is oriented towards the intersection of Bramalea Road and Bovaird Drive. It was the second temple established in Canada, following the Cardston Alberta Temple, and the first in Ontario, with its design inspired by the Denver Colorado Temple. The temple was announced on June 22, 1986, and officially dedicated from August 25 to 27, 1990, with services translated into multiple languages to accommodate the diverse community. Renovations began in October 2023 and were completed in December 2024, leading to a rededication on March 23, 2025, by President Jeffrey R. Holland.

name: Torreón Mexico Temple
description: The Torreón Mexico Temple is set to be built in Gómez Palacio, with groundbreaking services led by Elder Hugo Montoya on December 10, 2022. This single-story temple will cover approximately 10,000 square feet and will be located on a 0.89-acre site at the intersection of Paris and Amsterdam Streets, across from an existing meetinghouse. Plans include an ancillary building for patron accommodations, a distribution center, and a residence for the temple president and matron, along with an expansion of the meetinghouse for an arrival center. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021, this temple will be the 16th in Mexico. The country has a significant Latter-day Saint population of about 1.5 million, with missionary work beginning in 1875.

name: Trujillo Peru Temple
address: Av. Mansiche Km 3.5 Carretera hacia Huanchaco Huanchaco
description: The Trujillo Peru Temple is situated near the Campo Eterno cemetery along the highway to Huanchaco, close to the historic Chan Chan ruins. An accommodation center is available on-site for visitors and workers, with plans for a future meetinghouse as well. This temple is the second in Peru, following the Lima Peru Temple, and was announced on December 13, 2008. Groundbreaking took place on September 14, 2011, led by Elder Rafael E. Pino. The temple was dedicated on June 21, 2015, by President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, serving over 88,000 members in the region.

name: Tucson Arizona Temple
description: The Tucson Arizona Temple is located in the Catalina Foothills, north of Tucson, Arizona, within the Sonoran Desert. The temple grounds feature landscaping that includes red cactus flowers, ocotillo plants, and prickly pear cacti, along with grassy areas for gatherings. A distinctive aspect of the temple is its blue central dome, made from zinc-based tile imported from Germany, topped with a gold-leafed statue of the angel Moroni. This temple is the sixth in Arizona, with its groundbreaking ceremony held on October 17, 2015, and it was dedicated on August 13, 2017, by President Dieter F. Uchtdorf. The temple has a total area of 34,000 square feet and includes a 260-space parking lot, designed to blend with the natural desert surroundings.

name: Tuguegarao City Philippines Temple
description: The Tuguegarao City Philippines Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The official rendering was made public on February 18, 2025, along with the announcement of its location on a 6.3-acre site near Tuguegarao City Hall, south of Enrile Avenue. The temple will be a single-story structure, approximately 18,850 square feet, and will include on-site patron housing and a distribution center. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the April 2023 General Conference, marking it as the 11th temple for the Philippines. Tuguegarao City, the capital of Cagayan province, is situated nearly 300 miles north of Manila, in a country with a population of around 114 million.

name: Tula Mexico Temple
description: The Tula Mexico Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. An official rendering of the temple has yet to be made public. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the plans for the Tula Mexico Temple during the October 2022 General Conference. Tula, or Tula de Allende, is an ancient city in Hidalgo, Mexico, situated approximately 60 miles north of Mexico City and home to around 100,000 residents. This temple will be the second in Hidalgo, a region historically recognized as the capital of the Toltec empire.

name: Tulsa Oklahoma Temple
description: The Tulsa Oklahoma Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple will be situated on a 25.7-acre site in southeast Tulsa, near Broken Arrow, as announced on August 12, 2024. It is designed to be a single-story structure covering approximately 29,600 square feet. This temple will be the second in Oklahoma, following the Oklahoma City Oklahoma Temple, which was dedicated in 2000. Plans for the Tulsa Oklahoma Temple were revealed by President Russell M. Nelson during the October 2023 General Conference.

name: Tuxtla Gutiérrez Mexico Temple
address: Carretera a Chicoasén Kilometro 1.4 Esq. Paseo de la Roseta Fraccionamiento San José Chapultepec
description: The Tuxtla Gutiérrez Mexico Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place alongside those for the Fresno California Temple, Fukuoka Japan Temple, and Melbourne Australia Temple. Tuxtla Gutiérrez, the capital of Chiapas, Mexico's southernmost state bordering Guatemala, is known for its numerous ancient ruins. Significant archaeological finds in the area include carved monuments, stone boxes, pottery, and incense burners. In 1957, Elder Howard W. Hunter dedicated the region for gospel preaching from Mactumatza, a mountain overlooking the city. Elder Richard E. Turley Sr. emphasized the importance of temple work during the ceremony, encouraging members to prepare for the temple's open house and to foster a culture of regular temple attendance.

name: Twin Falls Idaho Temple
description: The Twin Falls Idaho Temple is located just south of the Snake River Canyon in northeastern Twin Falls, making it the tallest structure in the area. Its design draws inspiration from the nearby Shoshone Falls, featuring a waterfall theme in its architecture, stained-glass windows, and landscaping, including waterfall features at the entrance. The temple, which is the fourth in Idaho, was announced in October 2004 after a request from local stake presidents for a temple in the region. Groundbreaking took place on April 15, 2006, and the temple was dedicated on August 30, 2008. The building showcases beautiful murals by local artist Leon Parson and incorporates a Syringa flower motif throughout, reflecting Idaho's state flower.

name: Ulaanbaatar Mongolia Temple
address: Naadamchid Road Khan Uul District 8th khoroo
description: The Ulaanbaatar Mongolia Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. On September 15, 2025, the temple's exterior rendering was made public, and its location was confirmed as an 11-acre site on Naadamchid Road in the 8th khoroo of the Khan Uul District, approximately 4.5 km east of the airport. The temple will be a single-story structure covering about 18,850 square feet, accompanied by a patron housing facility and a meetinghouse. This will be Mongolia's first temple, serving a growing community of over 12,000 Latter-day Saints across roughly 25 congregations since the arrival of missionaries in 1992. The nearest temple is currently located in Hong Kong, over 1,800 miles away.

name: Urdaneta Philippines Temple
description: The Urdaneta Philippines Temple will be dedicated by President Dallin H. Oaks, First Counselor in the First Presidency, on Sunday, April 28, 2024, with two dedicatory sessions at 10:00 a.m. and 1:30 p.m. Public tours of the temple will take place from March 15 to March 30, 2024, following a media day and guest tours in mid-March. Groundbreaking for the temple occurred on January 16, 2019, presided over by Elder Jeffrey R. Holland. This temple, the third in the Philippines, is located off the MacArthur Highway near Urdaneta City and will serve over 100 stakes and districts in the Luzon Island Group. The temple features a golden sand granite exterior, inspired by Spanish colonial architecture, and includes intricate designs that reflect Filipino cultural motifs.

name: Uturoa French Polynesia Temple
description: The Uturoa French Polynesia Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the construction plans during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the second in French Polynesia, joining the Papeete Tahiti Temple, which was dedicated in 1983 and rededicated in 2006 after expansion. At the time of the announcement, the Pacific Area was marking the 180th anniversary of the arrival of missionaries in Tahiti. There are nearly 30,000 Latter-day Saints across about 100 congregations in French Polynesia.

name: Uyo Nigeria Temple
description: The Uyo Nigeria Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build the temple during the 195th Annual General Conference on April 6, 2025. This temple will be the seventh in Nigeria, joining the operational Aba Nigeria Temple and five others currently in planning: Abuja, Benin City, Calabar, Eket, and Lagos. Nigeria has over 250,000 Latter-day Saints across nearly 850 congregations. The region is recognized as one of the fastest-growing areas for the Church globally.

name: Vancouver British Columbia Temple
description: The Vancouver British Columbia Temple is situated on an elevated site near the Trans-Canada Highway, north of Langley in Metro Vancouver. The property also includes the Langley meetinghouse and the residence of the temple president, along with a serene wooded area that enhances the temple grounds. This temple, the first in British Columbia and the seventh in Canada, was dedicated after local members previously traveled to the Seattle Washington Temple. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on August 4, 2007, led by Elder Ronald A. Rasband, marking the start of construction on this significant site. The temple features a distinctive spire topped with a gold-leafed angel Moroni statue and is built from Branco Siena granite sourced from Brazil.

name: Vancouver Washington Temple
address: SE 20th Street and SE Bybee Road
description: The Vancouver Washington Temple will be constructed following a groundbreaking ceremony led by Elder Mark A. Bragg, General Authority Seventy, on August 23, 2025. The temple will be situated on a 15.11-acre site in Camas, northwest of SE 20th Street and SE Bybee Road, and will feature a multistory design of approximately 43,000 square feet. The official exterior rendering was made public on September 3, 2024. President Russell M. Nelson announced the temple's construction during the October 2023 General Conference, marking it as the sixth temple in Washington state and the second in the Portland metropolitan area. Washington is home to over 280,000 Latter-day Saints across 489 congregations.

name: Veracruz Mexico Temple
address: Ave. Ejercito Mexicano Esq. Michoacan Colonia Luis Echeverria
description: The Veracruz Mexico Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place alongside those for the Adelaide Australia Temple and the Louisville Kentucky Temple. Elder Carl B. Pratt, president of the Mexico South Area, noted the strong Church presence in Veracruz, which includes four stakes in the city and four more within a hundred-mile radius. This temple will be the fifth in the area, significantly reducing travel costs for members previously needing to go to the Mexico City Mexico Temple. The temple is situated in a historic seaport established in the 16th century. Elder Octaviano Tenorio emphasized the importance of families and the blessings of eternal life made possible through temple ordinances.

name: Vernal Utah Temple
description: The Vernal Utah Temple is a significant landmark in the Ashley Valley, constructed within the historic Uintah Stake Tabernacle. Situated two blocks south of Main Street, its domes and the steeple of the nearby Vernal Utah Glines Stake Center are visible from Highway 191. This temple, the first to be built from an existing structure, was dedicated in 1997 after extensive renovations of the dilapidated tabernacle, which had not been used for stake conferences since 1983. The groundbreaking ceremony attracted nearly 12,000 attendees, and the temple features a unique two-stage endowment room due to the building's narrow design. The Vernal Utah Temple, marked with the years 1907 and 1997, symbolizes both its origins as a tabernacle and its transformation into a temple.

name: Victoria British Columbia Temple
description: The Victoria British Columbia Temple is set to be constructed on a 4.6-acre site at 2750 Leigh Road, following a unanimous zoning amendment approval by the Langford City Council on August 18, 2025. While no official site location or groundbreaking date has been disclosed, a conceptual exterior rendering and site plan were shared with the Langford Sustainable Development Advisory Committee on August 11, 2025. President Russell M. Nelson announced the plans for the temple during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the eleventh in Canada, joining existing temples in cities such as Calgary, Edmonton, and Vancouver. Victoria, the capital of British Columbia, is located on the southeastern tip of Vancouver Island and has a significant Latter-day Saint community.

name: Vienna Austria Temple
description: The Vienna Austria Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no date set for groundbreaking. The temple will be situated on a 0.80-acre site at Silbergasse 2 in Vienna, as announced on October 30, 2023. It is designed to be a multi-story structure, approximately 15,300 square feet in size. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021. This will be the first temple for the Church in Austria, which is home to around 5,000 Latter-day Saints.

name: Villahermosa Mexico Temple
address: Avenida 27 de Febrero #1717 Colonia Atasta de Serra
description: The Villahermosa Mexico Temple's groundbreaking ceremony took place on the same day as that of the Ciudad Juárez Mexico Temple. It was later dedicated on the same day as the Nashville Tennessee Temple. Situated near Mexico's isthmus, the temple is located in a region rich with ancient ruins, often associated with Book of Mormon lands. Elder Richard E. Turley Sr. presided over the groundbreaking, recalling his uncle Harold E. Turley, who had previously served in the area. The Villahermosa Mexico Temple, the 85th dedicated temple, features an exterior of Blanco Guardiano white marble and includes a single spire topped with an angel Moroni statue.

name: Vitória Brazil Temple
description: The Vitória Brazil Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set yet. The temple will be located at Avenida Leitão da Silva #2055 in the Iteraré neighborhood of Vitória, near the Santa Maria de Vitória River. Announced on February 27, 2023, the temple will cover 10,600 square feet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed plans for the temple during the October 2021 General Conference. This temple will be the 14th in Brazil, joining others such as the Belém and São Paulo temples.

name: Viña del Mar Chile Temple
description: The Viña del Mar Chile Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple will be situated on a 1.87-acre site where the Viña del Mar Chile Stake center currently stands, located between 3rd North Street and 4th North Street in Viña del Mar. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 1, 2023, the temple is expected to cover approximately 30,000 square feet. This temple will be the first in the Valparaíso region and the fifth in Chile, which has a significant Latter-day Saint population. Viña del Mar, the fourth-largest city in Chile, is part of the Valparaíso metropolitan area.

name: Washington D.C. Temple
description: The Washington D.C. Temple, located approximately 10 miles north of the U.S. Capitol in Kensington, Maryland, is a prominent landmark along the Capital Beltway. Its striking architecture is complemented by a reflection pond and a water feature at the entrance. The temple grounds include the Washington D.C. Stake Center and the Visitors' Center, which offers interactive exhibits and hosts events throughout the year, including the festive Festival of Lights during Christmas. As the first temple built in the Eastern United States, it features six spires and stands at 288 feet, making it the tallest temple in the Church. The temple's exterior is clad in white Alabama marble, symbolizing purity, and it includes intricate stained glass windows and bronze medallions that represent various spiritual themes.

name: Wellington New Zealand Temple
address: Near Okowai Road and Whitford Brown Avenue Aotea
description: The Wellington New Zealand Temple will have its groundbreaking ceremony presided over by Elder Taniela B. Wakolo, First Counselor in the Pacific Area Presidency, on August 2, 2025. It will be built on a 3.35-acre site near Okowai Road and Whitford Brown Avenue in Porirua's Aotea neighborhood. The temple will feature a two-story design, covering approximately 14,900 square feet, along with an ancillary building for arrival facilities and patron housing. The official exterior rendering was made public on June 17, 2024, following the announcement of the temple's location on November 28, 2022. This will be the third temple in New Zealand and the southernmost temple of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

name: West Jordan Utah Temple
description: The West Jordan Utah Temple is currently in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date set. The temple's location was announced on April 22, 2024, as a 16.1-acre site west of Highway 111 at approximately 7148 South. An official exterior rendering was made public on April 14, 2025, and the temple is designed to be a multi-story structure of about 85,000 square feet, accompanied by a new meetinghouse. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction plans during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the 29th in Utah, situated in West Jordan, a suburb of Salt Lake City.

name: Wichita Kansas Temple
description: The Wichita Kansas Temple held its groundbreaking ceremony on September 7, 2024, presided over by Elder Steven R. Bangerter, First Counselor in the North America Central Area Presidency. The temple will be situated on a 6.42-acre site on North Meridian Avenue in the Moorings Plaza development in northern Wichita. It will be a single-story structure covering approximately 9,950 square feet. President Russell M. Nelson announced the construction of the temple during the April 2022 General Conference, marking it as the first temple in Kansas. The state is home to over 38,000 Latter-day Saints across about 75 congregations, with Wichita being its largest city.

name: Willamette Valley Oregon Temple
description: The Willamette Valley Oregon Temple is being constructed following a groundbreaking ceremony led by Elder Valeri V. Cordón on October 29, 2022. This 30,000-square-foot temple will occupy a 10.5-acre site at the intersection of International Boulevard and Corporate Way in Springfield, Oregon. Construction commenced on October 31, 2022, with an expected completion timeframe of two to three years. The temple will be the third in Oregon, joining existing temples in Portland and Medford. Plans for the Willamette Valley Oregon Temple were announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021.

name: Winchester Virginia Temple
description: The Winchester Virginia Temple will be built on an 11.27-acre site at 200 Merrimans Lane, following its location announcement on October 30, 2023. Elder Robert M. Daines, Second Counselor in the North America Northeast Area Presidency, led the groundbreaking ceremony on August 9, 2025. This temple will be Virginia's second, after the Richmond Virginia Temple, and will feature a single-story design of approximately 30,000 square feet. Plans for additional temples in Roanoke and Norfolk have also been revealed. Winchester is located in far Northwest Virginia, about 75 miles west of Washington, D.C., and serves over 97,000 Latter-day Saints in the state.

name: Winnipeg Manitoba Temple
description: The Winnipeg Manitoba Temple is situated at the entrance of The Neighbourhoods of Bridgwater in the city's southwest. Its design is inspired by early Winnipeg churches, featuring a red brick façade, a slate roof, and a gold-colored spire. This temple is notable as the ninth in Canada and the first in Manitoba. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on December 3, 2016, and the temple was dedicated on October 31, 2021, after a public open house from October 9 to 23. The temple's architecture includes elements reminiscent of small English country churches and incorporates the Prairie Crocus, Manitoba's provincial flower, throughout its design.

name: Winter Quarters Nebraska Temple
description: The Winter Quarters Nebraska Temple is the first temple established in Nebraska. It shares a design with the Snowflake Arizona Temple and has a similar core plan to the Quetzaltenango Guatemala Temple, with some exterior changes. This temple is one of three built on historically significant sites for the early Church, alongside the Palmyra New York Temple and the Nauvoo Illinois Temple. The groundbreaking ceremony took place near a pioneer cemetery in Historic Winter Quarters, Omaha, presided over by Elder Hugh W. Pinnock. The temple's dedicatory services were broadcast across North America, marking a significant moment for the Church and its members.

name: Yigo Guam Temple
description: The Yigo Guam Temple features cream-colored walls and a prominent tower, situated at the intersection of Marine Corps Drive and Milalak Drive in Yigo, near Andersen Air Force Base. Behind the temple, a meetinghouse includes a distribution center and an arrival center for members. The temple, the first in Micronesia, was announced by President Russell M. Nelson on October 7, 2018, and dedicated by Elder David A. Bednar on May 22, 2022. Following Typhoon Mawar on May 24, 2023, the temple experienced flooding but sustained no structural damage, leading to a two-month closure for repairs. The design incorporates local cultural elements, with a simple yet elegant aesthetic, and the grounds are adorned with tropical landscaping.

name: Yorba Linda California Temple
description: The Yorba Linda California Temple is set to be built on a 5.4-acre site at the intersection of Bastanchury Road and Osmond Street, where a previous meetinghouse was recently demolished. Announced by President Russell M. Nelson during the 191st Annual General Conference on April 4, 2021, the temple will cover approximately 30,000 square feet and will be the second temple in Orange County, joining the Newport Beach California Temple. The groundbreaking ceremony took place on June 18, 2022, led by Elder Mark A. Bragg, who offered a dedicatory prayer for the site. This temple will be the ninth in California, complementing the existing temples in the state. Yorba Linda is located about 35 miles southeast of downtown Los Angeles and has a significant population of Church members.

name: Yuma Arizona Temple
description: The Yuma Arizona Temple is in the planning phase, with no groundbreaking date or official site location announced yet. President Russell M. Nelson revealed the intention to build the temple during the 194th Annual General Conference on April 7, 2024. This temple will be the seventh in Arizona, joining existing temples such as the Gilbert, Mesa, Phoenix, Snowflake, Gila Valley, and Tucson Arizona Temples. Arizona is home to over 440,000 Latter-day Saints organized into approximately 925 congregations. The Mesa Arizona Temple, dedicated in October 1927, was the first temple established in the state.
